When you change only notes or layout, Changes shows one row per folder: the folder’s name with Notes and layout (the repository’s name for the top level). Stage and commit it like a file. These rows can’t be opened or discarded yet. A Private folder’s notes are never committed. When you clone a repository made in FlowJoe, its notes, order, layout, tags, placeholders and links appear in the new node. Tags you already have keep your own colour. If FlowJoe can’t read those details (for example, they were saved by a newer FlowJoe), the files still arrive and a notice says what couldn’t be used; FlowJoe never overwrites details it can’t read. When a merge leaves conflicts, the Changes menu offers Mark All Resolved, which becomes available once you have resolved every conflict yourself; FlowJoe never picks a side for you.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: When you merge a branch, FlowJoe’s own files are merged as FlowJoe things, never as text: slot by slot and field by field, against the point where the two branches split. Notes on one slot and tags on another, or a teammate’s notes on a different slot, simply combine. Tags added on both sides are all kept. When both branches reordered a gallery and the moves fit together, both are kept. What both branches changed in different ways (the same slot’s notes, a folder’s status, two orders that contradict, a slot removed on one branch and edited on the other) becomes a question in the same window as above, with Yours, on main and From feature side by side and Finish Merge at the end. Closing the window leaves the merge waiting under Merge Changes, where the folder’s Notes and layout row opens the questions again. Plain files that Git can’t merge still open the file editor afterwards; if a choice there raises a new question (for example you keep deleted the only file of a folder whose notes you changed), FlowJoe asks it before the merge is committed. Before the merge commit is made, FlowJoe checks that the merged notes and layout read back correctly. A Private folder’s notes are never read or merged, and if the other branch renamed it, it stays where it is here instead of arriving a second time under the new name. If the other branch renamed or moved that folder, FlowJoe still recognises it when it keeps FlowJoe’s own id for it or still holds most of the same files; a folder that was renamed and also had most of its files changed can’t be recognised. Automations merged in stay switched off. An Edit guest merges these the same way, answering only questions about what they can see. Right-click a file, folder, or tab for actions that fit what you selected: Where Useful actions File Open, preview, compare, Timeline, rename, cut, copy, move, download, delete, and copy its name or relative path. Folder New File, New Folder, Quick Open, Find in Folder, rename, cut, copy, paste,

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: paste, move, delete, and copy its name or relative path. Tab Close this tab, other tabs, tabs to the right, saved tabs, or all tabs; reveal the file in Explorer, preview it, open Timeline, or rename a working file. To rename a file, folder, or working-file tab, double-click its name, press F2, or choose Rename…. Press Enter or leave the field to save; Escape cancels. Errors stay beside the name so you can correct them. Older revisions are read-only, and the repository root cannot be renamed, moved, or deleted through Explorer. Renaming a folder updates the paths of all files and subfolders inside it. Renaming or moving a working file keeps its open draft and undo history. Delete… on a folder confirms the folder and its contents; any affected unsaved files must be saved or discarded before deletion can finish. Canceling or a failed save keeps the folder. File deletion also checks for new edits when its turn arrives; the file cannot be edited while deletion is being saved. Cut followed by Paste moves a file or folder within the same repository. Copy followed by Paste creates independent items. Pasting a copy into its original folder chooses a free name such as README copy.md; an existing destination elsewhere is never overwritten. Move to Folder… offers a destination picker. A folder cannot be moved into itself or one of its descendants. If a copy includes drafts, choose Save and Copy, Copy Saved Contents, or Cancel; copying saved contents leaves the source drafts untouched. A folder’s Quick Open… lists only files inside that folder and its descendants. Find in Folder… searches readable text there, including unsaved open drafts; selecting a result opens the file at the matching line. Binary files are skipped. Large searches show a limit notice so you can narrow the query. Closing the search, switching repositories, or locking protected content clears the results. Choose a tab close action to close the selected file or group. If any affected file has unsaved edits,

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: edits, FlowJoe asks whether to save, discard, or cancel; a canceled close or failed save leaves the file open.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: A file’s Timeline follows its branch, including after a rename or move. Open an earlier version, compare it with today’s file, or choose Restore This Version… to bring its contents back into the working file. Restoring does not create a commit. A deleted folder is restored only when its original identity and current branch baseline can still be verified; a new folder with the same name does not take its place. If a restore’s save cannot be confirmed, the restored file and its bytes stay available for recovery; the operation does not claim that it was saved. Open Changes opens a separate comparison tab labeled with the file and revision. Older comparisons are read-only on both sides; your working tab and unsaved draft stay available. Reopening the same comparison selects its existing tab. Renaming the branch or changing its remote keeps both pinned sides available. In Changes, choose Review Changes with Joe… for the current edits. Timeline offers Review Change with Joe…, and the commit Graph offers Review Commit with Joe…. The Graph also lets you compare a commit with its parent, your current branch, or another selected commit; create a branch or tag at that point; open it on GitHub; or copy its commit message or identifier. Unavailable actions are dimmed.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: File Explorer exposes each file as a named keyboard action: Tab to it and press Enter or Space to open it. Accessibility tools can identify the current file; that mark follows editor-tab changes and clears when the last file closes. F2 starts the existing inline rename field, Enter submits it, and Escape cancels and returns to the file row. A refused rename keeps the field and its error available. The merge-conflict window keeps Tab and Shift+Tab within its controls. Escape closes it when the editor is not using Escape for its own command; closing leaves the merge waiting so you can return to it. The window returns focus to its opener, or to Source Control if that control is no longer available. When resolving a Stash conflict, Escape closes the conflict editor first and returns you to the restore window; a second Escape can cancel the restore. With focus in the workbench, Ctrl/Cmd+S saves and Ctrl/Cmd+F finds text in the file. Focus a file row, folder row, or working-file tab and press F2 to rename it inline; press Enter to accept or Escape to cancel. Shift+F10 (or the Context Menu key) opens the menu for a focused Explorer row, tab, or Timeline entry. Use the divider’s arrow keys to resize the Explorer; hold Shift to move it farther, and use Home or End to move to a limit. Quick Open… is available from the Explorer folder/background menu. With focus on an Explorer row, Ctrl/Cmd+X, Ctrl/Cmd+C, and Ctrl/Cmd+V cut, copy, and paste repository items. These shortcuts keep their normal text-editing behavior inside name and search fields.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: The branch pill opens the repository’s branch list. You can create a branch, rename or delete one, or merge it into another branch. Delete Branch asks you to confirm and warns you when the branch holds commits that exist only on this computer, when they are not on GitHub, or when FlowJoe could not check. A branch that a node is open on cannot be deleted until you close that node. Choose Open Branch as Node to put a branch in the Flow tree as its own node. Each open branch node shares the repository’s history. A folder that is Private in the repository opens locked in the branch node too, with the same password; removing the password from one copy doesn’t change the other. To work on another branch, select its node in the tree; Switch Branch opens that same branch picker. To remove a branch node from the tree without touching the branch, choose Close Branch Node… and confirm; the branch and its commits stay in the repository. You get 5 seconds to Undo, which brings the node back with its automations and keeps its media safe.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: Use Fetch to check the remote for new commits. The repository row and Graph toolbar also provide Pull, Push, and sync actions. The row’s counts show changes waiting to come in or go out. Link, change, or remove the remote from the repo node’s … menu under Remote.

title: Repo nodes and Git
header: Bring a teammate’s changes into your gallery
content: Pulling (or merging another branch) downloads the new commits, but your gallery is not changed on its own. A row appears under the repository saying who sent changes, for example 3 changes from Sam, with a Review button. Review opens a window that lists, in FlowJoe terms, what will change: Added: new slots and folders. Changed: pictures or files replaced, notes edited, slots moved on the canvas, a folder’s layout or order. Renamed: files and folders with a new name. Their notes, chats and Memories stay with them. If the repository includes history, a teammate’s new chats, transcripts and Memories come in at the same time (see History in the repository). Removed: slots and folders your teammate removed. Needs your choice: things you both changed in different ways, and files you have open in the editor with unsaved changes. Choose Update Gallery to bring everything in at once, or Cancel to leave the gallery as it is. If something needs your choice, FlowJoe then asks about it, one question at a time (see Answer FlowJoe’s questions); Finish Update applies the update with your answers. Your own changes that aren’t committed yet are kept. Before the update, FlowJoe saves a restore point in Version History named Before updating ”…” from Git, and Undo takes the whole update back in one step. Private and frozen folders are left exactly as they are, even if your teammate renamed or removed the folder they are in. The window only says how many of their changes were left out, without naming them. If you change the gallery while the update is downloading, FlowJoe stops and asks you to review again rather than overwrite your work. Once every question is answered, the row leaves and the gallery is up to date. If you cancel the questions, nothing changes and the row stays, so you can review again later.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: When you and someone else changed the same thing in different ways, FlowJoe asks in its own terms, never as text with conflict markers. Each question names the slot or folder (for example You and Sam both changed “brief.pdf”) and what changed (Slot notes, Name, Order of slots, Tags, a canvas place…), shows your version and theirs side by side, and offers: Keep Mine: your version stays. Keep Theirs (or Keep Sam’s when FlowJoe knows who sent it): their version replaces yours. Keep Both, for notes and other text: their text goes under yours, so you can edit them together. A slot one of you removed while the other changed it is kept until you answer: Keep Mine or Keep Theirs decides whether it stays. For a file you have open with unsaved typing, Keep Theirs puts their version in place (or removes the file, if they removed it), throws your unsaved typing away and closes its tab; your own notes and tags on that slot stay. Keep Mine keeps the typing. Previous and Next go back to a question you already answered, to change it. Where taking theirs isn’t possible (it would move a Private or frozen folder, or a name is already used here), only Keep Mine is offered. Cancel, the ✕ or Esc close the window without changing anything.

title: Repo nodes and Git
header: Sign in to GitHub over HTTPS
content: For private GitHub repositories over HTTPS, choose Sign in with GitHub in Source Control. FlowJoe opens Git Credential Manager’s sign-in flow. This signs in HTTPS GitHub access; SSH remotes use your SSH agent instead. Your GitHub account also lives in the Source Control … menu, which shows Signed in as … and offers Sign Out of GitHub. Cloning a private repository from the New Node window works the same way. If GitHub says the repository is private or can’t be found, the window says so and offers Sign in with GitHub right there; once you’re signed in, the clone runs again by itself. If you’re already signed in and that account has no access, the window names the account and offers Try Again (after the owner adds you as a collaborator) or Use a different GitHub account. FlowJoe never opens a sign-in by itself.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: Many repositories keep big pictures, videos and other media in Git LFS (Large File Storage): the repository itself holds only a small placeholder, and the real file lives on the hosting service. FlowJoe reads these by itself; you never install anything. When you clone, pull, or choose Update Gallery, each large file arrives as a slot that says Not downloaded yet, with the file’s name and its real size. FlowJoe never shows the placeholder’s text as the file. To get the file, open the slot (click it), choose its Download button, or open it from the Explorer. FlowJoe checks that what arrives is exactly the file the repository names before it keeps anything; if it isn’t, nothing is saved and FlowJoe says so. Offline, or if anything goes wrong, the slot stays Not downloaded yet with a plain message, and nothing is lost: try again later. While a file downloads, a small ✕ sits next to Downloading…. Choose it (or press Escape while it has focus) to stop the download: nothing is kept, and the slot goes straight back to Not downloaded yet. A downloaded large file never shows up in Changes: it’s the same file the repository already has. A file in a Private folder is saved as Private, like the rest of that folder, and a locked Private folder must be unlocked first. A repository you cloned before FlowJoe could read large files shows their placeholder text at first; the next time you open Changes, those slots become Not downloaded yet by themselves, and nothing shows up as changed. Sending large files. Any file of 50 MB or more goes through Git LFS, and so does any file at a path the repository’s .gitattributes already marks for Git LFS. FlowJoe keeps the file’s bytes in the repository’s own large-file storage on your computer and commits only the small placeholder, so someone who clones with plain Git and Git LFS gets the real file. The first time you commit such a file at a new path, FlowJoe also adds one line for it to the repository’s .gitattributes file, which appears in the

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: the gallery like any other file. In Changes, a large file shows like any other file with a small Large file note. A file you downloaded and haven’t changed stays exactly as it was: it is never committed or sent again. When you Push, FlowJoe first sends the large files the new commits carry, then the commits. If the large files can’t be sent (no connection, no access, or the server’s large-file storage is full), nothing is pushed, your work stays as it is on this computer, and FlowJoe says why in plain words. Files in a Private folder are never sent, and FlowJoe checks the Private rule before anything goes up. The first push. Before a repository’s first push, FlowJoe shows how much will go up: the total size, the number of files, and what goes through Git and what through Git LFS. Choose Push to send it, or Cancel to send nothing. On GitHub, large files count against your GitHub storage. Limits. Large files have no size limit in FlowJoe; the hosting service sets its own. Ordinary files, under 50 MB, stay in Git as they always have; FlowJoe still refuses a single ordinary Git file over 100 MB when you clone or import a repository that already holds one. Signing in. Large files on GitHub use the same GitHub sign-in as cloning a private repository (above). FlowJoe sends your sign-in only to the repository’s own host when it asks where the file is, never to the server the file then comes from. SSH links. A repository you cloned with an SSH link (git@github.com:…) downloads its large files from the same host over HTTPS. On GitHub that uses your GitHub sign-in: if you aren’t signed in, or your account can’t see the repository, FlowJoe asks you to sign in with GitHub. On another host with no HTTPS download for them, FlowJoe tells you that large files need an HTTPS link. A different large-file server. If a repository names its own large-file address (in a file called .lfsconfig), FlowJoe uses it only when it is on the repository’s own host; otherwise FlowJoe ignores it.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: it. Guests. Any guest can download a large file they can see, stop the download and start it again, just as you can; the download runs on your computer with your sign-in, and nothing in a folder hidden from the guest is ever downloaded for them. A guest’s push sends its large files the same way. Moving a large file. Moved into another repository, or duplicated, a large file stays a large file. One you haven’t downloaded keeps its Download button, which still works after the repository it came from is deleted (FlowJoe then fetches it from that repository’s online copy); Changes reminds you to download it first, and once it’s downloaded the new repository commits and sends it as a large file. Not yet: large files open from their slot, not as text in the editor, and Joe can’t edit them.

title: Repo nodes and Git
header: Use an SSH remote (macOS and Linux)
content: SSH remotes work on macOS and Linux. On Windows they are not supported yet; FlowJoe tells you so and asks you to use an https:// address. Before using SSH, add or unlock your key in the SSH agent available to FlowJoe. FlowJoe does not copy private keys into the Flow, repo history, or workspace. If the agent starts after FlowJoe, restart FlowJoe so it can see the agent connection. FlowJoe uses the system OpenSSH client from a fixed location, not your PATH: /usr/bin/ssh or /bin/ssh. On Linux, install an OpenSSH client if neither path exists. SSH hosts must already have a trusted key in your standard OpenSSH known_hosts file (~/.ssh/known_hosts). Verify the host key fingerprint against information from your Git host before adding it. FlowJoe checks the host key strictly and stops if the host is unknown or has changed; it does not ask to trust a new host inside the app. Unknown or changed host keys are rejected. FlowJoe never offers a prompt that trusts a new host automatically. The Graph section shows commit history, branch and tag labels, and commit details; when GitHub has commits your branch does not, they appear on a separate purple lane that curves back to your branch where the two meet. Use Show Git Output in the Graph options or repository menu to inspect recent Git activity.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: In the Explorer menu, Preview File displays the repository file itself. Preview Slot Item opens the corresponding gallery preview for that exact file item, including the selected child of a stack. The repository preview can show text and code, Markdown, HTML, images, audio and video, PDFs, extracted Office text, and ZIP file listings. Office previews show extracted content rather than a full-fidelity editable Office document; a ZIP preview lists its entries rather than opening them as a folder. HTML and Markdown previews show saved content without running scripts or contacting websites. Images and styles from the same repository can load within preview limits. A preview does not start your app or development server, and custom fonts may not appear.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: Stash puts your uncommitted work away and returns the gallery to the last commit, so you can switch tasks without committing half-finished work. Open the Stash menu in Source Control and choose Stash…. In the Stash Changes window you can add an optional message, see what will be stashed, and turn Include new files on or off (it is on by default). New files that sit inside a stack are left out and stay in the gallery. Files you had staged come back staged. Your stashes appear in a Stashes group in the panel. Stashes stay on this computer: they are never pushed, and Sync, Pull, Push, and Fetch ignore them. Pop brings a stash back and removes it from the list. Pop Latest Stash takes the newest one, or choose Pop Stash… to pick. Apply brings a stash back and keeps it in the list. View Stash… shows the files in a stash. Drop Stash… deletes one stash, and Drop All Stashes… deletes every stash in the repository. Both ask you to confirm first. If a file changed in the gallery since you stashed it, the Restore window asks which version to keep for each such file: Keep Mine or Keep Stashed, or Compare… to combine them by hand. Nothing changes until you confirm. If you kept your own version of a file, the stash stays in the list. After you stash or pop, a toast offers Undo for 5 seconds. You can also press Delete on a focused stash row to drop it.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: For another way to stay close to your project, the optional FlowJoe extension for VS Code puts the Flow in your editor’s sidebar. Edit names, slot and stack notes, Flow and node summaries, and node status while keeping your code editor open. If you have the FlowJoe source checkout: In your editor, run Extensions: Install from VSIX… and select the supplied integrations/vscode-flowjoe/vscode-flowjoe-0.0.4.vsix file. Open FlowJoe’s desktop app and enable Settings → Joe AI → Agent Bridge (MCP). Choose Connect to FlowJoe in the editor’s FlowJoe panel. If prompted, use the bridge token shown in FlowJoe. Use Refresh Flow to bring in changes made in FlowJoe. Use version 0.0.4 or later. Earlier installers do not include the connection protection added in this audit. The extension connects only to FlowJoe on your own computer and refuses redirects. Change its connection settings in your editor’s user or machine settings; a project’s workspace settings cannot override them. Edits wait for approval in FlowJoe unless you enable Apply changes without asking (Agent Bridge → Advanced). This extension edits Flow content; repository working-file editing happens in the FlowJoe workbench. It uses refresh rather than a continuous stream of updates. Browser guests use the shared repository workbench in their browser.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: With Joe’s Read access in the desktop app, using an OpenAI or Gemini API model or a tool-capable CLI brain, you can ask about saved repository changes and commit identities, or ask for a saved-versus-committed file comparison. Joe can distinguish staged and unstaged files when the current Changes list is available. A read does not open or refresh that list. If its state cannot be verified, Joe reports staging as unavailable. Ask explicitly for saved text, an open unsaved draft, or an already-open historical file. Joe labels the source and checks that the file and draft version have not changed while reading. If a draft is not open, Joe reports that it is unavailable. Private and Hidden-from-Joe contents remain excluded. Large results are read in bounded parts; unverified deleted paths and oversized files are unavailable. These reads do not edit, save, stage, commit or run commands. External agents connected through the Agent Bridge, including the FlowJoe CLI, can make the same reads with Read or Propose access. Guests can make these reads for files and repositories visible in their shared Flow when Joe is enabled. Scheduled tasks cannot. In your own OpenAI API chat, Joe can read two independent saved repository files together. For example, ask him to compare named files using their saved text. For longer lists, the next saved-file read can start as earlier results are collected, with at most two reads in progress. Requests for changes and other actions still follow their normal order and approvals. An open historical tab can be read only while the file is still present and readable in that repository. Deleting the current file or making it private revokes the old tab’s read access. FlowJoe checks again before each provider request, including after a wait for approval or a reference chapter; changed files or access cancel the response instead of sending stale text.

title: Repo nodes and Git
header: Ask Joe to change a file
content: You can ask Joe to make one exact text change to one existing file in a repository, for example “in src/main.js, change retries = 3 to retries = 5”. Joe can base the change on the saved file or on your open unsaved draft, and he says which. This works in the desktop app for your own chats, and for an Edit guest’s Joe: the change is saved on the owner’s computer, the same way as the guest’s own Save, and only for files the guest can see. An external agent with Propose access, including the FlowJoe CLI, can propose the same edit; it arrives on an Agent request card for you to review, unless that CLI command uses --autoapprove (see the CLI guide). It is not available to scheduled tasks, since no one reviews the change. Joe’s answer is a review card, not a change. The card names the file and branch, says what the change is based on, and states Apply saves this file and No commit or push is included. A read-only before-and-after comparison opens in the repository editor, labeled Saved file · before (or Your unsaved draft · before) and Joe’s proposed edit · after. Look at the exact lines, then choose Apply, Revise to ask Joe for something different, or Reject. Nothing is written until you apply. If you type in that file after the preview, Apply turns off and the card says The file changed after this preview. Ask Joe for a fresh proposal. The old text must also appear exactly once in the file; if it is missing or appears more than once, Joe is told and can propose again. A file edit comes on its own card, never mixed with other changes. Applying saves the file in FlowJoe, the same as pressing Save. It does not write to a folder on your computer and does not commit or push; use Source Control for that. If the save cannot be completed, the edit stays in memory with FlowJoe’s recovery copy and the open tab shows Joe’s text until storage is available again. Undo (the card’s undo or “undo your last change”) puts back the previous version and the text your editor showed before,

title: Repo nodes and Git
header: Ask Joe to change a file
content: before, unless you saved that file again or typed in its open tab since, in which case nothing is undone.

title: Repo nodes and Git
header: Ask Joe to work with repositories
content: You can ask Joe to create a repository, clone a link, list your GitHub repositories, or clone several into separate nodes. For example: “List my GitHub repositories and clone the ones I choose under Projects.” Your signed-in account can access private repositories as well as public ones; Joe never asks for or receives your token. Joe lists the repository name, whether it is private on GitHub, its default branch and its estimated size. Reading the list or repository status makes no change. Before downloading or changing anything, Joe shows an approval slot. Untick repositories you do not want; the count and size update. Nothing starts with none selected. Clones run one at a time. Each successful repository appears as its own node, with a link you can select. A failed clone names the repository and leaves the others free to continue. Stop ends the current download and the remaining work; completed repositories remain. A failed save is reported rather than presented as saved. You can also ask Joe to fetch, pull, sync, commit, push, create a branch, open a branch as another node, or merge branches. Joe can first prepare the current Changes list when needed; a commit proposal then shows its exact files and drafted message before you approve. Branches open as separate nodes so the current one is preserved. Merge questions use the same review windows as Source Control. An unfinished merge says Needs your choice; closing its question or conflict window does not commit it. Stop also prevents the next step of other Git actions while a confirmation or preparation is waiting; work already completed keeps its actual result. A push changes the remote repository and has no ordinary Flow undo.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: As the owner, you can list and clone every repository your signed-in GitHub account can access, including private ones. Guests can list your account’s public repositories and any repository already visible in their shared Flow, even if it is private on GitHub. Your other private GitHub repositories stay unavailable to them. A View guest can read the permitted list and status; an Edit guest can ask Joe to create and clone nodes within their shared area. Your computer checks the guest’s current access again before creating each node. Private Flow folders and folders hidden from that guest stay hidden.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: When importing a repository folder, FlowJoe reads working files through the folder it opened. Replacing a subfolder with a symbolic link cannot redirect those reads elsewhere. A symbolic-link file is saved as its link text rather than loading its target. Files that change while being read are skipped; ordinary hardlinked files remain supported. Portable .fj and .json exports let you choose Private nodes one by one (unlike repositories, which never include them): an included Private node stays encrypted inside the exported file and opens with its own password. Every Private node starts excluded; included nodes carry history under the export’s ordinary history choices. See Export & import.

title: Repo nodes and Git
content: If this computer cannot read saved undo steps or a history picture, FlowJoe keeps the repository’s committed copy. An unavailable picture does not become a broken image or a deletion when you commit other changes. If a history import or update cannot finish, FlowJoe remembers the unfinished work across restarts and retries it in order when you next open Changes. Deleting undo history clears its saved steps while keeping the current notes and title. Deleting a history entry yourself still removes it from the repository for everyone, unless a teammate has changed that same entry. The incoming changes summary counts all commits since the gallery’s last update, including changes by people whose commits are further back in the history. Private nodes are saved encrypted. Unlock to edit and save repository files; lock to make their content unavailable. Joe can prepare and review changes and use existing approvals for commits and branches. Hidden from Joe and Frozen still apply. Commit or Stash deliberately puts selected content into Git as readable files; Private folders inside a repository always stay out, and a repository that is itself Private commits its files readable too. When a picture, link or event file leaves a Private node (moved to another node or deleted), FlowJoe removes its readable copy from its own Git storage after the next save; for a delete, once its Undo is no longer available.

title: Gallery & Slot Anatomy
content: The media hemisphere — slots, cards, and interactive elements. The right hemisphere of FlowJoe is the Gallery. The gallery holds your visual and document references, arranged as independent blocks called slots.

title: Gallery & Slot Anatomy
content: A slot is an individual container in the selected node’s gallery. It wraps any file, URL, embed, or interactive workbench into a card layout that includes: ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ [Type Icon] Title / Filename │ ├────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ MEDIA PREVIEW │ │ (Image, PDF, Video Player, etc.) │ │ │ ├────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Slot Notes: "This is why this file is │ │ here..." │ ├────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ [Tags] [Previous/Next Stack] │ └────────────────────────────────────────┘ The title names the reference, the media shows it, and the notes explain why it matters. Metadata Header: Shows the file type icon, name, and size. Interactive Preview: A responsive rendering area (e.g. an audio player, a scrollable doc frame, or a web link preview). Click it to open the full-size Preview view. Slot Notes: An isolated annotation field, backed by the full rich-text editor — slash commands, emoji, markdown shortcuts, and a floating formatting menu with Joe’s AI actions. Tag Tray: Custom category tags. Context Controls: Options to replace, duplicate, move, or combine the slot. In the Move to Node picker, use Tab to reach a destination and Enter or Space to choose it; Tab stays inside the picker until you close it. If you opened the slot menu with the keyboard, Cancel or Escape returns to the source slot control without moving the slot. After a successful move, focus returns to the source node in the tree.

title: Gallery & Slot Anatomy
content: The gallery toolbar (and the canvas expand bar) includes a set of “Collapse all” toggles that act on every slot for the current node at once: Collapse all media, Collapse all tag bins, and Collapse all notes each fold that part of every slot card down to save space, and expand it back out on a second click. Each toggle’s state is per-node — collapsing notes on one node doesn’t affect any other node, and a node you haven’t touched always opens with everything expanded.

title: Gallery & Slot Anatomy
content: FlowJoe uses a stable, unique ID for every slot (entryId). Notes Conservation: Even if you change the media item inside a slot or drag it to another position, any attached notes remain intact. Undo History: Slot actions (like editing notes) have their own isolated history lanes. Undo-ing a note edit does not disrupt tree editing. Joe References: Joe uses stable IDs to target slot-level mutations (such as replacing an image placeholder with a generated graphic).

title: Gallery & Slot Anatomy
content: Slots are created automatically when you drag-and-drop files onto the gallery grid, paste clipboard content, or add web URLs. You can also click the Add Item button at the end of the gallery to create empty placeholders, calendars, spreadsheets, or rich documents.

title: Gallery & Slot Anatomy
content: Right-clicking any slot card triggers a context menu of advanced file operations: You can open the focused slot’s menu with Shift+F10 or the Context Menu key. Use Tab to reach its actions, Enter or Space to activate one, and Escape to close a menu layer and return to the slot when the menu still owns focus. Tag Copying & Pasting: Quickly copy all tags from one card and Paste or Merge them onto other cards to build tag assets rapidly. Asset Operations: Convert images or documents to PDF, crop images inline, or manage image stacking (Convert to Stack, Add to Stack, and Flatten Stack). Ask Joe: You can ask Joe to copy a slot, or one item out of a stack, and leave the original in place; to crop a picture in its slot; or to turn a picture or a note into a PDF placed beside the original. Download & Zip Exports: Pack all images/files in a stack into a single .zip file for download (Download Stack Media ZIP), export calendar workbenches as .ics files, or download raw original/derived files. Notes Assistant: Right-click the notes field to access: Dictate Notes (Microphone): Triggers voice dictation to speak annotations directly into the text field. Spelling & Grammar Check (Spell-check): Instructs Joe to audit notes spelling and rewrite it cleanly for your approval. A virtual slot keeps its own canvas position and collapsed state while showing the master’s content. Replacing the master’s picture keeps every virtual slot following it. For a stack, spelling checks respect whether you chose the slot’s notes or one item’s notes; accepting a correction changes only those notes.

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
content: Configure how you view your media and write slot annotations. FlowJoe’s gallery is a freeform board by default, with an immersive alternate view for presenting or reviewing. Switching layouts only changes how slots are arranged — your media, stacks, tags, and notes stay put.

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
content: Use the layout control in the top bar of the Gallery panel to switch modes. The public toggle is: Canvas ↔ Theatre Mode

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
content: Canvas lets the team place a level route, sprite study and playtest plan together without changing the tree. An infinite 2D board. Place slots freely, pan and zoom the surface, and draw relationship lines between slots. Positions and connections are kept when you leave the layout and return. A card deliberately placed at canvas coordinates (0, 0) stays there after reopening or sharing the Flow, including when a duplicate lands there. The gallery toolbar’s three collapse controls are named Collapse all media, Collapse all tag bins and Collapse all notes for assistive technology. Each name changes to Expand all when its content is collapsed and follows your selected language. Reach an available control with Tab and activate it with Enter. Best for: Mind maps, design boards, storyboards, and any arrangement that isn’t a single list or wall. Behavior: Scroll to pan, pinch or Ctrl/Cmd-scroll to zoom, drag empty space to pan, and drag a slot to move it. Plain drag pans the board, so lasso selection uses Shift/Cmd/Ctrl-drag — the two gestures never fight. Positions are stored with each slot, so leaving Canvas for Theatre Mode and coming back does not throw away your placement. View state travels with the flow: Pan/zoom, the grid arrangement, Fit, snap-to-grid, and the colour filter are saved per node and export/import along with the rest of the flow — reopening an exported flow puts Canvas back the way you left it. Insert button: The plus button on each canvas card has a minimum 24-pixel target. Its glyph and neighboring controls keep their existing scale. Narrow windows: If the canvas toolbar does not fit, scroll sideways over it with a trackpad or hold Shift while using the mouse wheel. Tab also brings each toolbar control into view. The board stays put while you scroll the toolbar. Connections: Drag the handle on a slot’s edge onto another slot to link them, or choose Connect to… from its free-form Canvas menu. Connections… lets you find and select an existing line

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
content: line without clicking it. Colour a slot to colour its outgoing lines. See Canvas Connections for the full picture. Coordinate readout: Move your mouse over the board (or drag a slot) and a small readout appears next to the zoom percentage in the top-right corner. It shows two different coordinates: V is the viewport position — where your mouse is on your screen, in plain pixels. C is the canvas position — where that same point sits in the board’s own space, independent of how far you’ve zoomed or panned. This is the position a slot’s placement is actually saved as, so it stays meaningful no matter your current zoom level. While you’re dragging a slot, the readout switches to showing the slot’s canvas position plus how far it has moved (Δ), and whether Snap to Grid is on. Dragging several slots at once shows the count instead, with a shared movement delta. This readout is a reference for anyone who wants precise placement or is describing a position to someone else — it’s not required for everyday use of the canvas.

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
header: Changing one card’s width without dragging
content: In free-form Canvas, open the card’s menu and choose Card width…. Enter a width from 160 to 1600 pixels, then choose Apply or press plain Enter. Reset to gallery size removes that card’s custom width; Cancel or Escape leaves it unchanged. Tab moves between the field and buttons. Only that card changes. Other cards keep their sizes, and the chosen width remains when you reopen the board. Width is a view adjustment and keeps its existing read-only restrictions; it does not change the card’s media or notes.

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
content: An immersive panoramic arrangement: slots sit around the camera on the inside of a sphere. Best for: Visual presentations, spatial mood boards, review pass in a different “room.” Behavior: Drag to look around with smooth easing. Tap a card to open the normal preview while Theatre Mode can remain active underneath. Built with CSS 3D transforms (not a heavy WebGL scene), so it stays light on startup. Treat it as a special view: leave Theatre Mode (for example with Esc or the layout control) to return to Canvas.

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
content: Earlier versions of FlowJoe also offered Horizontal (filmstrip row), Vertical Notes (media + notes columns), and Masonry (packed wall) layouts. These have been retired in favor of Canvas and are no longer reachable from the layout control. Any saved preference for one of these from before the change now opens in Canvas instead — nothing about your media, stacks, tags, or notes was affected by the switch.

title: Gallery Layouts & Slot Notes
content: Every slot can carry optional notes: Markdown-friendly writing for bullets, emphasis, and short research notes. Isolated undo/redo per notes field — Cmd/Ctrl+Z in a note undoes that note, not the whole tree or gallery. Write-back from Joe — Joe can drop analysis into a slot’s notes when you ask. Formatted display in Canvas: A note with formatting (bold, lists, links, etc.) shows that formatting on the card at rest in Canvas, instead of showing the raw markdown text. Links in a note at rest are clickable and open in the in-app browser. The full rich-text editor: Clicking into a note to edit it gives you the same editor as Node Summary and Preview — type / for a block menu, : for emoji, use markdown shortcuts as you type, and select text for a floating toolbar with bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/highlight, lists, links, inline code, and Joe’s AI actions. There’s no persistent toolbar on the card, just the floating one. Escape or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter finishes editing. Canvas and Theatre Mode keep notes on the slot data even when the view emphasizes placement or immersion — open a slot to read or write them.

title: Slot Preview
content: The full-size view you get when you click a slot, and its rich-text notes editor. Click a gallery slot to open its full-size preview. View the image, scroll a PDF, play audio or video, and write or format the slot’s notes with the same rich-text editor used by Node Summary and Flow Summary. Text/code editing depends on whether the slot is an ordinary gallery item or a repository-owned file; see the note below. For what each file type looks like in this view, see Supported Media & Slots. For an ordinary gallery text or code item, Edit opens the gallery code editor. For a repository-owned slot, Edit hands off to the repository workbench for that exact file or selected stack item. If the slot has unsaved notes, choose Save to keep them before switching, Discard to continue without them, or Cancel to stay in Preview. The selected stack item is the one opened in the repository workbench. In the repository workbench, Save updates the working file, while Commit is a separate Source Control action. To browse repository folders and history, open the repo node’s File Explorer.

title: Slot Preview
header: Read the source beside your notes
content: In the fictional Hartwell Legal case, open the inspection-record slot and choose Both to read the PDF beside its slot notes. The source stays on the left; the notes on the right explain what the case team wants to check against it. Text gives the notes more room, while Media focuses on the document. The inspection record and its notes in the real Slot Preview. Both keeps the source and the team's comments visible together.

title: Slot Preview
content: When a PDF contains extractable text, FlowJoe makes that text available to accessibility tools in the gallery preview, Slot Preview and the full-window document preview. The displayed pages stay the same. Reading follows the PDF’s source order, which may differ from the visual arrangement of columns or tables. Image-only scans need text recognition first; this preview does not perform OCR.

title: Slot Preview
header: Keyboard controls on audio and video cards
content: On a gallery audio or video card, press Tab to reach Play/Pause and use Enter or Space to start or pause playback. Keep pressing Tab to reach seek, volume and mute. The controls stay visible while you use them with the keyboard, even when playback is paused. Use the arrow keys on seek and volume; Home and End set volume to its minimum and maximum. Play/Pause also reports whether playback is active to accessibility tools.

title: Slot Preview
content: If a Pinterest board or profile preview cannot load, use View board on Pinterest or View profile on Pinterest to open the saved page.

title: Slot Preview
content: When FlowJoe needs a screenshot for a website link, its background preview has a ten-second limit covering page loading and capture. A page that stalls stops that attempt instead of keeping a hidden window open. FlowJoe can still use available metadata when an ordinary screenshot attempt fails.

title: Slot Preview
content: From the repository Explorer, Preview File shows the repository file in the workbench. Preview Slot Item opens the standard gallery preview for the exact corresponding gallery item, with its slot preview and notes. The two actions show the same file through different views. The repository preview supports text/code, Markdown, HTML, images, audio/video, PDFs, extracted Office text, and ZIP entry listings. Office previews are read-only extracted content; ZIP previews list entries rather than opening a navigable folder. Repository HTML and Markdown previews are static and sandboxed. They block scripts, app access, and network requests. Relative CSS and images may load from the same repository within preview limits. Previews do not run Node or start a development server. Custom fonts are not guaranteed to render under the app’s current content policy.

title: Slot Preview
content: The notes field inside Preview uses the same rich-text editor as the summary views: Rich Formatting & Dropdowns: Heading styles (H1–H3, paragraph), text alignments (Left, Center, Right, Justify), advanced marks (Underline, Highlight, Inline Code, Subscript, Superscript), task lists / checklists, tables, blockquotes, and dividers. Slash Commands & Bubble Menu: Type / to insert structural blocks quickly or select text to format on the fly with the floating formatting menu. Undo/Redo: Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z (and the toolbar’s Undo/Redo icons) walk the same persistent history as the rest of FlowJoe, so your edits are still there to step back through after a reload. Native Right-Click: Right-clicking in the editor opens your system’s standard menu (cut/copy/paste, spelling suggestions, etc.) — dictation and spell-check live on the toolbar here instead. AI actions: Select some text (or just place your cursor in a paragraph) and click ✨ — on the toolbar, or in the floating menu that appears when you select text. Pick Improve, Fix grammar, Simplify, Shorten, Expand, Change tone, Translate, Turn into bullets, Summarize, or Continue writing, or choose Ask Joe… to give any other instruction. The suggestion streams in below your text as Joe writes it, then shows the changes highlighted once it’s done — Stop cancels a request in progress. You can Replace it, Insert it below instead, copy it, tweak it in the box before accepting, or discard it, and Cmd+Z undoes an accepted change. Collapsible Sections & Block Actions: Wrap any selection into a collapsible section to tuck away detail, then un-collapse it later while keeping the content. Hover any block for quick duplicate, copy-to-clipboard, and delete actions — plus drag its handle to reorder blocks. Images: Drag an image file straight onto the editor (or paste one) to insert it where you dropped it, or type /upload for a drop box. Click an image to align it, float it so text wraps around it, add a caption or alt text, and drag its

title: Slot Preview
content: its corner to resize. Images are stored inside the note itself, so each file is limited to 4 MB — larger ones are skipped with a notice. Emoji Shortcodes: Type : followed by a name — :fire, :check, :rocket — and pick from the popup. Live Voice Dictation: Dictate hands-free using FlowJoe’s speech engine, including automatic spoken punctuation and line-break conversion. Spellcheck Review: Built-in review makes editing clean and fast. Gallery slot/stack notes on the card itself now use this same editor — same slash commands, emoji picker, markdown shortcuts, and floating bubble menu. The only difference is that the card-level note has no persistent toolbar (there’s no room on a card), so find-and-replace and the toolbar dropdowns are Preview/Summary-only, and the card note keeps its own right-click menu with Dictate Notes and Spelling & Grammar Check. Full details: Rich-Text Editor.

title: Slot Preview
content: When you enlarge the app or use a short window, Preview fits the available space so Save and Cancel stay in view. Long notes scroll inside the editor. While you use Preview, Tab and Shift+Tab stay within its window. Text-editor shortcuts, including list indentation, keep their usual meaning. Minimize lets you work elsewhere; restore the window from its pill to continue the same draft. Inside a Spreadsheet or Rich Document editor, F6 returns to Preview’s Close control. The editor keeps its own Tab and Escape behavior.

title: Canvas Connections
content: Draw relationship lines between slots on the Canvas layout. On the Canvas layout you can draw lines between slots to show how they relate — an idea feeding a task, a bug tied to a feature, a reference supporting a decision. The lines are part of your flow: they save automatically and travel with the flow when you export or share it. Connections are a Canvas feature — Theatre Mode is an immersive view rather than an arrangement, so there’s no equivalent there.

title: Canvas Connections
content: A first-playable board links the route, the visual mechanic and the question to test. Arrowheads show the direction of each relationship. Hover a slot and a small round handle appears on its right edge. Drag from that handle onto another slot and release. While you drag, a dashed line follows your cursor and the slot under the pointer is outlined, so you can see exactly where the connection will land. Release on empty canvas to cancel — nothing changes. If your device or browser interrupts the drag, the gesture is cancelled too: existing connections stay as they were. Each line carries an arrowhead at the target end. Connections have a direction: A points at B, which is not the same as B pointing at A.

title: Canvas Connections
content: In free-form Canvas, open a card’s menu and choose Connect to…. Type in Search cards, Tab to the target card, and press Enter or Space. Cards already connected from this card are marked Already connected and cannot be chosen again. Cancel or Escape leaves the board unchanged. Choose Connections… in a card’s menu to find a line going to or from that card. Search, Tab to the connection, and press Enter or Space to select it. The picker closes; press plain Delete or Backspace to remove the selected line, or Escape to clear the selection. The normal Undo banner can restore a removed line. These are ordinary menu and button actions, with no extra keyboard shortcut to remember. Typing in notes, tree controls and other open windows keeps its own keys. Existing read-only and locked-content restrictions still apply.

title: Canvas Connections
content: You can use Connections… as described above, or use these pointer routes: Click the line, then press Delete or Backspace. Hold Shift, Cmd, or Ctrl while clicking to select several lines and remove them together. Lasso them: drag a selection box (Shift/Cmd/Ctrl-drag on canvas) and it catches connections along with slots. Drag the same pair again: repeating the exact drag that made a connection removes it. Removing a connection is undoable. A banner appears for five seconds with an Undo button, and using it restores exactly the connections you removed — connections you made in the meantime are left alone. Press Escape to clear a selection without deleting anything.

title: Canvas Connections
content: Right-click a slot on the canvas and choose Slot Color to pick from six colours, or None to clear it. The colour tints the slot’s edge — not its whole surface, so your media stays readable — and every line leaving that slot takes the same colour. On a busy board this is what lets you follow one thread with your eye: colour the slot a group of connections starts from, and that whole branch becomes traceable. You can ask Joe to colour a slot red, green, blue, violet, pink, or cyan, or to clear that colour, and to draw or remove a line between two slots on the same board. Each change waits for your approval.

title: Canvas Connections
content: Right-click anywhere on the gallery background and toggle Show Connections. It sits with the other show/hide options (Tag Bin, Notes, and so on). Hiding removes the lines completely rather than fading them, so they cannot get in the way of clicking or dragging. Your connections are not deleted — toggle it back on and they return. The setting is remembered.

title: Canvas Connections
header: What happens when slots move between nodes
content: Connections join two slots inside the same node’s gallery. That means: Moving a slot to another node breaks its connections. FlowJoe tells you how many were removed, counting both the connections leaving that slot and any pointing at it from slots staying behind. The move is undoable, and undoing restores the connections too. Copying a slot to another node does not carry its connections. The copy is a new slot, so it starts unconnected. The original keeps everything. The same is true when you ask Joe to copy a slot onto another node. If a connection points at a slot that no longer exists — deleted, or moved away — the line simply isn’t drawn. Nothing breaks, and the rest of that slot’s connections are unaffected.

title: Canvas Connections
content: Connections are stored with each slot as part of your flow, alongside its canvas position. There is nothing to turn on and nothing to select: Exports include them automatically, in the same file as everything else. Imports restore them, including when an imported flow’s slot IDs would otherwise collide with slots you already have. Canvas positions and connections are kept even when you switch to Theatre Mode and back, so a look around never disturbs your board.

title: Adding Media & Local Files
content: Drag-and-drop, copy-paste, and referencing files on disk. Populating your gallery is designed to be frictionless. FlowJoe lets you ingest files from your local system, grab clips from your clipboard, or link directly to files on disk.

title: Adding Media & Local Files
content: You can drag multiple files directly from your system finder/explorer and drop them onto: The Gallery Gaps: Adds them as new slots at the end of the gallery. An Existing Slot: Adds the dropped item as a new layer in a Stack. A Tree Node: Adds them directly to that node’s gallery, even if the node is not currently selected. Supported Drops: Individual files, folders (imported recursively), zip archives, and .fj packages. When you choose several files, FlowJoe asks whether to keep Every File Separate or make One Stacked Slot. Use separate slots to compare related sources side by side; use a stack for material you want to keep together in one card. Importing three exhibits for a fictional civil case: keep the inspection record, condition sketch and repair estimate separate, or group them into one stack.

title: Adding Media & Local Files
content: Add Item button: Click the grid addition card to choose files manually. Clipboard Paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V): Press paste while the gallery has focus to insert images, text snippets, or file paths currently in your clipboard.

title: Adding Media & Local Files
content: When adding local files, FlowJoe offers two modes: Mode Storage Location Performance Portability Import Copy Stored inside IndexedDB High (copies cached locally) Portable (packages into .fj) Linked Local File Kept in origin folder on disk Dependent on disk paths High disk risk (broken paths on other machines) If a drop cannot add any items because a file fails to be read or stored, FlowJoe reports the import error. Your existing gallery stays intact; after resolving the problem, you can retry the drop.

title: Adding Media & Local Files
content: A Linked Local File reference points directly to an absolute path on your hard drive (e.g. /Users/name/Projects/report.pdf). No Duplication: FlowJoe doesn’t duplicate large video or audio files, saving disk space. Live Updates: Editing the file in external software reflects instantly in FlowJoe’s preview. Path Warnings: If you move the project to another computer, links will break unless the file exists at the exact same absolute path. When you join an owner’s shared Flow in a browser, you can view its shared linked media through the owner while sharing is available. Your browser receives the file bytes without the owner’s local path. Choosing or relinking files on the owner’s disk, opening them in a native app, and revealing them in Finder or Explorer require the owner’s computer. An Edit guest can copy a shared linked-file slot. The copy is another reference to the same file, with its own card, title and notes; it does not duplicate the file on disk. A View guest can read the shared file but cannot create the copy. [!WARNING] Frozen Node Restrictions: Drag-drops and file additions are disabled inside Frozen nodes and Virtual Galleries to protect structure and search results. An Edit guest can replace a linked card’s content without overwriting or deleting the original file on the owner’s disk. Replacing their own content follows the usual contribution rules; replacing someone else’s content requires the owner’s removal permission. Private content remains excluded. Ordinary gallery uploads do not require Joe or picture generation to be enabled.

title: Adding Media & Local Files
content: Edit guests can use shared linked files in new or replacement stacks, copy an individual shared stack item, merge cards, and extract items. These operations retain working references through the owner; they do not overwrite the original files on disk. Private items remain excluded, including when another item in the same stack is shared. Converting an existing card into a stack preserves who created its original content. Creating a copy creates new guest-owned content. Removing or replacing content follows the same ordinary Edit and elevated removal rules as the rest of the shared Flow.

title: Supported Media & Slots
content: An overview of supported file formats, previews, and URL cards. FlowJoe displays many media types in a full-size preview. Click a slot to open it; see Slot Preview for the view and its rich-text notes editor. Repository files have a separate Explorer and editor workbench; Edit depends on the item type.

title: Supported Media & Slots
content: Formats: JPG/JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, SVG, and TIFF. HEIC/HEIF photos are accepted and converted to JPEG when you import them, so they can be previewed in FlowJoe and in a guest’s browser. HEIC note: FlowJoe stores the converted JPEG rather than the original HEIC file. The conversion does not carry over embedded HEIC metadata. HEIC/HEIF sequence files import their first image only. AI generation: Directly generated graphics from Joe write back as native image slots.

title: Supported Media & Slots
content: Video Formats: MP4, WebM, OGG, and MOV. Audio Formats: MP3, WAV, M4A, FLAC. Global Player: Audio slots include album-art extraction. Playing audio loads it into a global header music player that continues playing even if you navigate to different tree nodes. Send to Global Player: Right-click an audio slot to play it in the global player (or add it to the queue) without dragging. Queues & Playlists: Drag audio slots together to create temporary playback queues, or save named playlists.

title: Supported Media & Slots
content: PDFs: Rendered using a scrollable inline PDF frame with text search. Ordinary gallery Markdown, text & code: Open the slot and choose Edit in its preview to open the gallery code editor (see below). For a repository-owned file, the repository Explorer opens the repository workbench; Edit on its gallery slot hands off to that workbench for the exact selected file. Office Previews: Read-only previews for DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, RTF, EPUB, and open formats (ODT, ODP, ODS) when they are not opened as interactive workbenches. Markdown document previews keep each source line on its own line, including saved transcripts and text saved from Joe. The same line breaks appear in repository Markdown previews and when converting Markdown to PDF. Previously saved files benefit when reopened if their source still contains the breaks. Note: Legacy .doc, .xls, and .ppt files extract text natively if LibreOffice is installed and configured in your settings. A fictional civil-case Flow mixes two PDF exhibits with an image-based condition sketch. The slot notes explain how each source relates to the case. The Evidence & exhibits node keeps the source documents together. Open a slot when you want to read it at a larger size and work on its notes; see Slot Preview.

title: Supported Media & Slots
content: For an ordinary gallery item—not a repository-owned file—open a Markdown, plain text, JSON, HTML, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, YAML, shell, log, or similar native text/code slot, then choose Edit in the preview. Editor: Full code editor with syntax highlighting for common languages (the same editor engine VS Code uses). Toolbar: Theme, word wrap, undo/redo, format, find, compare against your last saved version, and a more-tools menu (line numbers, minimap, show whitespace, font size, go to line, select all, copy all, download, Save to disk… on desktop, discard changes). Save / Preview / Save to disk: Save writes back to the gallery item inside FlowJoe. Save to disk… (under more tools) opens the system save dialog to export a copy; it does not re-link the gallery slot to that path. Preview returns to the readable view. This code editor is for ordinary gallery document and code items. It has no project tree, terminal, or external language-server service. Repository-owned files use the separate Repo nodes and Git workbench; word-processor, spreadsheet, or calendar editing uses the interactive workbenches.

title: Supported Media & Slots
content: Link Cards: Dropping a URL extracts page titles, descriptions, and thumbnails to render a preview card. Interactive Embeds: Inline rendering of YouTube, Vimeo, PDF URLs, or Spotify frames. In-App Browser: Click a URL slot to load the web page in a secure in-app window, allowing you to browse and extract content directly into your gallery.

title: Supported Media & Slots
header: Repository files use a separate editor
content: In a repo node, choose Switch to File Explorer and select a file to open it in the repository workbench. If you open a repo-backed slot from the gallery preview and choose Edit, FlowJoe takes you to the repository workbench for that exact stack item. If the slot has unsaved notes, choose Save, Discard, or Cancel before the handoff. Save there updates the repository working file; use Source Control → Changes to stage it and create a Git commit. A regular gallery item’s Edit stays in the gallery code editor above. The repository workbench can preview text/code, Markdown, HTML, images, audio/video, PDFs, extracted Office text, and ZIP listings. HTML and Markdown previews are sandboxed and static: no scripts, app access, network requests, Node, or project server. Relative CSS/images can load from the same repository within limits. Custom fonts may not render. See Repo nodes and Git for Explorer, tabs, Save versus Commit, Timeline, menus, and comparisons.

title: Supported Media & Slots
content: Calendars, spreadsheets, and rich documents can also run as editable islands directly within your gallery. See Spreadsheets and related pages for details.

title: Media Stacks
content: Combine multiple versions or reference takes into a single slot. When researching or iterating, creating separate slots for every file version can clutter your gallery. FlowJoe resolves this with Stacks—allowing you to bundle multiple assets into a single card.

title: Media Stacks
content: A Stack is a single gallery slot that contains multiple overlapping files. ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐ │ [Stack Icon] Draft Versions (1 of 3) │ ├───────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ ACTIVE ITEM PREVIEW │ │ (Latest Draft PNG) │ │ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Notes: "Comparing taking edits..." │ ├───────────────────────────────────────┤ │ [< Previous] [Next >] │ └───────────────────────────────────────┘ Paper Moon keeps three graphic-novel cover studies together. The active study changes while the comparative slot notes stay with the stack. Active Item: The top card of the stack is the active item. Its preview, title, and size dictate the slot display. Cycling: Click the Left/Right arrow indicators to cycle through items. Slot notes stability: The notes written on the slot card remain visible regardless of which stack item is active, keeping comparative analysis unified.

title: Media Stacks
content: Right-click a slot or select multiple slots to manage stacks: Create Stack: Drag a file directly on top of an existing slot, or select multiple slots, right-click, and select Merge into Stack. Extract Item: Right-click the active stack item and select Extract from Stack to split it out as an independent slot. Split into separate cards: Ask Joe to split every stack item into its own gallery card, keeping them all, then review his proposal. Flatten Stack: Keeps only the active item and removes the other items from the stack. Use this when you want to keep one version; check which item is active before confirming. Consolidate: Ask Joe to combine several slots into one stack, then review and approve his proposal. Copy one item: Joe can copy one item out of a stack into its own slot beside the stack, leaving that item in the stack.

title: Media Stacks
content: Hovering over a stack slot displays thumbnail previews of the layers. Change Order: Drag and drop thumbnails to reorder the stack hierarchy. Promote to Top: Click any thumbnail to promote that item to the active top slot. Individual Deletion: Click the delete icon on a thumbnail to remove it from the stack without deleting other elements.

title: Media Stacks
content: When a stack is the master of virtual slots, changing its top item changes it everywhere. If one of those places is frozen, FlowJoe asks before a manual change, including arrow buttons, keyboard navigation and the preview window. Cancel leaves the top item as it was. Playing an audio stack can still advance to its next track without asking each time. A spelling correction belongs to the exact slot or item notes you checked. Switching the top item while the correction waits does not redirect it or replace the slot’s hidden notes.

title: Image Editor
content: Edit a picture in a full editor and save the result as a new version of its slot. Edit Image opens a picture from a slot in a full image editor right inside the gallery. Whatever you save is added as a new version on top of the slot: the original stays underneath in the slot’s stack, and Undo puts it back. The editor comes with FlowJoe: there is nothing to download or set up, and it works offline. Crop Image in the same menu stays the quickest way to just trim a picture.

title: Image Editor
content: Right-click a picture slot. Choose Edit Image › Open Editor… (just under Crop Image). Edit Image is greyed out for things it can’t edit, the same ones Crop Image can’t: a missing or placeholder picture, a video or a document, or a slot you can’t change. The editor opens PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC and SVG pictures (an SVG drawing is saved back as a PNG). For other kinds (an AVIF photo, for example) FlowJoe says so instead of opening it; Crop Image still works on them. An unlocked Private picture uses the same editor and quick fixes, and stays encrypted when saved; Save as New Version keeps its new version encrypted. Locking closes the editor and discards unsaved edits. The existing Compress action also keeps its replacement encrypted, and picture imports follow your existing compression choice. Deliberate exports and downloads produce the readable files you chose to save. The editor opens straight away on the picture you picked. While it is open, Tab skips the gallery controls covered by the editor; the visible tree and header stay usable. Closing the editor makes the gallery controls available again.

title: Image Editor
content: Below Open Editor… the Edit Image menu has one-click fixes that work without opening the editor: Quick fix What it does Auto-tone Balances the picture’s light and contrast automatically. Rotate Left / Rotate Right Turns the picture a quarter turn. Flip Horizontal Mirrors the picture left to right. Sharpen Sharpens the details. Resize… Asks for a new size first (see below). Each one is saved like Save as New Version: the result goes on top of the slot, the original stays underneath in the stack, and Undo in the message that appears (for example Sharpened. Saved as a new version in slot 1) puts the slot back as it was. A JPEG picture stays a JPEG; everything else is saved as a PNG. A quick fix takes a few seconds (the editor starts in the background first; large photos take longer). A small message at the edge of the window shows it’s working, for example Sharpening aster-bay-first-light.png…, and goes away when it’s done. You can keep using FlowJoe meanwhile, or switch to another app: the quick fix carries on while FlowJoe’s window is in the background. One quick fix runs at a time. Asking for another while one is running tells you to try again when it’s done. While the editor screen is open, quick fixes wait: close the editor first. Open Editor… also waits while a quick fix is still running. If a quick fix can’t be done, FlowJoe says so and the picture isn’t changed.

title: Image Editor
content: Resize… opens a small window with Width and Height in pixels and the picture’s current size below them. The link button between the fields keeps the proportions: change one side and the other follows. Click it to change the sides separately. Enter or Resize applies the size; Cancel or Esc closes the window without changing anything. Sizes are whole pixels. Resize stays off while the size is the picture’s current size, and the window says why when a size can’t be used (for example 0, or far too large for the editor).

title: Image Editor
content: The editor takes the place of the gallery, like Version History does. The title row shows Edit Image, the picture’s name, its slot and node, then Advanced, Export Image…, Save as New Version and ✕. Aster Bay, a fictional setting in Mosslight Atlas, shown in the real Image Editor. Below it: Tools down the left: Move, Crop, Select, Brush, Remove spots, Text, Shapes, then Pick color, Zoom and Pan. Hover a tool to see its name and shortcut key; with the screen’s buttons in focus, pressing that key picks the tool (it never triggers the tree’s own one-letter shortcuts). The editor starts on Move. A toolbar row across the top: Undo and Redo, then the options of the tool you picked (or a one-line hint about what it does), and Compare on the right. A status row under the picture: its size, color space (sRGB), zoom, − / + and Fit. The panel on the right, with three tabs: Adjust, Filters and Layers. Undo and Redo also bring the sliders back to match the picture, including an undo you type inside the picture (Cmd/Ctrl+Z).

title: Image Editor
content: Crop shows a frame on the picture with a rule-of-thirds grid, like Crop Image. Ratio (Original, Free, 1:1 Square, 4:5 Portrait, 9:16 Story) reshapes the frame, Straighten turns it (up to 45° either way), and W / H show the frame’s size. The other options rotate and flip the whole picture. Text: set the font, weight, size, color and alignment, then click the picture to type: the text starts in that style. Pick a text layer to change its style afterwards; Shadow needs a text layer picked. A crop frame or text you’re still typing is finished automatically when you save or compare, so what you see is what gets saved. In the rare case the editor doesn’t finish it in time, nothing is saved and FlowJoe tells you; choose Save as New Version again. Choose 1:1 Square to frame a square study before saving.

title: Image Editor
content: The panel on the right holds the everyday adjustments: Group Sliders Light Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows Color Warmth, Tint, Vibrance, Saturation Detail Sharpen, Clarity, Noise While you drag a slider you see a quick preview; when you let go, the editor works the change into the picture itself. On a large photo that can take a moment. Sliders stay changeable until you save. Reset puts all of them back to zero. Auto-tone balances the picture’s light and contrast automatically. It works on the untouched picture, so use it before moving the sliders.

title: Image Editor
content: Ready-made looks: Original, Warm morning, Soft film, Crisp, Black & white and Faded. Click one to apply it, and use Amount to make it stronger or softer. Original removes the look. A look works alongside your Adjust sliders; it doesn’t change them.

title: Image Editor
content: The picture’s layers, top to bottom. Click a layer to pick it, use the eye to hide or show it, and set its Opacity and Blend underneath. Drag a layer up or down to reorder it; a line shows where it will land. The buttons add a new layer, duplicate the picked one or delete it (FlowJoe asks first; Undo in the editor brings it back). The picture itself is the bottom layer and is locked (it shows a lock): it can’t be moved, duplicated or deleted, because it is what Save as New Version saves. Your look and your Adjust sliders show just above it as Look and Adjustments; their eyes hide or show them.

title: Image Editor
content: Compare shows the original and your edit side by side, split by a line you can drag. Press it again, pick a tool or switch tabs to go back to editing. Drag the dividing line to compare the original light with the brighter edit.

title: Image Editor
content: Turn on Advanced to use the editor’s additional tools and panels (Curves, Levels, brushes, layer styles and more), in the editor’s own layout; FlowJoe’s tools, toolbar row, status row and panel step aside. Save as New Version, Advanced and ✕ stay where they are. Turn it off to go back, with the tool you had picked. With the picture focused in Advanced, press Cmd+F on Mac or Ctrl+F on Windows/Linux to search the editor’s commands. For example, search for Gaussian Blur, Canvas Size or Liquify. Some commands need a selection or a suitable layer first.

title: Image Editor
content: Save as New Version applies your edits to the picture at full size. Large photos can take several seconds; FlowJoe shows that it’s working and you can keep using the rest of FlowJoe. When it’s done the editor closes and the slot shows the edited picture on top, with the original underneath. Undo in the message that appears puts the slot back as it was. A JPEG picture is saved as a JPEG; everything else is saved as a PNG. The saved version is one finished picture: reopening it does not restore the editor’s separate text, adjustment or other layers. The saved square study is on top. The 2 badge shows that the original remains in the stack.

title: Image Editor
content: Choose Export Image… to save a finished picture to your device while keeping the editor open. Pick PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF or TGA. For JPEG or lossy WebP, set Quality from 1 to 100. Lower quality usually makes a smaller file; higher quality keeps more detail. For WebP, turn on Lossless to keep every detail without a quality setting. Choose Export. In the desktop app, choose the file’s name and location; in a browser, the download follows your browser’s settings. PNG, TIFF and TGA keep all detail without a quality slider. JPEG has no transparency: transparent areas become white. Export makes one finished, flattened picture. It includes a pending crop or text edit, just as saving does. Your editor stays open with its edits. Export does not add a version to the slot or replace Save as New Version. If you close afterwards with unsaved edits, FlowJoe still asks whether to keep them in your Flow. Choose JPEG and adjust quality before exporting the fictional Aster Bay picture. WebP Lossless keeps every detail, so no quality slider is needed. An invited guest needs Edit access and the owner’s permission to export. Without it, Export Image… is hidden; editing and saving into the shared Flow follow their existing permissions.

title: Image Editor
content: ✕ or Esc closes the editor. A crop frame you have drawn, resized, moved or turned counts as an unsaved edit too. If you have unsaved edits, FlowJoe asks first: Save as New Version, Discard, or Cancel (which keeps you in the editor). Clicking another node in the tree (also with Shift or Cmd/Ctrl), opening History, deleting the node, importing or switching the Flow, restoring a version, and quitting or reloading FlowJoe ask too. A leave you ask for while a save is running waits for the save and then goes ahead. With Advanced on, or with Crop or Text picked, Esc inside the picture belongs to the tool (it cancels the crop frame or ends the typing); use ✕ to close.

title: Image Editor
content: The editor runs separately from the rest of FlowJoe. If it stops (it can run out of memory on a very large photo), only the editor is affected: FlowJoe shows The editor stopped. Your picture wasn’t changed. Your unsaved edits in the editor are lost. Choose Reopen Editor to start again on the same picture, or Close.

title: Image Editor
content: People you’ve invited to a shared Flow in their browser use your copy of the editor: they never install anything themselves. A guest who can crop a picture gets Edit Image › with Open Editor… and every quick fix, exactly as you do. The editor comes from your computer the first time they open it in their visit (about 12 MB) and then starts from what their browser already has. If you’re on an older version of FlowJoe that didn’t include the editor yet, they see Edit Image greyed out, without its arrow, with the line The owner hasn’t added the image editor yet. under it.
