A guest who can only view the Flow can’t crop, so they can’t edit pictures either. What a guest saves goes into your Flow the same way as their Crop Image does: a new version on top of the slot, the original underneath. Changing a picture someone else added follows the invitation’s removal permission, as Crop does: without it, FlowJoe keeps the picture as it is and tells the guest Unable to remove item, with Ask (your name) to remove it or grant removal permission. If someone replaces or removes the picture while it’s open in the editor, a quick fix or Crop Image, FlowJoe doesn’t save and says The edit wasn’t saved: the picture changed while the edit was open. In the editor your edits stay on screen. The editor works in current Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox. A browser that can’t draw it (it needs WebGL 2) shows This browser can’t run the image editor instead; the picture isn’t changed and Crop Image still works. In the browser, a quick fix keeps running only while the guest’s tab is open in front: browsers slow down tabs that aren’t being looked at, so a quick fix started just before switching tabs may take longer or not finish. The picture is never changed unless the fix finishes.

title: Image Editor
content: Settings › Gallery › Image Editor says the editor is built in and shows its version (for example Built in · version 0.15.1). There is nothing to download or remove. The card appears in the desktop app for the Flow’s owner; guests and the browser version don’t see it. The editor is based on PhotoCraft by the ArtCraft team (MIT licence). Its licence notices are in Settings › Data › Open-source licenses.

title: Virtual Slots
content: Show the same slot in more than one node without copying it. A Virtual Slot shows a slot that lives somewhere else in the same Flow. There is one real slot, the master, and any number of virtual slots that point to it. They all show the same picture or file, title, notes and tags. This is useful whenever the same thing belongs in several places. In a family tree, a wedding portrait can sit with both people in it. In a project, the same logo or reference board can sit in every branch that uses it.

title: Virtual Slots
content: The V marker and dashed border identify a virtual slot. This invitation is original fictional sample artwork. A virtual slot has a dashed outline and a small dashed V in its top-left corner, just right of the + button (on a stack, right of the item count). A master that is shown elsewhere has a small dashed M in the same place. Hover over the V or M, or click it, to see where the slot lives: On a V: the master’s node and slot number, plus any other places it is shown. On an M: every place it is shown. Every place in the card is a link. Click one to go to that node and slot. Press Esc to close the card. If a virtual slot’s master is no longer in the Flow, the card says so. You can remove the virtual slot, or keep it until the master comes back. A virtual slot can show a Private master to you only when both are in the same unlocked Private area. Guests and Joe never see Private masters.

title: Virtual Slots
content: Pick the original invitation once, then show it with both people instead of maintaining separate copies. Click + on a slot (or the + in the canvas toolbar) to open Add Slot, and choose Virtual Slot. Pick a node on the left. Its slots appear on the right. Pick the slot you want to show here, and choose Add Virtual Slot. The slot you picked becomes the master. If you pick a slot that is itself a virtual slot, the new one points at its master. You can pick a slot from the node you’re adding to. Private nodes are listed but can’t be opened, and a Private node doesn’t offer the Virtual Slot card. A virtual slot can’t be moved or copied into a Private node either, and a master whose virtual slots live in other nodes can’t be moved into one: FlowJoe tells you why and leaves everything where it was.

title: Virtual Slots
header: What you can do with a virtual slot today
content: Move it within its node, resize it on the canvas, and connect it to other slots. Where it sits belongs to that node. Remove it from its node with the trash button or Remove from This Node…. The master and any other virtual slots are not touched. Go to Master (right-click the slot) opens the master’s node and slot. Make Real Slot (right-click the slot) turns it into its own real slot: a copy of the master as it is now, with its own copy of the picture or file. After that it no longer changes with the master. Undo turns it back into a virtual slot. If a file can’t be copied, nothing changes and FlowJoe tells you, so the copy never shares the master’s file. A file that was already missing is skipped. Copy it (for example with the copy button on the next slot): the copy is another virtual slot of the same master. Right-clicking a virtual slot shows the usual slot menu with Go to Master and Make Real Slot on top. Tags, Crop and Replace change its master. A few actions are greyed out for now: building or changing a stack (Convert to Stack, adding, removing or reordering its items), renaming the file, converting to PDF, inserting clipboard media and the wireframe tool. Right-click a master to see every place it is shown. Each one is a link. A virtual slot can’t go into a stack, and other slots can’t be merged into it. Stack everything leaves virtual slots out and keeps them as they are.

title: Virtual Slots
content: The content follows the master until you deliberately make an independent real slot. Changing a virtual slot changes its master, and with it every other place the master is shown. You can edit a virtual slot’s title, notes and tags, turn Hide from Joe on or off, replace or crop its picture, compress it, and step through a stack to choose which item is on top, right where it is. Clicking its picture opens the master’s preview window, where you can edit it too. Which item is on top of a stack belongs to the master, so changing it at a virtual slot changes it everywhere the master is shown. Undo works wherever you are: an edit made at a virtual slot can be undone there, or from the master. Pressing Cmd+Z inside the master’s notes also undoes notes you typed at one of its virtual slots, because they’re the same notes. If the master is in a frozen node, its virtual slots can’t be changed either: they say so when you hover over the V. To change it, unfreeze the master’s node. If one of the master’s virtual slots sits in a frozen node, FlowJoe asks before you change the master: Change Master Slot? names the frozen node, because the change will show there too. Clicking into the title or notes and back out never asks. It asks when you leave the title or notes after actually changing them (or before a tag change); until you answer, nothing is changed anywhere. Choose Save Change to keep your change or Cancel to put the master’s text back as it was. Once you’ve said yes, it doesn’t ask again for that slot while you stay on the same node. A virtual slot that sits in a frozen node can’t be changed there, just like everything else in that node. Clicking its picture shows where its master is. Tagging a whole node from the node menu tags the master of each virtual slot in it too, wherever that master lives, the same as tagging the virtual slot itself. A virtual slot whose master can’t be changed (frozen, missing or inaccessible) is skipped. A retained pair in the same unlocked

title: Virtual Slots
content: unlocked Private area can be tagged by you. If any of those masters also shows in a frozen node, FlowJoe asks once before tagging, and Cancel tags nothing. Undo puts every slot’s tags back, masters included.

title: Virtual Slots
content: Searching by tag or text lists every place a slot appears: the master and each of its virtual slots, each in its own node. Virtual slots match on their master’s tags, title and notes. Tag filters work the same way: a virtual slot counts as carrying its master’s tags.

title: Virtual Slots
content: Removing a virtual slot (Remove from This Node) takes away only that virtual slot. Its master and every other place it is shown stay as they are. Removing a master that still has virtual slots elsewhere asks what should happen to them, before anything is removed. This happens whether you remove the slot itself, a selection, every slot in a node, or a whole node. Each master gets its own row with two choices: Make a new master: one of its virtual slots (you pick which; the first is chosen for you) becomes a real slot with the master’s picture, title, notes and tags, and the other virtual slots now show that one. Nothing is lost. Remove all its virtual slots: they go along with the master. A virtual slot inside a Private node is never offered as the new master; if it’s the only place left, the row removes it. If one of those virtual slots sits in a locked Private node, FlowJoe names the node and asks you to unlock it first, before anything is removed. If one of those virtual slots sits in a frozen node, the row says so, and confirming changes that node too. Cancel removes nothing. Undo brings back the master and every virtual slot as they were. A master that has virtual slots can’t be merged into a stack, because its virtual slots would lose it.

title: Virtual Slots
content: When you share a node with a guest, its virtual slots show their master’s picture, title, notes and tags, just as they do for you. If the guest can also see the node the master is in, the hover card looks exactly like yours, with working links. If the master’s node isn’t shared with them (including a part of the Flow you left out of their share), they still see the content, but the hover card says they don’t have access to the node the master is on. It never shows that node’s name or where it sits in your Flow, and it lists only the places the guest can see. A master in a Private node, or a hidden master slot, is never shown to them. A guest can change what a virtual slot shows only when they can edit the node its master is in. They can still use Make Real Slot to get their own copy in the node they’re working in, with its own copy of the picture or file, and change that copy as they like — unless the master is in a Private node or hidden. If a file can’t be copied on your computer, nothing changes and their change is refused. They can still move it, reorder it, connect it or remove it in the node they’re working in. A guest can remove a master slot too, with the same choice you get (make one of its virtual slots the new master, or remove them all), as long as every virtual slot of it is in a part of the Flow they can see and change. If any sits outside what you shared with them, or in a frozen node, only you can remove it, and FlowJoe tells them so. When a guest edits a master that has a virtual slot in a frozen node outside their share, they get the frozen-node warning without that node’s name.

title: Virtual Slots
header: Exporting a node with virtual slots
content: When you export a node on its own (or use Copy Node JSON), a virtual slot whose master lives elsewhere in your Flow brings that master’s picture, title, notes and tags along with it, so the export never points at something that isn’t there. A master that is hidden, or sits in a hidden or Private node, is never included in the export; that virtual slot travels as a bare pointer.

title: Virtual Slots
content: A virtual slot can’t point across the edge of a Private area. Moving nodes or slots across that edge is refused when it would separate a master from its virtual slots; moving the complete group together out of Private is allowed. A refused move leaves the whole selection where it was. Saving search results as a new node also respects this boundary. So when you make a node Private and some of its slots are shown in other nodes, FlowJoe asks first, before the password step: A master shown in other nodes: make one of those virtual slots the new master (it gets its own copy), or turn them all into real slots. Either way, the Private node keeps its own copy. A virtual slot that is itself in a Private node can’t become the new master. A virtual slot whose master is outside: it becomes a real slot, a copy of its master. When you make several branches Private at once, each branch gets its own Private area. Virtual slots between those branches become real copies too. Making their common parent Private keeps the slots together in one area; a node that already has its own password keeps its separate area. Every copy gets its own copy of the picture or file, so nothing is shared between the Private node and the rest of your Flow. The one exception is a rich document’s embedded pictures: they stay shared with the master, the same as when you make a real copy. Cancel changes nothing, and undoing Make Private puts the slots back as they were. If nothing crosses the edge, Make Private keeps those internal virtual slots, and you can use them after unlocking that Private area. If a picture or file cannot be copied, the whole step stops, nothing becomes Private, and the copies already staged for the step are cleaned up. If a slot to be changed or a master to be copied is in a locked Private node, FlowJoe asks you to unlock that node first.

title: Virtual Slots
header: Importing a node with virtual slots
content: When you import that file again — with File › Import (adding it to your Flow or replacing it), Import Node(s), or by dropping the .fj file on the tree — FlowJoe decides for each virtual slot in it: Its master is in the file too: it stays a virtual slot of that master. Its master is still in this Flow and hasn’t changed: it quietly reattaches to it as a virtual slot again. Its master is still in this Flow but has changed since you exported: the Imported Virtual Slots window lists each one, with a small picture of the master, where the master is (“Master in Rose Hartley · Slot 1”) and what changed (for example “notes changed” or “picture replaced”). For each one choose: Stay virtual (the default): shows the master as it is now, and follows it from here on. Own slot: keeps the version you exported as a separate real slot. Set all switches every row at once. Import N Slots goes ahead; Cancel stops the whole import and nothing is added. Its master isn’t in this Flow (another Flow, or the master was deleted), or it’s now in a Private node, or the slot lands in a Private node: it comes in as its own real slot, with the picture, title, notes and tags it had when you exported. If the master’s node was hidden from Joe, the new slot’s notes are hidden from Joe too. If the file has no pictures packed in it and the picture isn’t on this computer either, that slot comes in as a virtual slot with its master missing instead, so the import still goes ahead. Importing a virtual slot into a Private node makes it its own real slot even when its master came in the same file. This import rule differs from Make Private, which can retain an existing pair within one Private area. Several virtual slots of the same missing master stay together: the first becomes the real slot and the others show it. A virtual slot whose master was Private when you exported carried nothing, so it comes in as a virtual slot with its master missing.

title: Virtual Slots
content: Joe works with virtual slots the same way on every AI model you pick. Joe reads a virtual slot as a pointer. He knows which slot it shows and where that master lives, and he reads the master’s picture, title and notes once, at the master, rather than once for every place it appears. Hidden notes stay out of spell-check too. Correcting an item’s visible notes changes only those notes, even if you switch the stack’s top item or view another node before accepting. The slot’s own hidden notes stay untouched. A master Joe can’t see stays hidden. If the master sits in a node you’ve hidden from Joe (or a Private node), Joe only knows the slot is a “virtual slot of a slot hidden from Joe”. He sees nothing about it, can’t read it, and can’t add another virtual slot of it. A guest’s Joe sees what the guest sees, and never anything hidden from Joe. In a shared Flow, the guest’s Joe reads a virtual slot’s master whenever the guest can see it, including a master outside what you shared that the guest is shown, but never one in a node you’ve hidden from Joe; it never learns where an outside master lives. It can copy such a virtual slot and use Make Real Slot on it, just as the guest can, except when its master is hidden from Joe. Ask Joe to show a slot in another node (“put the wedding portrait in Walter too”) and he proposes a new virtual slot of it. Asking him to copy a virtual slot makes another virtual slot of the same master. He can also propose Make Real Slot when you want one place to stop changing with the master. Changes go to the master. When Joe changes what a virtual slot shows (its title, notes, tags or picture), he changes the master, so every place it is shown changes. If the master is also shown in a frozen node, the proposal card says so, and choosing Apply is your go-ahead. Joe’s button on a virtual slot opens Joe on its master. Pictures Joe makes, text you send into the slot, and dictation corrections all land on the master. If the master is shown in a frozen

title: Virtual Slots
content: frozen node, FlowJoe asks first, just as it does when you edit the master yourself. If the virtual slot can’t change its master, or the master is Private, Joe isn’t opened on it. Removing a master is your choice. Joe can propose removing a master slot that has virtual slots, but he never decides what happens to them. The proposal card says you’ll choose, and when you choose Apply, FlowJoe shows the same Remove Master Slot window you get yourself: make one of its virtual slots the new master, or remove them all. Cancel leaves everything as it was. Joe can’t remove such a master when one of its virtual slots is in a node hidden from him or in a frozen node, and a scheduled task never removes one on its own. A guest’s Joe works the same way for the guest: the guest makes the choice in the same window, and a master that is also shown somewhere the guest can’t change gets the same “only the owner can remove it” message the guest sees when removing it themselves. The FlowJoe command line and outside assistants connected over the Agent Bridge get the same actions and the same rules. Removing a master is held until you choose in the app when you approve it. A command-line session you started with --autoapprove applies the choice it sent (make a new master, or remove them all) without asking. What you hide from Joe stays hidden from every Joe, including a guest’s Joe and scheduled tasks. This keeps your guest’s own view and actions available: a guest can still use Make Real Slot and remove a master when their normal edit and removal rights allow it. Joe keeps the node’s name and place, but receives none of its hidden content.

title: Tags & Virtual Galleries
content: Flow-wide tags and dynamic cross-cutting search results. FlowJoe uses Tags and Virtual Galleries to provide dynamic, cross-cutting discovery views across your entire project hierarchy. Urban Canopy uses tags for topic and review state; one reference can have both.

title: Tags & Virtual Galleries
content: Manage your tag vocabulary in the Flow-level registry: Registry Location: Stored at the root of the Flow file. Customization: Add, rename, recolor (assign category colors), merge, or delete tags. Usage Counts: The registry displays how many slots are tagged with each label.

title: Tags & Virtual Galleries
content: Tag Editor: Click the tag badge on any gallery slot to open the tag picker. Assigning and reusing tags: Use the Tag Manager to assign tags. The slot menu also lets you copy tags and paste or merge them onto other cards. Accessible control names: The Tag Bin’s Manage control includes its visible wording in its spoken name, including after a language change. Stack Tagging: Stacks can be tagged as a single unit, or individual items within a stack can hold separate tags.

title: Tags & Virtual Galleries
content: One review queue spans two branches. The origin badges show where each reference actually lives. A Virtual Gallery is a dynamically generated gallery view. Use Query by tags (Q) to choose tags, or open gallery search and turn on All nodes to gather matching references into one view. In gallery search, Include tags, Include file names, and Include document text expand what is searched. Without All nodes, search filters the current gallery. You do not need a special search expression.

title: Tags & Virtual Galleries
content: To protect your folder hierarchy and avoid accidental data mutations, Virtual Galleries are structurally read-only: Action Allowed in Virtual Gallery? Notes Preview Media Yes Open PDFs, play audio, maximize images Edit Slot Notes Yes Edits save directly to the origin slot Origin Jump-Back Yes Click the origin card badge to jump to the real node in the tree Drag & Drop Reorder No Order is determined by search relevance Merge Stacks / Delete No Must perform structural edits on the origin node A virtual gallery is a view of existing content, not a new destination. Jump to the origin node before reorganizing its cards, and check Joe’s Flow / Node / Slot target before requesting changes. See Choosing Joe’s target.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: Research, bookmark, and clip web references directly into outline slots without leaving your workspace. The desktop app includes an In-App Browser. Browser guests open web links in their own browser rather than using the owner’s browser panel. Because research shouldn’t force you to toggle between your workspace and external browsers, FlowJoe embeds web browsing directly into the visual shell, allowing you to clip content, capture screenshots, and save bookmarks in one click. Keep the source and the reason you saved it together.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: The in-app browser is powered by a secure, sandboxed Electron runtime and features standard browser controls: Tab Management: Open multiple tabs, reorder them, pin tabs to save space, and organize tabs into color-coded Tab Groups. The Start Page (flowjoe://start): Your launchpad containing a Google/web search bar, lists of recent tabs, history logs, and your bookmarks. Persistent Session Restore: If you close FlowJoe, reopening the app automatically restores all your open tabs, their tab groups, and their complete back/forward navigation stacks.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: The main superpower of the embedded browser is its tight integration with the gallery: Send to Gallery: From any active web page, click the Send to Gallery button (or right-click and choose Send Tab to Gallery). Metadata Extraction: FlowJoe automatically extracts the page title, description, favicon, and canonical URL. Full-Page screenshots: Electron opens a background renderer to take a clean screenshot of the web page, saving it as a high-fidelity visual card directly in your active node’s gallery. Branded Fallbacks: If you save empty placeholders or documentation domains (e.g. example.com), FlowJoe automatically renders them as branded cards (using the signature coffee-mug logo), preventing clutter.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: Organize your web references with a powerful bookmarks system: Quick Bookmark: Click the star icon in the address bar to add a page to your favorites. Bookmark Folders: Save pages into custom folders. You can right-click a folder to open all links at once, turn a folder into a tab group, or send a folder’s URLs directly to your outlines. Bookmark All Tabs: Right-click the tab strip to bookmark all open tabs into a new folder instantly—perfect for packing up a research session. Import/Export: Sync bookmarks, tab groups, and history between devices. You can choose to merge new imports or replace existing local databases.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: FlowJoe records a chronological log of all your visits, saved locally in IndexedDB: Retention Controls: Configure history cleanup intervals in Settings (keep visits forever, or prune after 30, 90, or 365 days). Smart Pruning: When old history visits are pruned, FlowJoe preserves all metadata for bookmarked pages, ensuring your saved sites never lose their titles or descriptions. History to Folder: Turn any history time-bucket (e.g., “Yesterday’s research”) into a permanent folder or send it straight to an outline node.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: FlowJoe treats web security as a priority: Sandbox Mode: Web views run with nodeIntegration: false, contextIsolation: true, and sandbox: true to prevent malicious scripts from accessing local files. Website permissions: Websites in this panel cannot use the camera, microphone, or location. Open a site in your regular browser if it needs those permissions. Downloads follow the browser’s download settings, including whether to ask for a save location. Clear Browsing Data: In Settings → Browser, choose Website Data, FlowJoe Browser Data, or Both. Website data covers cookies and temporary files for known sites. FlowJoe browser data includes bookmarks, history, tabs, tab groups, and saved sessions; clearing it resets the tabs to the home page. Export browser data first if you want to keep it.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: In the desktop app with Joe’s Read access, explicitly ask Joe to read or summarize the current page. Explicit requests and refusals are recognized in all20 app languages. The page is shared for that request only; the page text is not saved into chat history. Unknown wording may need a clearer request. Joe can read the captured page in parts and receives its title, URL and capture time. Switching tabs, navigating or reloading cancels the old capture. The existing page extraction limit still applies, and Joe is told when the capture is incomplete. A model-generated tool request cannot grant permission on your behalf. Guest sessions and scheduled tasks cannot read the owner’s open browser page. The existing page context continues to work with each selectable Joe provider. Before sending it, FlowJoe checks that the page and your access still match the request. If either changed while Joe was preparing, that response is cancelled. In Joe’s chat, on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex), the page-reading tool can continue the same capture in parts. On a Mac this includes Antigravity; on Windows and Linux, Antigravity can’t use Flow tools yet. External agents, including the FlowJoe CLI, cannot use that page-reading tool, because they have no way to receive your page approval; the page you explicitly ask about still reaches every provider as context.

title: In-App Browser & Web Clipping
content: When a web page warns that leaving could lose changes, FlowJoe shows its Leave/Stay warning in your selected app language. Choose Stay to return to the page or Leave to continue.

title: Global Audio Player & Soundtrack
content: Vibe to your favorite music, work tapes, podcast refs, or voice logs without breaking your flow state. Staying in the flow means having the right sound in your ears. Whether you are mixing music tracks, auditing podcast clips, reviewing client feedback notes, or just vibing to your favorite focus beats, FlowJoe ensures audio is never treated as a silent, static attachment. FlowJoe features a Global Header Audio Player built directly into the workspace frame—giving you persistent playback that flows with you as you branch, draft, and brainstorm. Opening and closing music cues for a podcast. These are original synthetic three-note cues, not speech recordings.

title: Global Audio Player & Soundtrack
content: Most tools force you to stay on a specific page to listen to attached audio, or open cluttering external media player windows. In FlowJoe, audio lives on the header shell: Zero Interruption: Start a track in the tree’s Research branch, and keep listening as you jump into Milestones to update tasks or brainstorm with Joe. Exclusivity Sync: Starting playback on the header player automatically pauses any other video or audio cards playing on your active gallery board, keeping your workspace aurally clean.

title: Global Audio Player & Soundtrack
content: Curation is instantaneous. You don’t need to manually configure files to build a queue: Drag-and-Drop: Drag individual audio slots or entire media stacks from your gallery and drop them onto the header player to build a temporary queue. Right-Click Instead: Right-click any audio slot and choose Send to Global Player to load it into the header player and start it, so the music keeps playing when you leave the node. If that track is already the one playing, it simply carries on from where it is. Choose Add to Queue to line the track up after what is playing without interrupting it (if nothing is loaded yet, it starts playing). Auto-Filter Queues: By default, the player compiles a queue from your currently selected tree node. You can add a Tag Filter (e.g. #mix-take-3 or #voicemail) to automatically isolate target audio files. Format-Safe: Dropping stacks containing mixed media (e.g. images + audio files) is fully supported; FlowJoe filters out non-audio files automatically.

title: Global Audio Player & Soundtrack
content: The active queue keeps both cues together and links each one back to its source node. Clicking the queue button on the header player opens the Playlist Modal—your command center for track management: Current Queue Tab: Manage your active playback queue. Reorder tracks using drag-and-drop, delete items, search through titles/nodes/tags, or click the link badge to jump directly to the origin tree node where that audio file resides. Saved Playlists Tab: Turn your active queue into a named, permanent playlist. You can reload, update, rename, or reorder playlists at any time. Keyboard Control: Capture full keyboard navigation inside the playlist modal: Space / Enter to play the selected track. Delete / Backspace to remove tracks from the queue. Cmd/Ctrl+A to select all tracks. Escape to dismiss the panel.

title: Global Audio Player & Soundtrack
content: FlowJoe parses incoming audio files (MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV, FLAC, OGG) on drag-import and builds rich visual assets: ID3 Metadata Extraction: Instantly extracts track title, artist name, and album metadata to format player titles and list rows. Embedded Album Art: Automatically extracts embedded cover art and caches it in local storage, rendering it as the preview thumbnail of the gallery slot. Artwork Flyout: Open the cover art panel to upload custom files or generate placeholders, keeping your references visually striking. Joe: You can ask Joe to set, replace, or remove the album art on an audio item, using a picture already saved in FlowJoe. On a linked audio file the cover is remembered on this machine and does not change the file itself. Joe: You can ask Joe to play the current queue, choose a saved playlist by name, change playback mode, play one gallery audio file once, or play audio carrying one of your tags. These controls take effect right away; they do not use an approval card. Hiding the player stops playback.

title: Global Audio Player & Soundtrack
content: “Play some music.” Joe starts the current queue. If it is empty, he starts the first non-empty saved playlist he can access, in the order shown in the player. “Shuffle the current queue.” Joe turns on shuffle for that queue. “Loop this track.” Joe turns on repeat-one. “Play the playlist in order” uses sequential mode, which repeats the queue when it reaches the end. “Play the audio in the Opening node once.” If the node has several audio files, name the slot or stack item so Joe can choose the exact file; playback stops when that file ends. “Play something tagged calm.” Joe can match a mood or vibe only when your visible audio slots have a matching user tag. Add tags such as calm, focus, or upbeat to the audio you want grouped; Joe does not guess a mood from a filename. “Save this queue as Focus Mix.” Joe saves the current queue under that name. To save tagged audio without starting playback or changing the current queue, ask “Make a playlist called Quiet Work from audio tagged calm.” He asks for a name if you did not give one and will not overwrite an existing playlist. Joe can only select a one-off file or tag he can see. Hidden-from-Joe and locked private nodes are not searched or played. Joe does not list track titles in his tool results.

title: Global Audio Player & Soundtrack
content: Your soundtracks are as portable as your outlines. When you export your app preferences, FlowJoe bundles all your saved playlists and loop settings, allowing you to transfer your focus environment cleanly between devices.

title: Integrated terminal (Forge)
content: Keep shell sessions and connected coding assistants beside your workspace. Forge brings a real terminal into the desktop app, so your command-line work can sit beside the ideas, references, and notes that explain it. Open Terminal from the app rail.

title: Integrated terminal (Forge)
content: Use + to open another tab. Double-click a tab to rename it. Drag tabs to reorder them, move them between panels, or drop them in empty space to create another panel. Move and resize panels within the FlowJoe window. Maximize expands a panel inside that window. You can also focus a tab and press Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key, or right-click it: Move left and Move right reorder the tab; an action is unavailable at that end of the strip. Move to new panel carries the tab to another panel. It is unavailable when the tab is already alone. Move to… lists the other existing panels by their current tab names, such as Main terminal (Shell). Choosing a hidden or minimized panel reveals it. Use the menu’s arrow keys, Home and End to move between available actions, and Enter or Space to choose. Right opens Move to…; Left returns from its submenu. Escape closes the innermost menu. Focus follows the moved tab, and its shell and output keep running. An empty detached panel closes. These menu keys apply to focused tabs; typing in a shell or renaming a tab keeps its usual behavior.

title: Integrated terminal (Forge)
content: Minimizing a panel keeps its shells running. Closing the main panel hides it and preserves its sessions for reopening. Closing a detached panel or an individual tab ends its shells. Quitting or reloading FlowJoe also ends sessions. Screen readers can navigate the terminal’s visible rows and receive announcements as output arrives. For a very large burst of output, xterm limits live announcements while keeping the rows available to read.

title: Integrated terminal (Forge)
content: Enable Settings → Joe AI → Agent Bridge (MCP), then run your connected assistant in Forge or another terminal. The bridge runs in FlowJoe independently of the shell. Forge is a normal terminal: commands use your account’s permissions, and can change files just as they can in another terminal app. Agent Bridge approval controls apply to changes requested through FlowJoe’s bridge, rather than every command you type. You can also use an installed tool as Joe’s brain. In that case you talk to Joe in his chat panel; you do not need to open Forge or keep a terminal conversation running. An interactive assistant in Forge and Joe’s conversation have separate histories. See Agent Bridge for connection and approval settings. Terminal sessions are a desktop feature; they are unavailable in standalone browsers and shared guest sessions.

title: Integrated terminal (Forge)
content: Only the selected excerpt is offered for the question. Sharing it does not grant terminal control. Joe cannot see your terminal on his own. When you want him to look at some output, select those lines in the terminal tab you are viewing, then ask Joe about them in his chat. Joe asks to read the output, and a card appears in his chat: Share selected output with Joe? It shows the tab, the selected lines and the exact text. Nothing is shared until you press Share with Joe. Press Cancel and nothing is shared. If nothing is selected, Joe asks you to select the lines first. If you close the tab before pressing Share, nothing is shared. While the card waits, New chat cancels it and nothing is shared. Switching to another node or slot keeps it waiting, and it is there when you come back. Escape also cancels it. Only the selected excerpt is shared for that question. Other tabs and later output stay private. After sharing, Revoke future access stops Joe from reading that excerpt again later in the conversation. What he already received stays in the chat. Joe can also re-read the excerpt only while its card is still in the chat: if you close and reopen Joe, he can no longer read it again, though what he already received stays. Sharing output does not let Joe type into the terminal or run commands. This works in Joe’s chat in the desktop app, on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex). On a Mac this includes Antigravity; on Windows and Linux, Antigravity can’t use Flow tools yet. It is not available to shared guests, scheduled tasks, or assistants connected from outside through the Agent Bridge. Shared excerpts are forgotten when you reload FlowJoe.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: Live, formulas-ready spreadsheets running inside your gallery slots. The Spreadsheet Workbench uses Univer Sheets to edit cells beside your research.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: New Spreadsheet: Click Add Slot (or Add First Slot on an empty node) in the gallery and select New Spreadsheet. This initializes an empty slot running the Univer Sheets engine. Importing Files: Drag and drop .csv, .tsv, .xlsx, .ods, or .xls files directly onto the gallery. FlowJoe turns each one into an editable spreadsheet slot automatically (there is no prompt), and keeps your untouched original file hidden behind it so you can download it again.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: An imported CSV becomes an editable launch budget. These illustrative totals are imported values, not a demonstrated formula calculation. Formulas & Math: Supports standard spreadsheet formulas (SUM, IF, etc.). Multi-Tab Sheets: Add, rename, and delete multiple tabs inside a single spreadsheet slot. Formatting: Edit font styling, backgrounds, borders, alignment, and column widths. Exporting: Download the sheet from the slot’s menu. It saves in the same format you imported (.csv, .tsv, .xlsx or .ods); a new spreadsheet, or an imported .xls, downloads as .xlsx. Appearance: The spreadsheet always uses a light look, even when the app is in a dark theme.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: Treat imported spreadsheets as editable copies focused on values, sheets, and basic formulas. Charts, pivot tables, macros, and advanced formatting are not preserved. Use Download Original for the unchanged source, especially for complex workbooks or legacy .xls files. CSV and TSV downloads contain one sheet. Very large sheets and long cell text can be cut down during import; use Download Original for the complete source. Download Original in the slot’s menu returns the untouched imported file. Its filename adds _orig before the source extension, such as Budget_orig.xlsx, so you can distinguish it from the edited copy. It stays hidden behind the single editable slot.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: Joe and external terminal agents can read spreadsheet content using the get_island_content tool. Analysis: Ask Joe questions like “Summarize the total budget in the budget spreadsheet” or “Find the outliers in this CSV slot.” Write-back: Joe can set the value of a single cell at a time (for example “Put 1200 in B3”). He does not write formulas, change formatting, or add rows and columns. [!NOTE] Resource Isolation: The spreadsheet workbench only loads its UI dependencies when you open it, keeping the rest of the gallery fast and lightweight. Joe can list the sheets and read a specific range, such as A2001:C2050, then continue through larger results in pages. He reports which cells were actually read; stored formulas do not prove a fresh calculation. The Spreadsheet file-type badge appears beside the Preview title, leaving the editor toolbar clear.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: While editing, press F6 (or Ctrl+F6) to return to Preview’s Close control. This moves keyboard focus without closing the spreadsheet. Tab continues to navigate cells, Escape keeps its normal editor action, and autosave continues as usual. The editor stays out of the way after you leave it, even if a cursor movement was still finishing. You can use Tab to return to the workbench controls or click the editing area to continue typing. Closing Preview or moving to another stack item waits for your edits to save. If saving fails, the editor stays open with your draft. Once storage is available again, retry Close, Save, or the stack move without retyping your changes. An earlier autosave finishing does not cancel that retry: your latest changes still need to save. Keep the editor open until saving succeeds. Preview also waits for your latest edit when an earlier autosave is still finishing; it stays open until that edit is saved. Closing the desktop window or quitting FlowJoe also waits for your editor to save. If saving cannot be confirmed, choose Stay open to keep your draft, or Retry save once storage is available again. Close anyway or Quit anyway leaves without confirming the save and may lose your unsaved changes.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: Accessibility tools can identify the Font, Font size, Range / Defined names, Add sheet, Open sheet menu and More controls. The built-in editor currently uses English for these controls, even when FlowJoe uses another language. These names do not change how you edit cells or format text. When Zoom has keyboard focus, the arrow keys adjust it. When More has focus, Enter opens it and Escape closes it and returns focus. Arrow keys in the Font field keep their text-field behavior.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: The earlier native Mac checks below concern the canvas Editor. Screen-reader speech and nonvisual editing are not yet verified on Mac. Current accessibility checks found that the built-in editor exposes toolbar controls but does not expose the tested cell values through the Mac text-reading interfaces checked. This remains an open accessibility limitation. F6 still moves focus from the editor to Preview’s Close control.

title: Spreadsheet Workbench
content: Preview starts in Editor. Choose Read content for a native table of the current sheet’s populated cells. Column letters, row numbers and cell names retain the original coordinates. Empty rows and columns are omitted; there is no reading-view row limit. Values use the live editor’s display, including available formula results, dates and currency. Return to Editor, choose another sheet, then Read content to read it. The switch keeps the same editor and does not change formulas, formatting or data. F6 returns to Preview’s Close control from the reading pane too. Reading is separate from nonvisual editing: this view does not make canvas editing accessible or establish spoken screen-reader results. Charts, drawings and every merged-cell layout are not reproduced.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: Real word-processing islands for drafting documents. The Rich Document Workbench utilizes Univer Docs to provide a real word-processing engine inside individual gallery slots.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: Create Blank Document: Click Add Slot, choose New Document…, then pick Rich Text Document. Importing Text: Drag and drop .docx, .odt, or .rtf files to import them. They open as editable document slots with styled text, lists, and embedded images; your untouched original stays hidden behind the slot so you can download it again.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: The Northstar launch brief opens as an editable document. The source RTF remains available separately. Typography styling: Change headers, font weights, colors, text alignment, and spacing. Image Integration: Paste images directly from your clipboard into the body of the document. Headers & Footers: Double-click the top or bottom margin of a page to edit its header or footer. Tables from imported files are kept when you save, but they cannot be edited in the editor yet. Exporting: Download your edited copy from the slot’s menu. It always saves as a .docx file (.odt and .rtf files are imported but not written back). Appearance: The editor always uses a light look, even when the app is in a dark theme. Download Original in the slot’s menu returns the untouched imported file, with _orig before its source extension (for example, Brief_orig.rtf). It stays hidden behind the single editable slot, separate from the edited DOCX download.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: Joe can work with your rich documents: Content Retrieval: Joe reads document text using the get_island_content tool. Drafting and Editing: Joe can read your document and suggest rewrites, spelling fixes, or expansions in chat, but he cannot write changes directly into a rich document yet. Copy the text you want into the editor. Joe can read a late section by block and continue through a long document in pages, including stored headers and footers. If the document changes during a read, he must read it again rather than combine different versions. When you edit a shared rich text document as an Edit guest, pictures you add are saved with the document on the owner’s computer. Later saves keep its existing pictures and imported original. The Rich Document file-type badge appears beside the Preview title, leaving the editor toolbar clear.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: While editing, press F6 (or Ctrl+F6) to return to Preview’s Close control. This moves keyboard focus without closing the document. Tab and Escape keep their normal editor actions, and autosave continues as usual. The editor stays out of the way after you leave it, even if a cursor movement was still finishing. You can use Tab to return to the workbench controls or click the editing area to continue typing. Closing Preview or moving to another stack item waits for your edits to save. If saving fails, the editor stays open with your draft. Once storage is available again, retry Close, Save, or the stack move without retyping your changes. An earlier autosave finishing does not cancel that retry: your latest changes still need to save. Keep the editor open until saving succeeds. Preview also waits for your latest edit when an earlier autosave is still finishing; it stays open until that edit is saved. Closing the desktop window or quitting FlowJoe also waits for your editor to save. If saving cannot be confirmed, choose Stay open to keep your draft, or Retry save once storage is available again. Close anyway or Quit anyway leaves without confirming the save and may lose your unsaved changes. When saving your edits, this also protects pictures you paste into the document: if a picture cannot be saved, your draft stays open for you to retry.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: Accessibility tools can identify the Font, Font size and More controls. The built-in editor currently uses English for these controls, even when FlowJoe uses another language. These names do not change how you format your document. When Zoom has keyboard focus, the arrow keys adjust it. When More has focus, Enter opens it and Escape closes it and returns focus. Arrow keys in the Font field keep their text-field behavior.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: The earlier native Mac checks below concern the canvas Editor. Screen-reader speech and nonvisual editing are not yet verified on Mac. Current accessibility checks found that the built-in editor exposes toolbar controls but does not expose the tested document text through the Mac text-reading interfaces checked. This remains an open accessibility limitation. F6 still moves focus from the editor to Preview’s Close control.

title: Rich Document Workbench
content: Preview starts in Editor. Choose Read content for the current document’s main body as native headings, paragraphs, lists and simple text emphasis where the document carries that information. Return to Editor to edit; switching retains the same document and does not change its text or formatting. F6 returns to Preview’s Close control from the reading pane too. This optional view supports reading, not nonvisual editing or verified screen-reader speech. It does not reproduce every table, drawing, embedded object, header or footer. The earlier Mac editor-text limitation remains separate from this native reading view.

title: Calendar Workbench
content: Manage timelines, schedules, and ICS files in a unified view. The Calendar Workbench uses FullCalendar to schedule events beside your research.

title: Calendar Workbench
content: Choose the shape that fits the work: one editable calendar or events organized into cards or nodes. You can import schedules in several shapes: Import ICS/iCal: Drop a .ics or .ical file onto the tree or gallery to create a calendar slot directly. To choose its shape, use Add Slot → Image or File and select the calendar file. The picker offers a Calendar Slot, separate Event Cards, one Stack, or Event Nodes grouped under the selected parent. New Blank Calendar: Click New Calendar from the gallery menu.

title: Calendar Workbench
content: The launch milestones in List view. Times are displayed in the viewing computer’s timezone; this sample was captured in America/Denver. Open a Calendar slot to use the FullCalendar workbench: Multiple Views: Switch between Month, Week, Day, and Agenda List views. Manage Events: Tab to New event, Enter, then Save; Cancel/Close returns. Edit or delete existing events. Drag & Resize: Drag event cards to change dates, or drag block edges to resize duration. Changes save in the FlowJoe calendar; download an .ics copy to use elsewhere. Exporting: Save calendars back to a standard .ics file.

title: Calendar Workbench
content: Joe receives calendar agendas as parsed, readable text: Planning: Ask Joe “Find conflicts in my schedule next week” or “Draft an itinerary for Tuesday.” Original versus edited copy: Download Original keeps the untouched imported calendar. Downloading the edited calendar creates an .ics file from its current events; it does not preserve every original calendar field. Calendar Slot and Stack keep this hidden original; its filename adds _orig before the source extension, such as Team_orig.ics. Event Cards and Event Nodes have no single original file.

title: Calendar Workbench
content: Calendar imports are copies, not live subscriptions to Google Calendar, Outlook, or another provider. Recurring events retain readable recurrence information, but FlowJoe does not expand every occurrence or provide reminder notifications or provider write-back. Joe can read a date window in a named timezone and continue through events beyond the first page. He reads stored events; this does not expand recurring events or sync with an outside calendar. The Calendar file-type badge appears beside the Preview title, leaving the editor toolbar clear.

title: Calendar Workbench
content: If Start cannot be read, or a supplied End cannot be read or comes before or at Start, the event form stays open and identifies the field to correct. Your previous event and the text you entered remain available. Correct the field and Save again, or Cancel to keep the previous event. End can be left blank. For an all-day event, End remains the first day after the event. When you open an existing event with the keyboard, Cancel or the event form’s close button returns you to that event when it is still visible. If you already moved to another window, closing the form leaves your focus there.

title: Pet Joe
content: Show, resize, and interact with the optional animated companion in FlowJoe's gallery. Pet Joe is an optional 8-bit companion in the gallery. He is hidden by default and appears after the selected gallery has loaded. The optional animated companion. You can show or hide it from the rail.

title: Pet Joe
content: Use the Pet Joe button in the app rail to show or hide him. Right-click Pet Joe and choose Settings to resize him. The slider ranges from 96 to 192 px in 8 px steps. Reset size returns him to 128 px, and FlowJoe remembers a size you choose.

title: Pet Joe
content: On startup, he appears at the right end of his gallery path, takes a coffee sip, then walks across the path. At either end, he stops for coffee and turns after the sip. Hovering over him stops his travel and starts a coffee sip in place. After you move the pointer away, he completes the sip, turns, and resumes walking. When you add or reorder a tree item or gallery item, he points toward that change. When the global music player starts a song or changes tracks during playback, he dances for three seconds, facing the direction he was walking, then returns to Joe’s current activity. Click Pet Joe to open or focus Joe chat. The buttons below him start a new chat or live dictation. Right-click for Hide Pet Joe and Settings. Pet Joe follows FlowJoe’s motion preferences. Reduced motion or disabled animations stop his travel and sprite animation. Joe’s accessible status remains available when Pet Joe is hidden.

title: Meeting Joe
content: How to open Joe, interact, and manage active AI chat sessions. Joe is your local AI collaborator. Here is how you access Joe and manage your chat sessions.

title: Meeting Joe
content: You can invoke Joe’s assistant panel from multiple places: Robot icon: Click the robot on the left rail or in the header to open Joe’s panel. The speech bubbles right after it open Chat, where you talk with the people in a shared Flow, not with Joe. Joe and Chat share the right-hand column; whichever is showing is highlighted in both places. Keyboard Shortcut: Press Cmd+Shift+A / Ctrl+Shift+A to open, minimize, or restore the Joe panel. (Ctrl+J copies the selected node’s JSON — it does not open Joe.) Node Summary brainstorm: Click “Brainstorm with Joe” inside the Node Summary modal. Gallery Slot Brainstorm: Select a gallery card and click the Robot button to open chat targeted to that specific slot.

title: Meeting Joe
content: A draft question for the Lantern Vale board. It has not been sent; the greeting and suggestions are the app’s actual opening state. When Joe is active, his interface is clean and lightweight: Docked or floating: Joe normally opens beside the gallery. Drag the divider to resize the column, use Widen for more room, or pop Joe out into a floating window. All four docked tabs share your chosen column width; the default is 280 pixels. Streaming replies: Joe’s answers appear as they’re written, not all at once at the end — including replies that come after he reads or checks something (a multi-step answer streams in each step). Joe can finish a reply or move to its next step as soon as the completed response arrives, even if the connection takes longer to close. On the Claude-family CLI brains (see Bring Your Own Brain), the terminal agent’s own reply streams too; Gemini API replies also stream. Grok and Antigravity currently show their full reply at once instead. Multi-step desktop replies: With Luna 6 and your OpenAI key, Joe automatically reuses a connection while reading or checking things for your answer. Your model, token prices and approval choices stay the same. Stop also ends connection startup. Stop really stops. Clicking Stop cancels the current reply, including a wait for the chapter picker or TypeSafe. On a CLI brain (Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Antigravity), it also cancels the running CLI request and closes any temporary Flow connection. It does not undo changes already applied. Keyboard focus after Stop or Regenerate: When the focused Stop button changes back to a disabled Send button, focus moves to the message box. Using the focused Regenerate control also returns focus to the message box. If you have moved to another control, Joe leaves focus there. Voice Dictation: Click the microphone icon or hold your voice shortcut key to dictate prompts. Joe supports a robust voice command set (e.g. saying “comma”, “new line”, or “delete last word” inserts the

title: Meeting Joe
content: the correct characters). Talk with Joe: In a private desktop chat, open the arrow beside the microphone for a live voice conversation. It uses your saved Joe voice and selected chat brain. Live voice is $0.05/minute, plus brain and tool usage. See Talk with Joe for controls and recovery. Clickable prompt suggestions: Ask Joe for ideas or prompts you could try next, and he can show them as buttons below his reply. Clicking one puts it in the message box; review or edit it before sending. Joe voice: Choose a voice in Settings → AI → Joe voice. The existing ten voices have Mini and Full read-aloud choices. The Live conversation voices group adds 21 choices labelled with their language and regional accent, where applicable. In the desktop app, choosing a voice or pressing its speaker button plays a short billed sample; press the button again to stop. Samples do not use your microphone. Read-aloud: Mini and Full choices can read replies manually or through Auto-read Joe replies aloud. Live-only choices are for Talk with Joe; selecting one makes read-aloud unavailable while keeping your saved auto-read preference. Choose Mini or Full again to restore it. The selected chat brain stays unchanged. Numbers in read-aloud: The check before playback recognizes forms such as “one hundred and one” for 101 and Spanish integer forms such as “veintiún” for 21. Negative numbers must keep their minus sign; speech that changes the number is rejected. This does not cover every number format or language. Stopping read-aloud: Stopping speech also cancels startup. A late voice-session connection cannot restart it, and incomplete generation is rejected before its audio plays. Stopping also ends a wait for your audio device to start. Read-aloud and preview buttons return to their normal state when playback finishes, including when the sound has already ended as the response finishes arriving. Voice startup errors: If voice startup fails, Joe ends the attempt and shows an error instead of

title: Meeting Joe
content: of waiting for the full speech timeout. You can try again when ready. Honest waits and clear errors. If a request needs to retry (a brief provider hiccup), Joe’s status shows Retrying… instead of looking stuck on “thinking”. If something goes wrong — you’re out of quota, your key was rejected, or the provider is having trouble — the chat shows a plain-language reason instead of a raw technical error, with the original provider text available underneath if you need it for support. If a chat message genuinely fails to save (for example, storage is full), you see a one-time warning toast instead of silently losing it. Regenerate stays available. After starting a new conversation and reopening FlowJoe, the Regenerate option on Joe’s last reply keeps working, instead of silently disappearing. OpenAI voice pricing · October 2026 Vendor pricing, not FlowJoe pricing. USD list rates checked October 22, 2026; OpenAI bills your API account. Voice choice Model Generated audio / 1M tokens Text input / 1M tokens Mini gpt-realtime-2.1-mini $20 $0.60 Full gpt-realtime-2.1 $64 $4 Live conversation voices cost $0.05/minute, including their Settings samples. During a conversation, brain and tool usage are extra.Text input is charged in addition to generated audio. Full’s audio rate is 3.2× Mini’s. Voice previews are billed too.Check current OpenAI voice pricing before use; rates can change.

title: Meeting Joe
content: Use What Joe received this turn beside a sent message to see its recorded context. Included tools lists tool instructions included for that turn; it does not mean Joe used every tool. Available on demand appears only when that request actually offered tool groups to load as needed. Skills and Knowledge appear when there is something to show. This view explains a past turn. The Off / Read / Propose selector still controls Joe’s Flow access, and the wrench beside the prompt still opens extra-context options.

title: Meeting Joe
content: The target section below the tabs shows the node and, when selected, its slot. Chat, Spelling, Transcribe and Images use the same node tree and slot list. Whole flow: Click the crosshair at the far left of the target section. Joe opens Flow Chat and the target shows just the Flow name. Click the crosshair again to return to the previous node or slot, including the previous tool tab. Node or slot: Open the node picker, then right-click a node inside Joe’s target tree. The menu offers Target the whole flow, Target this node, then Choose a slot…. Choosing a node opens that node’s Chat; choosing a slot keeps the tool tab you are using. Long slot lists scroll. The open list stays on the node you chose while Joe refreshes in the background; if its slots are reordered, your choice still follows the same slot. You can also open this menu from a focused tree row with Shift+F10. Slot field in Chat: A node conversation shows Choose a slot… without marking any slot selected. Choosing one opens that slot’s conversation. You can also use the slot field directly in the other three tabs. Across tabs: An explicit slot choice in Spelling, Transcribe or Images stays selected when you return to Chat. Merely opening a tool from a node conversation uses a remembered slot, or its first slot, and returns to the node conversation when you switch back without choosing another slot. Opening a tool from Flow Chat returns to an available node/slot and exposes the same selectors. Last used: A separate Last used badge marks the most recently visited slot in that node, including gallery visits and notes editing. It is separate from Joe’s selected-target highlight, so you can see both while Joe is locked to another slot. Recent slot visits are remembered on this computer after restart and follow the slot when it is reordered. Deleted slots are not replaced by whichever slot takes their old position. Lock: The lock keeps Joe on the chosen target while you browse. Explicit target choices still work

title: Meeting Joe
content: work when locked; unfinished operations and read-only conversations keep their existing target restrictions. Unsent Chat text stays with its conversation. Unapplied Spelling text stays with its slot while you change tabs, choose another slot or visit Flow Chat and return. These unfinished text drafts are kept for this session; apply or save them before closing the app. The recent-visit badge is a separate remembered preference, not a saved Spelling draft. Replacing or reopening a Flow starts a new document session; unfinished drafts from the previous document are not inserted into the new one. Ordinary updates to the same shared Flow keep your session drafts. Send stays dimmed and disabled until your message contains text beyond spaces or blank lines. While Joe is preparing or answering, the button becomes Stop and stays available even when the message box is empty. While Joe is preparing a reply, answering, compacting a conversation or waiting for a proposal decision, target choices keep the current work in place. Clicking Chat during a reply keeps that reply running. A chosen slot follows its identity when slots are reordered; if it disappears, choose a live destination before sending again. Loading an older conversation only updates the place you are still viewing. Replacing the Flow ends work that belonged to the previous document. With OpenAI, spelling uses the lower-cost Luna 6 helper independently of your chosen chat model. Spelling protects embedded images and other media during correction. If Joe returns an incomplete or damaged media reference, FlowJoe rejects that correction instead of offering it for Apply. Notes containing only media are left unchanged without an AI request. Spelling checks the destination again when you press Apply. If the node or an ancestor is now frozen or password-locked, your role is View, or the workspace is temporarily unable to accept edits, the correction is not written and the review remains available.

title: Meeting Joe
header: Your conversations stay with their place
content: Each slot, node and summary keeps its own conversation with Joe. A slot’s conversation stays with that slot: moving or reordering slots keeps it attached, and nothing is dropped to make room for newer ones, so every older conversation is kept. Chat History: Click History (the clock icon) at the top of Joe’s chat to see the conversations for the place you are on. The list names the real place (for example Research › Slot 3) and ends with All conversations in this flow · N, which opens the Chat History tab of History. Back to …: When Joe’s docked panel follows you to a different node or slot, a Back to “conversation title” · N messages row appears under the new place so you can return to the conversation you left. It stays until you click it, dismiss it with Dismiss, send a message in the new place, lock the new place, or switch somewhere else again. It only appears when the conversation you left had messages. Guests can return to conversations in shared, nonprivate work; a conversation becomes unavailable when its place is made private or removed from their share. Omit, Pin and Delete buttons sit flush against the message they belong to. In a narrow Joe column they turn into small icons; hover one to see its name. Shared conversations: Your messages and guests’ messages carry a small avatar beside the bottom-right of the bubble. Hover or keyboard-focus the avatar to see who wrote it. A matching avatar above the message box shows who else is typing to Joe. A slot moved into a private node keeps its conversation private immediately. If saved chat cannot be read, FlowJoe protects it from being replaced; reopen the conversation after storage is available again. See History & Recovery for the Chat History and Image History tabs.

title: Meeting Joe
content: Joe is given a bundle with each send, not only the sentence you typed: Where you are — the selected node, its summary, and the active gallery slot or stack. The flow map — a name-and-id outline of the tree. By default this is limited to the node you are on, everything under it, and the path up to the root (Limit map to my location, on by default). You can send the whole tree, or omit the map entirely, with the checkboxes above the message box. The text of the current slot, plus any documents, spreadsheets, or files you attach. How those choices affect cost: Token usage with Joe. [!TIP] Pill Minimization: You can minimize the Joe panel into a floating tray button. Your session histories and generated image cards are preserved, allowing you to quickly pop Joe open, review a draft, and close him again.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: Choose Joe’s connection, set up your keys, and use a brain that suits your work. Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB) lets you choose the intelligence behind Joe. Use your own provider API key, or connect a supported command-line assistant you already use. Your workspace lives locally; the context needed for an AI request goes to the chosen provider. A command-line tool, or CLI, is an app you run by typing commands in a terminal. FlowJoe can use some of these tools behind the scenes, so you keep talking to Joe in the familiar chat panel. The connection direction determines where you converse and which approval settings apply. When you use OpenAI, automatic image titles and archived-chat titles use Luna 6 to keep these short labeling tasks inexpensive, independently of your selected chat model. A title request that cannot finish keeps the existing fallback; it does not change your main reply or generated image.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: Your account, your usage: API brains use your provider key and its usage charges. CLI brains use that tool’s account, plan, and limits. FlowJoe adds no markup to either connection. How much context you send affects usage; see Token usage with Joe. Model Choice: You choose exactly which model drives Joe—whether you want the speed of a lighter model or the reasoning of a frontier model. Privacy & Control: Owner requests go from your desktop to the selected provider or installed tool, rather than through a FlowJoe AI service. Shared guests use the owner’s authorized connection; they do not receive its credentials.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: Choose how FlowJoe keeps each key in Settings → APIs. Desktop storage: Keys normally use OS encryption. If it fails or is weak, Use for this session keeps the saved key intact; Try again retries a failed read. Temporary keys end when you quit FlowJoe. Browser storage: New keys last until refresh or close. Save on this computer as plain text requires an explicit choice. Existing plaintext copies stay until you choose to keep or remove them. Tasks need a key again after its session ends. Export choice: Keys are excluded from portable exports by default. You can explicitly include an OpenAI key, so review that checkbox before sharing a package. API-key encryption protects the saved key only. Private nodes have their own encryption. See What is encrypted today.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: To adjust your model config: For an API brain, add its key in Settings → APIs. For a CLI brain, install and sign into its tool first, as described below. Click the model settings button inside the Joe panel — or the brain name in the status bar — to pick the brain behind Joe: OpenAI models (API key): Sol 6.1, Sol 6.1 Ultrafast (the same model on OpenAI’s faster, six-times-priced tier; never chosen for you; it speeds up Joe’s chat replies only), Terra 6.1, Luna 6 (the default), Sol 6, and Astra 6, plus Luna, Terra, and Sol from the GPT-5.6 family. Anthropic API: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 use your own Anthropic API key. This is separate from a Claude Code login: you can have both. xAI API: Grok 4.7 uses your own xAI API key. This is separate from a Grok terminal login. Gemini API: Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 4 Argon use a separate Google Gemini API key. See setup below. CLI brains (no API key): route Joe through an agent CLI you have already installed and signed into on your own machine — Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Haiku, Grok, Antigravity (4 Argon), Antigravity (3.8), Codex (6.1 Sol), Codex (6.1 Terra), Codex (6 Sol), Codex (6 Luna), Codex (5.6 Sol), Codex (5.6 Terra), Codex (5.6 Luna), or Codex (6 Astra). CLI installation and sign-in belong to the owner’s desktop. Authorized browser guests use a supported, isolated version of that selected owner CLI through Joe; they do not install it or receive its credentials. Antigravity is currently available only to the owner. Temperature and response length are managed automatically per model — there is no manual temperature dial, and GPT-5.6 / GPT-6 models run at their fixed default temperature.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: How the brain menu is arranged
content: Joe’s brain menu groups the brains by company: OpenAI first, then Anthropic · Claude, xAI · Grok and Google · Gemini. Each line says how it connects: · API key — it uses the key you saved in Settings → APIs. · Claude Code login ✓, · Codex login ✓, · Grok login ✓, · Antigravity login ✓ — it uses a terminal tool you are signed into. More dollar signs mean a more expensive AI choice: $ is the lowest-cost group and $$$$ is the highest. These symbols help you compare choices; they are not the price of a message. Plan means usage counts toward the account you signed into. See What the dollar signs mean. A company you have no key for shows one dimmed line instead of one line per model, for example Grok 4.7 — needs an xAI key, Gemini — needs a Gemini key or OpenAI — needs an OpenAI key. Once you save that key, the line opens up into the company’s models. The brain list in the status bar shows the same brains in the same order; under each API-key brain it shows the account and the start and end of the key, and a company without a key reads Needs an … API key.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: When your OpenAI key can’t use a model
content: An OpenAI project doesn’t always have access to every model. FlowJoe asks OpenAI which models your saved key can use when you open the app and each time you save or test the key, and it dims the OpenAI brains your key can’t use. In Joe’s brain menu they read … · not available on this key; in the status bar’s brain list they read Not available on this OpenAI key, and you can’t pick them. If OpenAI refuses a message because your project has no access to the model, FlowJoe remembers that too. Nothing is hidden and your brain is never switched for you. If the brain you already chose turns out to be one your key can’t use, it stays selected so you can see why a message fails. To fix it, check model access in your OpenAI organization settings, then press Test or Save on the OpenAI key in Settings → APIs so FlowJoe checks again. If FlowJoe can’t reach OpenAI to ask (for example when you’re offline), it treats every OpenAI brain as available.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Where to get an OpenAI key
content: Create one at platform.openai.com/api-keys, then paste it into Settings → APIs → OpenAI API Key. Keys start with sk-. You pay OpenAI directly for what you use; FlowJoe never takes a cut and never sees the key.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: Open Settings → APIs → Gemini API Key, paste a key from Google AI Studio, choose Test, then Save. A successful key test does not give the project an allowance for every model. Select Gemini 3.8 Flash or Gemini 4 Argon in Joe’s brain picker. Both use the same key. Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s larger model; a free Gemini key has no Gemini 4 Argon allowance, so use a key whose Google Cloud project has a paid Gemini API tier and Argon quota. Either one supports chat and writing assistance. This connection can read permitted Flow content and propose Flow, memory and task changes through the existing approval cards. It cannot search the web or use Code interpreter. Small background jobs (choosing which manual chapters to load, spell-check, compaction and attachment memories) run on Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, a cheaper model on the same key. See Token usage. If Google says your account or project has no allowance for the selected model, waiting or shortening the message will not create one. Check that key’s project, Billing Tier, and model quota in Google AI Studio, then retry after the project has access. Google documents model limits by tier and billing status and upgrades. Joe returns this refusal immediately instead of waiting through retries. Antigravity’s Google login uses its own plan and limits; it does not give a Gemini API key paid project quota.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Set up Claude or Grok with an API key
content: Open Settings → APIs and click the button beside Anthropic API Key or xAI API Key. Paste your key. The empty field shows how the provider’s keys start (sk-ant- for Anthropic, xai- for xAI), and the link under it opens the page where you create one (platform.claude.com/settings/keys or console.x.ai). Press Test. You see Testing…, then Works or Key rejected. The check lists your account’s models; it does not send a prompt or cost anything. Press Save, then pick the model in Joe’s brain menu. Some Anthropic answers have their own plain message: Key rejected: Anthropic needs a key made inside a workspace — this key was created outside any Anthropic workspace. Create a new key inside a workspace and paste that one. The key works, but the account has no credit — add credit to your Anthropic account, then try again. Gemini or xAI says the account is out of credit — Joe shows the provider’s own reason under a short explanation. Add credit (Gemini: your prepaid balance or billing in Google AI Studio; xAI: your team’s credits in the xAI console), then try again. A per-minute rate limit looks different: wait a moment and retry. “Couldn’t get a reply from …” — the request never got an answer. Check your internet connection; if it keeps happening, check that the key still has credit. This reads the same on every brain, and after a change was already made in your flow Joe says so first. Test never saves. Pressing Test checks the key you typed without storing it, for xAI too (FlowJoe checks xAI keys through the desktop app). Only Save changes your saved key, so a mistyped key never replaces one that works. xAI brains need the FlowJoe desktop app: in a plain web browser, Grok shows as “Desktop app only” in both brain lists and can’t be picked, and Test in the xAI window says the same. Like Gemini, these brains cannot search the web or use Code interpreter; the two switches are greyed out with a note that names the provider. Every one of these brains reads attached documents such as

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Set up Claude or Grok with an API key
content: as PDFs, Grok 4.7 included. If you send a message with an API-key brain whose key is missing, Joe tells you which key to add in Settings → APIs instead of sending it.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: FlowJoe does not install a CLI brain for you. Install its tool and finish sign-in in your own terminal. The brain’s choice stays dimmed when FlowJoe cannot detect a usable installation or account: Brain Needs this installed Sign in by running Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5 / Opus 5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Haiku the claude CLI claude Grok the grok CLI grok Antigravity the agy CLI agy Codex (6.1 Sol, 6 Sol, 6 Luna, 5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna, 6 Astra) the codex CLI codex login (your ChatGPT account) Codex lets Joe run on your ChatGPT plan instead of an OpenAI API key. It offers the same OpenAI models as the API-key menu: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna, and GPT-6 Astra. Quick helper tasks use GPT-5.6 Luna. Before Joe can use Codex for the first time, run codex once in a terminal so it saves its list of models on your computer; until then Joe tells you to do that. Which of these models your ChatGPT plan includes is up to OpenAI: if Codex doesn’t offer the one you picked, Joe says so and you can pick another. Gemini CLI is no longer one of Joe’s brains: Google no longer lets individuals use that tool with a personal Google sign-in. Signed in to Google? Pick Antigravity, which uses the same Google account. Have a Gemini API key? Pick Gemini 3.8 Flash or Gemini 4 Argon. If Gemini CLI was Joe’s brain, FlowJoe switched it to Antigravity (3.8) for you; if Antigravity isn’t installed and signed in, Joe moves on to the first brain that works. Antigravity offers 4 Argon and 3.8 Flash, both at Medium thinking. Quick helper tasks use 3.8 Flash Low. An older saved 3.7 choice now uses 3.8. Model access depends on your Google plan and installed Antigravity version. If a brain is greyed out, check the explanation in the picker. The tool may be missing, not signed in, or unsupported on your platform. These brains use the tool’s own account and billing; you do not paste an API key into FlowJoe for them.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Which brains can work with your Flow?
