content: Connection What Joe can do OpenAI API Read permitted content and propose Flow changes. Web search and hosted Code interpreter are available when enabled. Claude-family CLI Read permitted content, use Flow tools, inspect supported images, and propose changes. Replies appear as they arrive. Grok CLI Read permitted content, use Flow tools, inspect supported images, and propose changes. Replies arrive together when ready. Codex CLI Read permitted content, use Flow tools, inspect supported images, and propose changes. Replies arrive together when ready. Antigravity On a Mac: read permitted content, use Flow tools, and propose changes. On Windows and Linux it can only discuss the context supplied with the conversation, and it runs with your own Antigravity settings. On a Mac it can inspect pictures and PDF page images through a private temporary image folder. Web search is not available with Antigravity yet. Owner only; replies arrive together when ready. Gemini API Chat, permitted Flow reads, and proposals through the existing approval cards. No hosted web search or Code interpreter. Anthropic API Chat, permitted Flow reads, and proposals through the existing approval cards. No hosted web search or Code interpreter. xAI API Chat, permitted Flow reads, and proposals through the existing approval cards. No hosted web search or Code interpreter. Reads attached documents such as PDFs. Desktop app only. For brains with Flow tools, Off / Read / Propose sets the limit on what they can access through FlowJoe. Choosing a stronger brain does not unlock private content. Whichever brain you choose, Joe’s own changes always come to you as a card to approve; Agent Bridge’s Apply changes without asking setting only affects outside assistants. Guest Joe has separate invitation-based approval rules. See Permissions & privacy. Claude, Grok, Codex and Antigravity (on a Mac) use the same supported Flow actions as OpenAI. They connect to those actions through MCP, the connection format used

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Which brains can work with your Flow?
content: used by compatible AI tools. FlowJoe sets up this temporary connection for Joe automatically; you do not need to enable an outside assistant under Agent Bridge first. The Web search switch also applies to CLI brains; their available search tools depend on the selected provider. Web search is not available with Antigravity yet, so the switch is greyed out while Antigravity is Joe’s brain. FlowJoe’s hosted Code interpreter is an OpenAI feature, separate from running commands in a terminal. On launch, Web search starts on and Code interpreter starts off. Choosing Codex as Joe’s brain is separate from connecting those tools as outside assistants through Agent Bridge; you don’t need one for the other.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: A CLI brain, Agent Bridge, or Forge?
content: These three features fit together without being the same thing: BYOB chooses who answers as Joe inside FlowJoe. Agent Bridge lets an outside assistant work with the active Flow, using its own connection and approval controls. Forge is FlowJoe’s integrated terminal, where you run commands or an interactive assistant yourself. Joe’s chat history belongs to FlowJoe. Choosing a CLI brain does not resume a terminal conversation you already have open in Forge. Stop cancels the current CLI request; it does not undo changes already applied. Asking Joe to undo his last change works across the whole conversation on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok, Codex and, on a Mac, Antigravity). If a turn fails, FlowJoe shows the actual error or explains that the conversation is too large for that brain. FlowJoe’s access settings control its Flow tools. They are not a general restriction on everything an owner’s installed command-line tool can do on the computer; that tool has its own permissions and configuration.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: What happens with no key and no CLI brain
content: Chat and AI writing need a supported brain. Image generation separately needs an OpenAI API key, even when your chat uses Gemini or a command-line brain. Free local transcription does not need an AI key. Everything else works normally without any key — your tree, galleries, notes, documents, workspaces, and import/export are entirely local and never need an AI provider.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: Settings → APIs lists your keys in two groups (drag a row by its handle to reorder it within its group): Your AI accounts: OpenAI API Key, Anthropic API Key, Gemini API Key and xAI API Key. Extra services: TypeSafe API Key. Under each name, a short line shows where that key stands: A green dot and Key saved, with the start and end of the key (for example sk-proj…Q7f2), so you can tell which key it is without revealing it. An empty dot and No key yet. A red dot and Key rejected at last check, when the last Test of the saved key failed. Saving a different key or removing it clears the red line. Before you have saved any AI key, a sentence at the top explains what keys are for, and that supported terminal logins work without one.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Viewing, copying and removing a key
content: Open Settings → APIs and click the button beside the key’s name (for example OpenAI API Key). By default, the key is hidden behind a password mask (••••••••). Click the Eye icon (Show key) to reveal the plaintext key, so you can verify it or copy it. To remove the key, click the trash icon (Remove key) beside the eye. FlowJoe asks first; Cancel is on the right and already selected, so pressing Enter keeps the key. The trash icon is dimmed while there is no saved key. In the OpenAI key window, saves and removals finish in the order you request them. If you edit the key or reopen its window while an earlier change is finishing, that change will not close the newer window or erase your entry. Closing the window does not undo a storage write already underway. If storage reports a failure, the window stays open so you can try again.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Making Joe faster: the optional TypeSafe key
content: Before Joe answers, he first works out what he needs to look at — whether you are asking him to change something, whether he needs the shape of your flow, which part of the manual is relevant. Its wait depends on the selected brain; a command-line helper also has to start its tool. Add a TypeSafe API key and that decision runs on a model built purely for fast structured judgments, taking roughly a fifth of a second instead — on every message, whichever brain you are using. The difference is largest on the CLI brains (Claude, Grok, Antigravity, Codex). When TypeSafe answers, Joe avoids starting a second copy of the command-line tool just to pick the manual chapters. If TypeSafe cannot answer or is unsure, the selected brain’s own helper tries within the time left; it never switches to another company’s model. See the chapter picker and its waits. It is entirely optional. Without a key, everything works exactly as it does today — including the flow map, which is then never trimmed (see below). If the key is missing, wrong, expired, or the service is unreachable, FlowJoe quietly falls back to the normal path. Nothing breaks — Joe is simply not faster, and the map is not trimmed. It is stored as securely as your OpenAI key, and it is a separate key: adding or removing one never affects the other. It is desktop only. The Test button explains when TypeSafe is unavailable rather than reporting a network error. To set it up, get a key from console.typesafe.ai, open Settings → APIs, click the button next to TypeSafe API Key, paste the key, press Test, then Save. TypeSafe is a separate online service. When enabled, it receives relevant message text, node names (each with the name of the node it sits under) and summaries, file text, Joe’s replies, and — when Joe searches your pictures — small previews of them, for the routing, picture search and checks it performs. See what TypeSafe checks and receives. Use TypeSafe turns it off without deleting your key. Double-check Joe’s

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: Making Joe faster: the optional TypeSafe key
content: Joe’s work turns the three trust checks on or off. Context selection and map ranking stay available while TypeSafe is on.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
header: It also trims a big flow map
content: With a TypeSafe key, the same model does a second job: when you send Joe your whole flow, it picks out the parts relevant to what you just asked. This only applies when you have unticked both map options in the chat box — “Omit entire flow map” and “Limit map to my location”. That is the case where Joe sees your entire tree on every message, which on a large flow is most of what you are sending him. On a 274-node flow, one such question kept 41 nodes — the right branch and its parents — and left out the rest. Nothing is hidden from Joe. The map tells him it has been trimmed, how many of your nodes it is showing, and that anything not listed still exists. He can pull the full tree whenever he needs it, and is told to do that before ever saying something of yours does not exist. Questions about the whole flow skip it. “How many nodes do I have?”, “what am I neglecting?”, “do I have anything about X?” — these cannot be answered from a subset, so they get everything. Any problem sends the whole map. A slow answer, a garbled one, an answer that only covers some of your nodes, or a flow you edited while it was thinking — all of them fall back to the full tree. It never quietly sends Joe less. Small flows are left alone (under 60 nodes), and so are flows you have already narrowed with “Limit map to my location” — that is your choice of branch, not something to second-guess.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: The key panels have a Test button. Press it and FlowJoe makes one tiny real request to that provider and tells you immediately whether the key was accepted. Worth doing whenever you paste a new key — otherwise a mistyped or expired one looks fine until the next time you actually ask Joe something. In the OpenAI key window, editing or removing the key, or closing the window, ends a pending test. Its old result cannot validate a new entry. Press Test again after changing the key; only Save stores it. The same OpenAI Test can also collect announced shutdown dates for seven older image and online-transcription models. With Flow tools at Read or Propose, ask Joe which of those models have an announced retirement. The details are dated observations from the last completed manual Test, kept for this app session; they may come from an earlier key. Account access and future availability need separate checks. Missing retirement details leave Joe without that information and do not reject an otherwise accepted key. Test refreshes the observation, and removing the key clears it. Earlier replies keep their normal conversation history. Ordinary chat sends do not make another model-list request.

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: A guest’s Joe can use shared Flow tools and web tools, but cannot use the CLI to read your computer’s unrelated files, run commands, or reach your other installed integrations. FlowJoe checks the installed CLI version before sending the guest’s request. An unsupported version or a brain unavailable to guests stops that request; FlowJoe does not silently choose another provider. For the selectable CLI brains, supported guest release families are Claude 2.1.302 or later within 2.1, Grok 1.0.52 or later within 1.0, Codex 0.162.1 or later within 0.162 and 0.163.0 or later within 0.163. When a tool updates to a newer family, guests see a message that Joe can’t use that brain in the shared conversation right now, until FlowJoe checks the new version; your own use is unaffected. Antigravity is not available to guests. Grok uses a temporary connection for each Joe request. Guests can ask Joe to read shared content and propose changes for approval without approving a folder in Grok first. Their requests do not load your Grok, Claude Code, Cursor or Codex integrations, hooks, skills or instructions, or skills you keep in your home folder’s .agents folder. When you use Grok yourself, Joe uses your Grok sign-in and the models you set up, but none of your other Grok settings, tools or integrations. Like Claude, Joe on Grok can use only FlowJoe’s Flow tools and, when Web search is on, web search. It cannot run commands, read or change files on your computer, or use your other connected tools. Joe uses the Flow access you selected for that request; choosing chat-only keeps Flow tools off even if you have also connected Grok through Agent Bridge. FlowJoe does not add temporary folders to Grok’s saved trusted folders. Codex works the same way, for you and for guests. Joe uses your sign-in, but none of that tool’s other settings: not its instructions files (such as Codex’s AGENTS.md), skills, plugins, extensions, hooks, memories or other connected tools, and not skills kept in your

title: Bring Your Own Brain (BYOB)
content: your home folder’s .agents folder. Joe can use only FlowJoe’s Flow tools at the access you chose and, when Web search is on, web search. For pictures and PDF page images, FlowJoe gives him read-only access to a private temporary image folder and deletes it after the reply finishes or stops. He cannot run commands, change files, or read unrelated files on your computer. If Codex refreshes your ChatGPT sign-in during a request, FlowJoe saves the refreshed sign-in back once the request ends, so you stay signed in. When you use Antigravity on a Mac, Joe uses your Antigravity sign-in, but none of your other Antigravity settings, tools, plugins or integrations, including a FlowJoe connection you added through Agent Bridge. As on Claude and Grok, Joe can use only FlowJoe’s Flow tools; Web search is not available with Antigravity yet. For pictures and PDF page images, FlowJoe gives him read-only access to a private temporary image folder and deletes it after the reply finishes or stops. He cannot run commands, change files, or read unrelated files on your computer. Joe uses the Flow access you selected for that request, and choosing chat-only keeps Flow tools off. The picker checks your Antigravity sign-in with Google before showing Antigravity as ready. On Windows and Linux, if you have connected Antigravity to FlowJoe under Agent Bridge, Joe will not use Antigravity as his brain: that connection would let him reach your Flow outside the access you chose for the chat. Disconnect Antigravity under Settings → Joe AI → Agent Bridge (MCP), or pick another brain.

title: Permissions & privacy
content: Choose what Joe can read and which changes he can propose. Joe can help at the level you choose—from a conversation about an idea to a reviewed reorganization of your Flow.

title: Permissions & privacy
content: Set the default in Settings → Joe AI. The selector in Chat overrides that default for the current conversation. Starting a new conversation clears the override. Level What Joe can do Off Chat and explain FlowJoe, without automatic access to your Flow or tools to read or change it. Read Read permitted Flow content to answer questions, without changing it. Propose Read permitted content and offer changes for you to review. These permissions apply to OpenAI, Gemini API and supported command-line brains. A brain may offer fewer features: on Windows and Linux, Antigravity does not support callable Flow tools or changes. These settings govern access through FlowJoe; installed command-line tools have their own computer-access permissions.

title: Permissions & privacy
header: Keep content out of Joe’s reach
content: Private nodes: Their summaries, notes, gallery content, and descendants stay out of Joe’s Flow access, even while you unlock them for your own use. Hidden from Joe: Keeps a node’s contents and its descendants’ contents out of Joe’s access while leaving them available to you. Names and contents are separate: Joe can still see a sealed node’s name and position in the Flow map. This lets him understand where it belongs and refer to it in conversation without opening or changing its contents. Keep sensitive details out of node names. These controls govern content Joe receives from the Flow. They cannot remove text you already pasted into a conversation or sent earlier.

title: Permissions & privacy
content: With OpenAI API chat at Read or Propose, you can ask about the current storage mode, save blocks, export changes, pending conflict review, selected/responding model, Joe permissions, or a small performance sample. Joe reads only the requested facts. Unavailable measurements are marked as unavailable; an export-changes indicator does not prove that a local save failed or succeeded. No keys, local paths or diagnostic logs are included. After a manual OpenAI key Test, model facts can also include dated shutdown metadata for seven older image and online-transcription choices. These session-only observations may be unavailable or come from an earlier key; they do not establish your current account’s access or guarantee a model’s lifetime. Guests do not receive the owner’s observation. In a browser guest session, this reader can describe only the already available session model and permissions. Owner storage, save, conflict and computer diagnostics remain unavailable. New guest schedule inspection through Joe and transport parity are separate pending work; the existing shared Tasks lists are unchanged.

title: Permissions & privacy
content: The wrench beside the prompt opens extra-context options, including web search, code interpreter and Flow-map choices. Its badge counts selected options, not Joe’s full tool set. The Off / Read / Propose selector sets Joe’s access to your Flow; the wrench does not replace that permission choice. Review the context choices for your next send. Map-size controls do not replace privacy controls. Use Add extra context to choose gallery items for your next message. The target controls choose the Flow, node, or slot you are discussing. The token bar estimates how much context the send includes. Limit map to my location narrows the outline. Omit entire flow map leaves the outline off that send. These are focus and cost controls; use Private or Hidden from Joe to seal content. See Choosing Joe’s target, Token usage, and Security & privacy.

title: Permissions & privacy
content: A slot’s or stack item’s Hide from Joe choice also keeps its notes out of spelling checks. Checking an item’s visible notes never sends or changes the slot’s hidden notes. Accepting a correction changes the exact notes you checked, even if you have since changed the stack’s top item or opened another node. Choosing a new Joe target starts the next check there. A virtual slot follows its master’s privacy choices. A guest’s Joe can read an outside master’s content when the guest is shown it, without learning where that master lives; anything hidden from Joe stays hidden from every Joe. Unlocking a Private area for yourself still gives Joe no access.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Ask questions, analyze spreadsheets, generate graphics, and dictate notes. Joe is capable of complex research, text reviews, and creative drafting. Here is how you use his core capabilities. This page is about chatting with Joe (the robot). To talk with the people in a shared Flow, use Chat (the speech bubbles). Long chats can continue by looking up older messages as needed. You can choose summary compaction instead in Settings → Joe AI; manual Compact Older Turns, Joe Memories and saved attachment descriptions remain available. See Context & Memories. Each send includes more than the prompt you typed. To see the cost and to shrink the tree outline Joe is given, use the token bar and the Limit map to my location / Omit entire flow map checkboxes above the message box. See Token usage with Joe. Chat, Spelling, Transcribe and Images share the target controls below their tabs. Use the crosshair for Flow Chat, or right-click a node inside Joe’s target tree to choose Flow, Node or Slot. Choosing a slot in a tool keeps that tab and carries the choice into Chat. See Choosing Joe’s target for the slot list, Last used badge and draft behavior. Choose the context that helps Joe answer the question; do not send unrelated material.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
header: Add a requirement while Joe is replying
content: In your own private OpenAI API chat, keep typing in the prompt while Joe works. Press Enter to send a text update for that reply; Shift+Enter adds a new line. In docked Joe you can also use the Send update arrow beside Stop. For example: “Only change the selected branch” or “Keep the original names.” The update shows Sending update… or Queued for this reply while it waits to be included, then Added to this reply when inclusion is confirmed. On supported GPT-6 API connections in the desktop app, the new direction can reach Joe before the current reply finishes. Some updates wait for the next safe continuation, especially when Joe is working from files he has read. Joe may finish an already-started step before taking the new direction. An earlier proposal that has not started applying is replaced; completed changes are kept. Only one update can wait at a time. The continued reply uses your selected brain and can incur normal provider charges; the receipt includes both the original response and its continuation. If delivery fails or is uncertain, Restore update to prompt puts the text back beside anything you have typed since. Check the conversation before resending an unconfirmed update; FlowJoe does not resend it automatically. Stop remains available. If the update hint is unavailable, keep your draft until Joe finishes or use Stop. This interaction is currently available for private OpenAI API chat, not CLI brains, other providers, shared conversations or guest chat. Changing the brain or API key during preparation makes updates unavailable for that reply.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Use Regenerate on Joe’s latest reply to ask again with that earlier message and its saved references. The text and available attachment or context choices you are preparing for your next message stay in the prompt area, including choices changed while Joe replies. Regenerate does not add those unsent choices to the earlier request. References already included in the conversation keep their usual sent status. Unavailable references or context cannot remain selected. It uses your current selected brain and can incur normal provider charges.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: In owner chat and authorized external CLI/MCP sessions, Read or Propose permission lets Joe look up permitted history in the current Flow: earlier conversations, generated-image prompts and model details, retained transcripts, and dates/revisions of verified public changes. Try “Find the chat where we chose the launch name” or “Which image prompt did I use yesterday?” He reads longer results in portions and gives their source dates and conversation/message references. The current chat stays open. Locked Private sources and Hidden from Joe sources are excluded, as are deleted or uncertain owners and unavailable older copies. After you unlock a Private node, Joe can use it through the normal context, attachment and approved-action controls. Use Hidden from Joe separately if you want to work on the node without giving Joe access. Computer-only history stays local to its owner. Results can be partial, so an empty search does not prove something never existed. Image lookup returns prompt/details without fetching the picture, and requires every recorded source and reference picture to remain available to Joe; version lookup does not restore anything. Authorized external CLI/MCP connections receive these history readers with Read or Propose access. Guests and scheduled runs do not receive them. See the action reference.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Joe can read files attached to your gallery slots: PDF & Office Analysis: Ask Joe to summarize text, translate pages, or look up terms. Spreadsheets: Joe evaluates sheet rows and columns to compile budgets or highlight averages. Images: Joe inspects images (JPG, PNG) to describe layouts, extract text, or check designs. Large documents, spreadsheets and calendars are read in sections. Name the heading, sheet and cell range, or dates you need. When Joe reads a PDF from your gallery, he knows which page each passage is on, so you can ask about a specific page (“what does page 12 say?”) and he can point you to the page where he found something. For a full review, ask Joe to continue through the remaining available sections and say what, if anything, was left unread. A text summary covers the text FlowJoe could extract; it does not establish that every page, diagram or embedded image was examined. File-conversion limits are separate from reading the available text. Joe is also told when a PDF page has no readable text, such as a page that is only a chart, photo or scan. In chat he can then look at that page as a picture, so “what does the chart on page 7 show?” gets a real answer. The first time he wants to look at pages of a PDF, Joe asks you, because each page sent as a picture uses noticeably more of your AI usage than reading text; he looks at a few pages at a time, only the ones he needs. If you say no, he answers from the text and tells you the visuals were not read. In a browser, PDF text extraction reads at most the first 100 pages, and Joe is told which pages were left out. For visual details, give Joe the relevant image or screenshot as well.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: With your own OpenAI API key and Luna 6, Joe can combine several permitted saved repository text files into a compact comparison. Name the files and the facts you want compared. Joe uses source paths and supporting excerpts to ground the comparison and identifies any file read only in part. This can reduce AI token usage for larger comparisons, although it may take longer than ordinary reads. Each file read covers at most 12,000 characters, and one reply can coordinate up to eight distinct saved files. For a complete review of a longer file, ask Joe to continue through its remaining sections using ordinary reads. Existing Flow permissions still apply; the admitted text is processed by OpenAI. Single-file questions, open drafts and historical versions use ordinary reads.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Joe’s Images tab gives you a small creative studio beside your references: describe a picture, use an existing image as a guide, and keep useful results together as a stack. It needs an OpenAI API key, regardless of your chat brain. Shared guests use the owner’s enabled image connection. Choose an image model, quality, size, and output format before generating. Background choices depend on the model and format. Use the reference-image control to select an accessible image and enable it for the request. In the Images tab, the compact Auto, New and Edit pills choose how the next request uses the preview: Auto continues the saved image thread when one exists, or starts a new generation. New clears the saved preview and thread and starts fresh. It keeps starting fresh until you choose another mode. Edit edits the image in the preview when a saved thread exists; otherwise it starts a fresh request. Edit can be unavailable when the selected model cannot continue a saved image response. You can generate graphics directly in your workspace: Prompting: Ask Joe “Generate a logo for my coffee shop in sepia style.” Reference Images: Attach an existing gallery image as a reference to steer Joe’s generation style or layout. Write-back Options: Generated images render inside a chat card. You can click Send to Gallery to save it as a new slot, insert it into a stack, or replace an existing image. If generation fails: Your previous generated picture and its prompt remain available. A failed replacement request does not clear that draft. The new request stays in the prompt box so you can retry it. Stop: If you stop while the image response is arriving, that late response is not accepted as the finished replacement. Images request timeout: In the Images tab, an image request that has not finished after three minutes stops with a timeout message. Your previous picture stays available, and you can try again. Pressing Stop still shows the normal stopped message. Survives a restart: A

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: A generated image you haven’t sent to the gallery yet still shows, and can still be sent or reused, after you close and reopen FlowJoe. If a generated image genuinely can’t be recovered, the card says so with a plain note instead of showing a blank frame. Conversations saved with a Private node, their archived sessions and compacted memory are saved encrypted with the node, including older conversations saved before you made it Private. They stay available through the normal history controls, and moving a slot or undoing the move keeps its conversations and late replies. A Private node’s unfinished generated picture, prompts and image history are also kept under the same node password, including older picture-generation history belonging to the node. Other nodes’ history and independent public pictures keep their normal rules. Removing protection keeps the generated draft and image history usable normally. Relocking hides those working pictures and prompts; unlocking restores the saved draft.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Open image-generation history from Images. Change Current node to All if necessary, find a picture, and open it to restore its preview, prompt, and saved generation choices. Choose Auto or Edit to continue where supported, or New for a fresh picture. You can send a result to the gallery as a new slot, add it to a stack, or replace an item. The restored picture, its prompt and its saved details stay together when you reopen Joe. If the picture itself is missing, Joe restores its available prompt history and keeps the missing-picture warning. Pictures made in a chat keep that chat generation’s own prompt history; an unrelated draft in Images is kept separate. This drawer can find older pictures kept on this computer even when their original node is no longer in the current Flow. History → Images is narrower: it lists pictures whose source node is still in this Flow. Guest history always stays within the guest’s shared access.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Images made through a shared Joe conversation or the Images tab are kept with the owner’s Flow, including their image bytes and history entry. The existing image-history drawer shows results whose source is shared with you; reopening or reloading the guest app reads that owner-kept history. View access can inspect shared history and use the Joe conversation features the owner enabled. Changing shared gallery content and saving a history result into the gallery require Edit access. Saving someone else’s shared result does not change who created it. Removing an image-history entry does not remove a picture still used in shared chat or the gallery; that picture continues to follow its source’s privacy and sharing permissions. Private sources and hidden stack items are excluded. A public stack item stays available even when a sibling is private. If the source becomes private or access ends while a new history entry is being saved, that entry is refused. Older entries whose source cannot be established reliably are withheld rather than attached to a different item.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
header: A node’s look, and changes in the gallery
content: You can ask Joe to change the workspace itself. Each of these still waits on an approval card: Give a node one of the Theme-menu looks by its menu name. He is shown the real list. A made-up name is refused. Clearing the look lets the node inherit again. Copy a slot, or one item out of a stack, and leave the original where it is. Crop a picture in its slot. The picture stays in that slot, so any lines on the canvas board stay with it. Turn a picture or a note into a PDF and place that PDF beside the original. Set, replace, or remove the album art on an audio item, using a picture already saved in FlowJoe. On a linked audio file the cover stays on this machine and does not change the file. Color a slot on the canvas board red, green, blue, violet, pink, or cyan, or clear that color. Move a canvas card, change its width, or restore its usual width. Draw or remove a line between two slots on the same board. You can ask Joe to control the header player right away, with no approval card. For example: “Play some music” starts the current queue, or the first accessible saved playlist if the queue is empty. “Shuffle the queue” or “loop this track” changes playback mode. Sequential mode plays in order and repeats the queue; repeat-one loops the current track. “Play the audio in the Opening node once” plays one chosen gallery audio file and stops when it ends. If there is more than one file in the slot or stack, tell Joe which one. “Play something tagged calm” works when audio slots have a matching user tag. Joe can use visible tag names and descriptions to match a vibe; he does not infer moods from filenames or node names. “Save this queue as Focus Mix” creates a named playlist. To save audio carrying a tag without starting playback or changing the current queue, ask “Make a playlist called Quiet Work from audio tagged calm.” Joe will not overwrite an existing playlist. Joe can load a saved playlist by its exact name, pause playback, show the player, or hide it (which stops

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
header: A node’s look, and changes in the gallery
content: stops playback). A locked private or hidden-from-Joe node is not available to him.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: For text drafts: Diff Presentation: Selecting a text box and running Spell & Grammar opens a review modal showing a side-by-side green/red diff of corrections. My Tweaks: You can write edits before applying. Accept/Cancel: Click Accept to write corrections directly into the source note, document, or summary with full undo-history support.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Turn recordings into text in Joe’s Transcribe tab. Choose free local Whisper for offline processing on your computer, or your paid OpenAI API account. FlowJoe discovers compatible installed models, walks you through optional downloads, and remembers your choices. Local output can be plain text or timestamped segments; speaker labels remain an online option. See Transcribe audio for setup, model sizes and the complete walkthrough.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: In a private desktop conversation, open the arrow beside the microphone and choose Talk with Joe…, then Start voice. An OpenAI API key and a supported Joe voice from Settings → AI → Joe voice are required. The microphone starts only after you choose Start voice. Choose a voice in Settings → AI → Joe voice. Additional Live voices show their language and, where applicable, regional accent. Choosing one or pressing its speaker button plays a short billed sample without using your microphone; press again to stop. Live-only voices work in Talk with Joe; Mini and Full choices also support ordinary read-aloud. A changed choice applies to the next voice conversation. Speak naturally. Your selected chat brain still handles requests and tools, with the conversation’s usual permissions and approval cards. Check the chat and review proposed changes before applying them. Spoken replies alone do not confirm that a change was applied. Mute microphone stops Joe from hearing you while the conversation stays open. Quiet Joe silences his voice; Let Joe speak turns it back on. This is separate from muting your microphone. End voice finishes the voice conversation. If Joe is still working, choose whether that work continues in chat or stops. Hiding or minimizing Joe, or leaving the Chat tab, ends voice. Work Joe has already started continues in that conversation. Choosing New Chat, restoring a different conversation, or choosing another node or slot ends voice and stops its unfinished work. Joe saves the spoken transcript before switching. If saving fails, the original conversation stays open for recovery. Replacing the Flow or switching between Local and Workspace storage also ends voice. Joe saves before the switch and waits until it finishes before another voice conversation can start. Live voice costs $0.05 per minute, plus your selected brain and tool usage. The voice display shows an estimate; missing final usage is marked unconfirmed. Live voice has no preset

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: preset conversation-duration or silence limit. It is separate from the Mini and Full prices for ordinary read-aloud. Your spoken transcript stays in the conversation. If it cannot be saved, keep the conversation open and use Try again. Starting another voice session waits until the save succeeds. If microphone access is denied, allow it in your system settings and try again. If the voice connection is lost, work Joe has already started continues in chat; use the usual Stop control to stop it. A lost connection does not undo changes already completed; check the chat before repeating a request. For speech you want to edit before sending, choose Dictate message instead. The microphone’s ordinary dictation behavior and spoken punctuation commands remain available.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: When voice dictation is active, you can use spoken commands to structure text: Say Output ”comma” , ”period” . ”new line” / “line break” Inserts a line break ”delete last word” Deletes the preceding word ”clear all” Clears the entire text field

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: Keep your conversation moving while Joe researches in the background. Joe stays your collaborator and brings the findings back to you. You can keep talking, change direction, or cancel the research without managing another agent yourself. With any brain (an OpenAI, Gemini, xAI or Anthropic API brain, or a terminal brain such as Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Antigravity), Joe can ask a read-only Researcher to examine selected gallery references when that helps your task. There is nothing extra to enable or approve: Joe can delegate focused comparisons across several references he has not read yet and brings the findings into his final answer. Routine questions, single-reference lookups, and answers already supported by your conversation stay with Joe. A compact Researcher card shows the task and where it belongs. Select Show assignment while it runs, or Show findings & references after completion, to inspect the details and available usage. You can keep chatting with Joe while research runs. Stop research appears only while that research is working and cancels that assignment; once findings are in there is nothing left to stop there, and stopping Joe’s reply keeps them. Stopping a different Joe reply leaves research running. If you stop Joe’s reply while he is presenting completed research, the findings stay available in the card. Changed references or access invalidate findings rather than keeping them as current evidence. When findings arrive during a reply, Joe finishes that reply before reviewing and presenting them. You can ask Joe for progress or to cancel and replace the assignment. The researcher cannot edit your Flow, run commands or access references Joe cannot read. Normal approvals still apply to changes Joe later proposes. The card’s details explain whether research was cancelled, timed out, lost access to its references, encountered an AI service error, returned a result that did not pass FlowJoe’s checks (so it was not used), or stopped because of an

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
content: an unexpected problem. An unavailable reference can prevent research from starting. Ask Joe to try again when you want a new attempt; failed or stopped replies do not restart themselves. Researchers work over selected gallery references in your own chat (or a guest’s shared chat) on an OpenAI, Gemini, xAI or Anthropic API brain, or a terminal brain, using that same brain and model. On a terminal brain the background work is more runs of the same terminal assistant on your existing login (no API key is needed or used), so it counts against that login’s usage, and the usage shown is approximate. Background work needs Flow access to be on (Read-Only or Propose), and on Antigravity it works on macOS. Terminal brains read pictures for background work where that assistant can accept them: Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity on a Mac. Antigravity reads those pictures and PDF-page images from the same private temporary image folder used for ordinary chat; FlowJoe deletes it after the run finishes or stops. Guests can use background work too when Joe is on for their invitation and the owner’s brain is an API brain or a terminal brain other than Antigravity: it stays within what the invitation lets Joe read, runs on the owner’s Joe brain and account (on a terminal brain, the owner’s own login), and shows no usage or cost to the guest. A guest on Antigravity keeps Joe’s existing behavior. If the owner changes the selected terminal brain or model before a background job or its combined answer starts, that work stops rather than sending its references or findings to the new brain. Research and Joe’s review are included in the review reply’s receipt (a guest sees no usage or cost, because the owner pays); delegation does not guarantee lower token use or cost.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
header: Get another perspective with the Reviewer
content: Joe can ask an independent Reviewer to examine a candidate idea, plan, proposed change, or supplied code. He chooses an approach suited to your question, and you can ask for one explicitly: Approach What it helps with Critique Weak assumptions, unclear reasoning, feasibility, and tradeoffs. Adversarial check Counterexamples and conditions under which a claim or plan fails. Security review Specific risks visible in the code and context you provide. Requirements check Whether the proposal meets each stated condition, with missing evidence kept unverified. Explore alternatives Other approaches, their advantages, tradeoffs, assumptions, and open questions. For example: “Have a Reviewer challenge this plan,” “Check the security of this supplied handler,” or “Explore other ways we could approach this.” Joe provides the candidate and criteria. The Reviewer receives a focused assignment and supplied material in a separate context; Joe considers the results and brings you his own answer. Routine questions can stay with Joe. You can use shared gallery references or a passage already in the conversation. The Reviewer card shows the assignment. Select Show assignment, Show findings & references, or Show alternatives & references to inspect the details. There is no approach menu or additional permission to manage. Keep talking to Joe while it runs, ask for progress, or use Stop review to cancel it. If you stop Joe’s returning explanation, completed results remain available while their material and access are still valid. A clean review means no supported issues were found within the supplied material. A security review looks at the code and context provided; it does not run the program or inspect unshared files. Exploration returns options rather than treating them as defects, and Joe should leave a choice open when important constraints are unknown. Reviews and suggested fixes do not apply changes or approve publication. The Reviewer works in your own chat (or a guest’s shared

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
header: Get another perspective with the Reviewer
content: shared chat) on an OpenAI, Gemini, xAI or Anthropic API brain, or a terminal brain (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, or Antigravity on macOS; for a guest, any of these except Antigravity), with Flow read access, using that same brain and model; on a terminal brain it runs on the assistant’s existing login and its usage is approximate. Guests can use it within their access, on the owner’s account, on the owner’s brain, including a terminal brain other than Antigravity. Reviewer work and Joe’s synthesis are included in the returning reply’s receipt, and the card shows available Reviewer token counts; a guest sees no usage or cost, because the owner pays. An extra perspective does not guarantee correctness, lower token use, or lower cost.

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
header: Background work: several jobs at once
content: For a request with independent parts, Joe can run up to three read-only jobs at the same time, in any mix of Researchers and Reviewers. They appear together as one Background work group in the chat, where the work started. The group header shows live counts (for example “2 working · 1 complete”) and Stop all when two or more jobs exist and one is still working. Each job is a compact row with its task, Researcher or Reviewer, its status, and Stop research / Stop review only while that job is working. Use Show assignment or Show findings & references on a row to open its details, and Show combined usage at the bottom for the recorded usage of Joe and the specialist work, including available usage from failed, stopped or replaced jobs. Missing final counts remain marked pending. While any job is unfinished, or its results are waiting for Joe’s answer, a one-line progress strip sits just above the message box: “Background work · 2 working · 1 complete”, with Show and Stop all (Stop when there is only one job). Click Show, or anywhere on the strip, to scroll to the group and move focus to it. Stop all stops only jobs that are still working and keeps completed findings. If results arrive while Joe is busy with another reply, the strip says “Joe answers after his current reply”. It leaves once Joe’s combined answer is delivered or there is nothing left to deliver. You can keep chatting the whole time. When every job has finished, Joe gives one combined answer. If a job was stopped or could not finish, he says what was not checked and uses only the completed evidence; nothing is retried automatically. New related work you ask for while the group is open joins it and counts toward the three. Once Joe starts the combined answer, the group is closed and later work starts a new group. If you ask for more jobs than there is room for, Joe starts as many as fit, up to three at once, and says plainly which were not started. If you ask for a fourth job while three are running or

title: Chat, Analysis & Dictation
header: Background work: several jobs at once
content: or waiting, Joe tells you plainly that three is the most at once, that nothing was queued, and offers to wait or to stop one. If you change one request, Joe cancels and replaces only that job. Stopping Joe’s combined reply keeps all completed findings. Jobs that were still working when you closed or reloaded the app show as interrupted and do not resume. Background jobs finish on the brain and model that started them; if you switch brains or models while some are still working or waiting, Joe offers to wait for them or stop them before starting new ones. When you use an input method to compose text in Chat or an image prompt, Enter confirms your text without sending it or starting image generation. Once composition finishes, Enter and the usual line-break shortcuts work as before.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Turn a recording into text for free on your computer, or use your paid OpenAI API account. Turn interviews, voice notes and other recordings into editable text by asking Joe in Chat or using the Transcribe tab. You can use free transcription on your computer or the paid online service. The local transcription engine does not need an API key; chatting with Joe uses your selected brain as usual. Choose the processing route before starting. Review the resulting transcript for errors.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Keep the audio file in a gallery slot or stack, then ask “Can you transcribe this recording?” You can also name a recording in another accessible node. Joe uses your saved method, model, language and local output format. Your request starts the run without another approval. Joe starts a background job and becomes available for your next message. A compact card above the message box shows progress and elapsed time. A moving highlight means the job is active but has no measured percentage yet; a solid fill shows measured progress. With reduced motion enabled, the activity highlight stays still. Use Stop transcription on that card to cancel only the recording job; Chat’s usual Stop controls the current reply. Closing Joe’s panel does not stop transcription, but FlowJoe must stay open. Jobs do not resume after app restart. If the recording is unclear, choose the recording Joe offers. If local transcription needs setup, open the setup link, select or install a model in Transcribe, then ask again. Joe never switches from local to paid online transcription automatically. You can ask “How is the transcription going?” while discussing something else. Local jobs show approximate time remaining after enough recognition progress is available; until then, or when the engine provides no reliable progress, the card says Estimating time remaining…. Joe does not spend model calls polling. Completion arrives as an event; a chat notice waits until any active reply finishes and belongs only to the conversation that started the job. The full result is kept in Recent transcripts. Completion still shows the opening lines of the transcript, plus Open and Copy. Use Open beneath the result to edit that exact transcript in Transcribe, or Copy to copy the text. Joe can discuss the result afterward. A gallery copy is a separate save. Starting transcription from Chat requires the owner’s Propose & modify Flow access. Guest transcription remains available through the existing Transcribe tab.

title: Transcribe audio
content: The shared action transcribe_audio accepts the source nodeId and recording’s stable entryId from the Flow snapshot. A stack recording uses its own entry ID. Joe’s API brains, supported CLI brains and authenticated external Agent Bridge clients can use it with Propose access. External API/CLI/MCP calls keep their existing waiting behavior and retain results without opening or changing Chat. Native API Chat and native CLI brains start detached jobs by default. The same tool accepts action: "status" with the returned jobId (omit it for the latest job), or action: "cancel" with an exact job ID. Status includes state, measured progress and nullable remainingMs; only completed results report saved and a record ID. Background controls are native Chat only; an external session cannot inspect or cancel native Chat jobs. It is not offered to scheduled runs. For the standalone CLI, put the IDs in input.json: {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","entryId":"YOUR_AUDIO_ENTRY_ID"} flowjoe-cli action transcribe_audio --file input.json --wait 3600 --json Agent Bridge must be enabled and FlowJoe must remain open. Choose a wait long enough for your recording and computer; Ctrl+C cancels. Multiple external matches return choose_audio and IDs to resolve with the user. The result includes recordId, saved, text and truncated. The returned text is limited to 12,000 characters; the retained transcript is complete. For more, use query_history with kind: "transcript", then read_history with the returned revision and continuation. See the CLI action reference.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Method Cost Where the recording is processed Internet Whisper · Free on this computer No usage fees; uses your computer’s processing power On your computer Needed for the first model download, then works offline OpenAI · Paid online Charged to your OpenAI API account Audio is uploaded to OpenAI Required Free local transcription is available in the desktop app. Browser and shared guest sessions keep their existing online transcription route. A ChatGPT subscription does not supply OpenAI API credit. For a recording in a Private node, unlock the node before starting. Choosing online transcription sends the recording to your chosen provider in the usual way; Private status does not add another consent step. Locking the source or switching away from its Flow stops unfinished work from being added to that node. A Private node’s recordings and transcripts are saved encrypted; see Security & privacy. Your method, local model and local output format are remembered on this computer. Switching methods keeps your paid model choice. FlowJoe does not switch to a paid service if a local run fails.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Open Joe and choose Transcribe. Keep your audio recording in a gallery slot or stack in the selected node. Choose Set up Whisper, or Manage local models if models are already available. FlowJoe checks for compatible models already on your computer. Ready on this computer means no download is needed. Choose a model, read its size and description, then click Use. If you need a model, choose one under Download once and click its Download button. A model is the file that recognizes speech. FlowJoe handles downloading and checking it; you do not need a terminal or a separate software installer. Wait for the model to become ready, then click Use. Downloading alone does not change your transcription method or saved model. You can cancel a download and try again. Back returns to Transcribe without changing your saved method/model. Your selected recording and existing transcript stay in place.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Small is a balanced starting point. Choose Base for a smaller download; consider Medium, Large v3 or Turbo for difficult speech if your computer has enough memory. Speed varies with your computer and recording. Download Approximate file size What to consider Base 148 MB Smaller download and faster processing for clear recordings Small 488 MB Balanced speed and accuracy Medium 1.53 GB More memory; can help with difficult recordings Large v3 3.10 GB Highest download size and memory use among these choices Turbo · Compressed 575 MB Compact version of a larger model; speed depends on your computer All these download choices support multiple languages. An installed model labeled English only is for English recordings. Existing compatible models can include Tiny or other English-only variants. Their actual file sizes appear in the chooser and may differ from the download table because their file format differs. The size is disk space for the model file, not the amount of memory needed while it runs. Models are downloaded separately; choosing a large model does not make everyone else’s FlowJoe installer larger.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Choose a node or slot in Joe’s target bar, then select the recording in Source. The visible Source heading also names this selector for assistive technology. A node shows recordings grouped by slot, including the audio items in each stack. Choosing a recording targets its slot. A slot target shows only recordings in that slot; selecting the node again returns to all its slots. Choose your Transcription method. For local transcription, choose an installed Local model. Under Options, choose Plain text, Whisper - Timestamps or Speaker Labels + Timestamps. For online transcription, the original Model menu offers the paid choices. Leave Language on Auto, or choose English when appropriate. Click Transcribe. The button changes to Stop, with a working indicator. The status shows the current stage and elapsed time; a percentage appears only when the engine supplies one. Click Stop to cancel. While stopping, wait for the recording to be released. Your previous transcript and edits return after cancellation. Review or edit the result. Copy copies the text. Save opens the destination chooser so you can put the transcript in gallery notes or a summary. The history marks it saved only after the destination is saved successfully. Changing Options affects your next transcription. It does not rewrite text already in the transcript box. Online transcription saves a result only after the service confirms it is complete. If the connection ends early or stops sending data for 90 seconds, the run fails rather than saving a partial transcript as finished. You can retry the recording. Stop also works while the online result is arriving.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Completed transcripts and your edits are kept automatically for the current Flow, even before you save a gallery copy. Returning to Transcribe after a reload restores the latest transcript. Open Recent transcripts to reopen an earlier result, remove one, or clear the history. Removing history does not delete the recording or a copy you saved in the gallery. Clear removes the transcripts currently available in the list, including available results marked Keep on this computer only. It does not remove records inside locked Private nodes. Unlock the node first to remove those results. Retained transcripts and edits of a Private node are saved encrypted under the same node password, including older transcripts saved before you made the node Private. Saved text, older versions and normal Recent access stay available after unlocking. This does not change the choice between local and paid-online transcription. The transcription method controls where speech recognition runs. Storage follows the Flow’s storage mode: Local mode, including a standalone browser: transcript history is kept in this browser or app’s local data, separately for each Flow. Clearing browser/app data removes that local copy; use an export for a backup. Workspace folder: eligible history is also kept in the Workspace’s .flowjoe/transcript-history.json file and restored when that Workspace opens. Private-source transcripts and transcripts marked Keep on this computer only stay in local data instead. Transcript history is registered app data and is excluded from orphaned-media cleanup. Private transcripts become unavailable when their source is locked. A transcript whose source was removed remains available in history for copying or saving, subject to its privacy restrictions. In owner chat and authorized external CLI/MCP sessions, you can ask Joe to find or quote a retained transcript in the current Flow. He reads bounded text portions with source dates only when the recording still has an admitted

title: Transcribe audio
content: admitted public source. Private, Hidden from Joe, removed and uncertain sources stay unavailable to this reader, even if you can still copy them in the human history. A recording converted into a stack or moved to another public node keeps its retained source link. Ambiguous or newly private sources are withheld. Reading does not upload the audio or start recognition. Joe reads a bounded portion of history already loaded with the Flow; unusually large or unavailable retained collections can be unavailable to this reader while ordinary History remains readable. Results may be partial; guests and scheduled runs do not receive these readers. Authorized external CLI/MCP sessions can use them with Read or Propose access; see the action reference. Joe can also read a Private node’s own transcripts after you unlock their still-available recording source. Hidden from Joe and locked or uncertain sources remain unavailable. Exports have an Include transcript history option, enabled by default. Private-source transcripts start excluded; explicitly include their Private nodes to include eligible transcripts. An already-unlocked node does not require its password again. Computer-only transcripts remain excluded. See Export & Import. If FlowJoe can’t read the saved transcript history, the Flow still exports without it and a notice says so; the kept transcripts on your computer are left unchanged. If you open a Flow whose transcript history was saved by a newer FlowJoe, this version still shows it, but new transcripts and edits are not kept there; FlowJoe warns you and the text stays copyable. In a Workspace folder saved by a newer FlowJoe, new transcripts stay on this computer.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Open Recent transcripts in Transcribe to read the retained results shared with you. Private sources and transcripts the owner keeps on their computer are excluded. Removing a recording does not remove its retained text when its shared origin is known. Selecting a recording still restores its retained text after the owner merges it into a stack or reopens the Flow. Hiding the recording or moving it outside your share also withholds its retained words, even when other pictures in the same stack remain shared. View access: open and read shared retained results. When the owner enables Joe, transcribe shared audio into a personal result and edit it in your browser. This personal draft survives closing Joe or reloading the same browser tab; it does not change the owner’s history. Saving into shared content requires Edit access. Edit access: edit retained text and save a gallery copy through the existing Save chooser. Text edits are saved through the owner, with a pending recovery copy in your browser. Removal: Edit can remove its own results; removing someone else’s results or a separate conflict result they contributed requires the owner’s elevated removal permission. A mixed removal tells you what was kept. Ordinary text edits do not change who created the result. The owner keeps the authoritative history with the Flow. Ending or losing access to the share clears the guest browser’s shared data and pending drafts; it does not delete the owner’s history. Keep on this computer only is controlled by the owner. Reading existing results does not require permission to run Joe; new online recognition uses the owner’s enabled connection. Personal drafts are cleared when their audio is hidden or removed, the guest’s role changes, or the share ends. Local model setup remains a desktop function.

title: Transcribe audio
header: Plain text, timestamps and speaker labels
content: Plain text: readable recognized text without added time markers. Whisper - Timestamps: each segment includes a start time such as [01:24]. Speaker Labels + Timestamps: separates voices into numbered speakers, with a time marker on each line. Local transcription includes its speaker detector with FlowJoe: no account, token or extra download is needed. The ordinary Whisper speech model setup is still required. Speaker numbers distinguish voices; they do not identify people. Local plain text and timestamps use the same recognition model. Choose the model for speed and accuracy, and choose Options for how the transcript should look. All local model sizes have no per-use API fee.

title: Transcribe audio
header: Change, add or remove a model
content: Use Manage local models any time. Selecting a model to inspect it does not change your saved method/model; click Use to adopt it. Under More options, Locate an existing model… lets you select a compatible model file that FlowJoe did not find automatically. FlowJoe checks the file before offering it. An unrelated or modified model file may be refused. A model downloaded by FlowJoe can be removed from this screen after confirmation to free disk space. FlowJoe does not delete model files it found elsewhere on your computer. If a selected model is removed or moved, choose another ready model or download it again. New model choices may arrive with FlowJoe updates. You choose whether to download a bigger or different model; FlowJoe does not replace your selected model automatically. Transcripts keep following their original recording when you merge audio into a stack. Moving that stack into a Private node excludes its retained transcripts from exports by default. The owner can explicitly include eligible transcripts by selecting the Private node; an already-unlocked node does not require its password again, and unlocking alone does not include it. An Edit guest with export permission can include eligible retained transcripts; FlowJoe checks access again before saving the export.

title: Transcribe audio
header: Ask Joe about a YouTube video
content: Paste a YouTube link (or ask about a video you have open) and Joe can read what is said in it. If FlowJoe’s built-in browser was closed, it rises to just its tab row at the bottom of the window. A YouTube tab with a small Joe badge appears beside your own active tab; Joe’s status line says Reading the video’s captions…. A video Joe opens stays paused and muted the whole time. You can keep working while Joe reads. When Joe is done, his tab closes and the browser goes back to how it was: if it was closed, it slides away again; if you had tabs open, you stay on yours. If you expanded the browser meanwhile, it stays open. If the video is already open in one of your own tabs, Joe reads it there and leaves your tab as it is.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Open Joe chat, give Joe at least Read-only Flow access, and paste: Read the captions of https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc. Summarize Steve Jobs’ three stories, give a timestamp for each, and explain his main takeaway. You should briefly see Joe’s badged tab beside your own tab in the browser’s bottom tab row. It closes when the read finishes, and Joe answers in the chat with a summary and timestamps. If you already have that video open, Joe uses your tab and leaves it open without pausing or muting it. No local transcription model is needed for YouTube captions. Then, in the same conversation, try: Using that transcript, explain the connecting-the-dots section and give its timestamp. Joe reuses the transcript already read for that conversation, so this follow-up does not need to open the video again.

title: Transcribe audio
content: The whole transcript, however long. Joe reads the full captions — a three-hour podcast included — and works through a long transcript in sections, quoting with timestamps. Captions are needed. Joe reads YouTube’s own transcript. If a video has none, Joe says so; you can send him the transcript another way, or transcribe a recording you have. YouTube asks for a person. If YouTube shows its unusual-traffic check, Joe stops and tells you right away. Open YouTube in FlowJoe’s browser to complete the check yourself, then ask Joe again. Joe does not try to pass the check or retry it. Stopping. Stop in the Joe chat, or closing Joe’s tab yourself, ends the read. Stop also cancels a request waiting behind another read without waiting for that video to finish. Your YouTube account. Joe’s tab uses the same YouTube session as your built-in browser, so videos Joe reads can appear in your YouTube watch history and recommendations. History and saved tabs. Joe’s tab is never added to your browser history or saved tabs, and it can’t be brought back with Reopen Closed Tab. Guests. A guest’s Joe can read a YouTube video too, when the owner has Joe switched on for that guest. The read happens on the owner’s computer: the owner briefly sees Joe’s tab in their tab row. If the owner switches off a guest’s Joe while a request is waiting, that request will not open a tab. Every brain. This works the same whichever brain runs Joe. Outside assistants connected through the Agent Bridge can’t use it.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Local transcription keeps the audio on your computer and works offline after setup. If you later attach or paste the transcript into an online Joe conversation, that text follows the chat provider’s normal processing rules. Local transcription has no length or file-size limit — a long meeting or lecture runs in one go, and takes as long as your computer needs. FlowJoe first converts the recording in a separate, locked-down background step (so even a damaged or malicious audio file never reaches Whisper directly), which needs free memory for a very long recording; if your computer runs out, FlowJoe tells you so — the app itself keeps running — and you can close other apps or split the file. The recording must be in an audio format your computer can decode. Your audio output device’s sample rate does not affect local transcription. Quitting FlowJoe stops pending model detection as well as active transcription. No compatible model found: choose a download, or use More options to locate a supported file. Download did not finish: check your connection and available disk space, then retry. Your saved method/model stays unchanged. Model unavailable: it may have moved or been removed. Open management and choose a ready model. Local engine unavailable: use a supported desktop build with the transcription engine included. Compatible existing models may still be available. FlowJoe will not automatically upload your recording. Slow transcription: try a smaller model or close other memory-heavy apps. Free transcription uses this computer’s resources. Wrong words: try a clearer recording or a more capable model, and review the transcript before relying on it. Online transcription accepts recordings up to 25 MB. Use a shorter or compressed recording if yours exceeds that limit. For online transcription, the app shows the selected model and its published cost estimate. OpenAI bills API usage separately from any ChatGPT subscription. See Token usage with Joe for other paid AI

title: Transcribe audio
content: AI activity.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Open Manage local models, choose a model downloaded by FlowJoe, and expand More options. Choose Remove downloaded model, then confirm in FlowJoe’s dialog. Cancel or Escape keeps it. You can download it again later. Models found outside FlowJoe remain untouched, and removing a model does not remove your recordings or saved transcripts.

title: Transcribe audio
header: Add finished transcripts beside their recordings
content: After a background Chat transcription finishes, Joe offers Add to gallery or Not now using his usual proposal card. You can keep chatting while deciding. Nothing is added before you accept. Add to gallery saves each complete transcript as a text document in a stack with its matching audio, on the same node. The audio stays first. Joe confirms where he put the documents; Show in gallery selects the matching transcript. The confirmation remains available in conversation history. Not now leaves the results in Recent transcripts, with their opening lines and separate Open buttons. Opening one does not replace or remove another. Keep on this computer only controls the retained result; accepting Add to gallery creates a separate gallery copy that follows the node’s sharing rules. If the gallery changes appear but saving fails, Joe says they are still unsaved. The confirmation keeps Show in gallery; the same proposal cannot add another copy. Use FlowJoe’s normal Save or Undo to recover. The opening transcript preview, Open, and Copy remain available after adding it to a stack.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Ask Joe, “Transcribe only the first minute of this podcast,” or specify a start and end time. FlowJoe prepares that excerpt before speech recognition or an online upload; it does not transcribe the full recording and cut the text afterward. The recording stays unchanged. The background card shows the requested interval, and the retained result keeps its time range. Transcript timestamps are relative to the excerpt. If you correct a running job to a shorter interval, Joe can stop that job and start the requested excerpt after stopping finishes. Each new reply receives the current job state so Joe can check what is actually running.

title: Transcribe audio
content: Your local model selection and installed model files stay on this computer across builds. FlowJoe also recognizes existing compatible Whisper models. On macOS, an existing Homebrew Whisper installation can use the matching installed library recorded by its PyTorch installation when Homebrew’s current library link has changed. This recovery is limited to the Whisper process. It does not download another model. If the engine cannot start, Joe reports an engine problem and directs you to repair Whisper or choose another installed model. That is distinct from a missing-model setup request. FlowJoe does not silently switch to paid transcription.

title: Transcribe audio
content: The background transcription card lines up with the chat prompt field. It shows a percentage when the engine supplies one, and names preparation or speaker detection when those steps are running. A recognition percentage does not measure the later speaker-detection step. Joe’s status clears that percentage when the next step starts. A remaining-time estimate appears only after enough measured local recognition progress. Near completion, during speaker detection, or when timing is unavailable, the card says it is still estimating instead of promising a finish time.

title: Token usage with Joe
content: What each send costs, how the token bar works, and how to shrink the flow map. You pay your AI provider for what Joe is sent, not only for the sentence you typed. Each send includes the flow outline, where you are in the tree, the current slot’s notes, recent chat, and any files you attached. Two checkboxes above the message box control the largest piece: the flow map. Choose the context that helps Joe answer the question; do not send unrelated material.

title: Token usage with Joe
content: Whisper · Free on this computer in Joe’s Transcribe tab runs locally after a one-time model download. It uses no OpenAI API credit and has no per-use fee. OpenAI · Paid online uploads the recording and is charged to your API account; its estimate appears in the transcription window. This is separate from the chat token bar described below. See Transcribe audio.

title: Token usage with Joe
content: A typical Joe send is a bundle: Your message and the recent chat turns still in this session. The flow map — the tree outline: every included node, slot, and stack item by name and id, plus your written Flow Summary. Names only, not file contents. Where you are — the current node, current slot, flow name, and small counts. The current slot’s notes — and, for a stack, every item’s notes. Joe Memories, compacted chat memory, and any attached files or images. Joe’s built-in instructions (the same on every send). Tool definitions — the list of actions Joe is allowed to take this send (propose changes, read the flow, look up the manual, web search, code interpreter), each described to the model. These definitions can be one of the larger fixed costs: the size depends on your permission level, available features and the model’s tokenizer. Descriptions are kept short without removing Joe’s actions. At Off, only the manual-lookup tool remains. You are billed for the whole bundle. On a large tree, the flow map is usually the biggest slice; after that, the tool definitions and Joe’s instructions are the biggest fixed pieces. When Smart context loading is on there is also a small chapter-picking step before the reply, with a second request if its first helper misses — see A second request per send below.

title: Token usage with Joe
content: At the bottom of the Joe panel is a segmented token bar. It shows how much of the model’s context window this send would use. In the docked Joe panel the bar is the small token count beside Send. Hover over it to peek at the breakdown; press it to keep the breakdown open (it then has a close button). The breakdown is one column: This send with its total and its share of the context window, the bar, then one line per part with its tokens and its share of this send. Parts with nothing in them are listed together on one line (“Not in this send: …”). Press What each part is to open a sentence under each part — Joe system also lists its modules with their counts — plus the Draft line and the tokens-per-minute note; press Hide what each part is or Escape to fold them away again. In the floating Joe window, the ? next to the bar opens the same breakdown with the explanations already open. The breakdown never covers a reply’s cost receipt: while a receipt is open, hovering the count does not open the breakdown (so you can reach Send), pressing the count folds the receipt away first, and opening a receipt closes the breakdown. The bar is split into the same labels the legend uses: Bucket What it is Joe system Joe’s built-in instructions. Tools The tool definitions Joe is handed this send, plus the short usage notes that come with Web search and Code interpreter when they are on. Shrinks when you lower Joe’s flow permission; Off still sends the manual-lookup tool. Flow map The tree outline and your Flow Summary. This is what Omit entire flow map removes from the automatic send. Location Where you are — current node, current slot, flow name, small counts, and any recent transcription-job status Joe is sent. Slot data The current slot’s full notes (and every stack item’s notes). FlowJoe manual App-help chapters loaded for this send. Joe Memories Notes you asked Joe to remember. Compacted Memory The saved summary that replaced older turns. Chat messages The visible turns in this

title: Token usage with Joe
content: this session. Empties when you clear the conversation. Attachments Images, files, JSON, or extra items you attached. Estimate buffer A fixed 4% safety margin on top of everything counted, for request framing and tokenizer differences. It is padding, not a measurement — it does not stand in for anything the bar has not counted. While a transcription runs, Joe’s automatic context identifies the job and any requested time range. He checks live status when asked about progress; a changing percentage is not repeated with every chat message. The progress card still shows the current measurements. Each chat message also shows a small cost chip (for example +150 tok/send). Pinning, omitting, or deleting a message updates the bar immediately. The number does not move while you type. Your unsent draft is shown separately as draft +N on send and is added to the total only when you send. The FlowJoe manual count starts with a short estimate, then updates when the selected chapters have loaded. If Joe selects different chapters or you switch conversations, an older lookup cannot replace the newer count. The bar is an estimate based on the text’s characters and scripts. Recognized decomposed accents and Korean syllables receive a conservative extra allowance. Context warnings or compaction can therefore appear earlier for that text. After each reply the app records the provider’s real input-token count next to the estimate it made for that send (visible in the diagnostics/debug output), so a persistent gap can be spotted and fixed. Across Joe’s API-key and supported sign-in brains, most detailed tool instructions and parameters load only when needed. Joe keeps each permitted action’s name and purpose available, so this does not remove actions to save tokens. Some connections load the details themselves; others use FlowJoe’s internal lookup before calling the same action. Saved-file program tools keep their existing loading behavior. Loading can add a step, so savings depend on

title: Token usage with Joe
