content: Save this as changes.json: [ {"verb": "createNode", "args": {"position": "root", "values": {"name": "CLI notes"}}} ] Check the changes first, then apply them: flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --preview flowjoe-cli apply changes.json The second command waits while you approve or reject the request in FlowJoe. Keep the terminal command running until it reports the result. To apply without approval cards, including deletion approvals, use: flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --autoapprove --autoapprove applies only to that command. It changes no saved setting and does not change other agents’ approvals. FlowJoe still enforces permissions, privacy protections and validation. You need a desktop build that supports this option; the CLI refuses to send actions if support is absent.

title: Start using the CLI
content: The CLI uses the same available Flow actions as the Agent Bridge: reading, searching, organizing nodes and references, editing supported content, preparing media and more. Run flowjoe-cli actions to see what your running app offers. Some actions depend on your app’s features and permissions. Image generation uses your configured service and may incur its usual charges. This first version requires the desktop app. It does not provide every desktop setting or control, open/import/export whole Flows, switch workspaces, or run by itself without FlowJoe. See the command reference, scripting examples, and approvals and troubleshooting. For step-by-step examples, start with everyday tasks. The complete action reference covers each bridge action. The editing verbs have examples in node changes, gallery and stack changes, and Flow details and automations.

title: CLI commands
content: The commands and options available in flowjoe-cli. read_chat_attachment also supports retained attachment memory selected through an admitted history record; omitting mode keeps the connection-upload behavior. Repository reads use action read_repository and action read_repo_file; see the repository inputs. Use one run connection for continuation. Run flowjoe-cli --help whenever you need a reminder. Use --version to see the installed CLI version. Command What it does flowjoe-cli status Checks that the running desktop app is reachable. flowjoe-cli show Shows the current Flow’s node names and IDs. flowjoe-cli search "words" Finds visible matching Flow text. flowjoe-cli actions Lists the actions your running app offers. flowjoe-cli actions search_flow Shows one action’s description and expected input. flowjoe-cli apply changes.json Applies a file of Flow changes after the required approval. flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --preview Checks the changes without applying them. flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --autoapprove Applies without approval cards, including for deletions. flowjoe-cli run steps.json Runs a list of actions in one connection. flowjoe-cli action search_flow --file input.json Uses a particular action directly.

title: CLI commands
content: Option Meaning --json Outputs JSON for scripts instead of the readable summary. --wait 60 Stops waiting after 60 seconds. The default is 120 seconds. --settings-file <path> Uses a particular app bridge settings file. --autoapprove Skips approval cards for this apply, run or action command, including deletions. --preview Checks an apply command without applying or queuing changes. Use - instead of a JSON filename to read from standard input. To pass a value beginning with -- as an argument, put -- before it. Quote search phrases containing spaces. --preview always keeps an apply command non-mutating, even with --autoapprove. A preview checks the changes; it does not draw a new preview panel in FlowJoe. There are no saved CLI approval settings.

title: CLI commands
content: apply accepts either an array of changes or an object containing ops: { "ops": [ {"verb": "createNode", "args": {"position": "root", "values": {"name": "Research"}}} ] } A single file is sent as one Flow change request. FlowJoe validates it and applies it atomically: if an operation fails, the patch is rolled back. Use node IDs from show when an action needs an existing node. Use flowjoe-cli actions describe_patch_protocol to inspect the catalog action, then flowjoe-cli action describe_patch_protocol --json to read the current change names and arguments.

title: CLI commands
content: The readable commands cover common tasks. action gives scripts access to the full live action catalog, including future actions without waiting for a new convenience command in the CLI. For example, save {"query":"launch plan","limit":10} in input.json, then run: flowjoe-cli action search_flow --file input.json --json See the complete action reference for inputs, examples, returned data and approval behavior, and everyday tasks for reading notes and other common jobs. The editing verbs are covered by the node, gallery/stack and Flow/task references. The advanced action names and JSON fields match the running app. Read their instructions with actions <name> before using them. Some actions ask you to choose a file or interact in FlowJoe; --autoapprove skips approval cards, not file pickers or missing service setup.

title: CLI commands
content: --json writes one JSON result to standard output. Progress messages, such as waiting for approval, go to standard error. Tool content is preserved, including images and multiple text blocks. Successful help/version commands print their usual text, even if --json is also supplied. Results include version: 1, status, and autoapprove. Action results are under result; run also includes steps. An error includes error and a readable message. show --json returns the app’s permitted snapshot content rather than only the names shown by ordinary show. Exit code Meaning 0 The command completed, changes applied, or a preview passed. 2 Invalid command, file, action name or result reference. 3 The connection or required app capability was unavailable. 4 An app action failed. 5 You rejected the approval request in FlowJoe. 6 Completion was not confirmed before the waiting time ran out. 130 The command was interrupted. Inputs are limited to 16 MB. Action lists are limited to 1,000 steps. A time limit or interruption does not prove an edit was canceled. Check FlowJoe before repeating it.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
content: Read notes, inspect branches, edit content, add references, and check results. Retained attachment memory can recover saved evidence after a document’s original bytes are gone. It returns stored memory text and provenance, not the original document. To inspect a repository, use repository state and file reads. Choose saved bytes or an actual already-open draft/revision; reading never opens or saves an editor. To change one exact piece of text in a saved file, read it with source: "saved", then propose editRepoFileText with its oid as expectedOid; the change saves the file in FlowJoe without writing your working folder, committing or pushing. Install and connect using Start using the CLI. These examples work on the currently open Flow; they do not open or switch Flows. Replace YOUR_NODE_ID with an ID from show. For an action with inputs, save the JSON block as input.json, then run its command.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
content: flowjoe-cli show flowjoe-cli search "launch plan" --json show lists node names and IDs. Search returns visible matches and their node IDs; it searches node and gallery notes, but does not search the text inside document files.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
header: Read a node’s notes and information
content: Save as input.json: { "rootId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "maxDepth": 1, "includeSummary": true, "includeGallery": true } flowjoe-cli action get_flow_snapshot --file input.json --json Find the target ID in the returned nodes list. Its summary is the node’s notes; other fields can include status, tags, theme, Freeze state and gallery details. rootId selects the branch, and maxDepth bounds the returned depth. The branch may include children; identify the node by ID rather than assuming a particular array position. Missing or marked text can mean it is hidden from Joe. --autoapprove does not reveal it. The result is inside the CLI envelope’s result.content: a text block contains the app’s JSON. For example, the inner snapshot data has this general shape (fields depend on your Flow): { "treeName": "Launch research", "flowSummary": "Research and decisions for the launch.", "nodes": [ {"id": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "name": "Research", "summary": "Questions to investigate next."} ] } This is an illustration of the inner data, not a complete response or an input file.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
header: Read the Flow’s notes or a whole branch
content: flowjoe-cli show --json The returned snapshot includes treeName and, when present and permitted, flowSummary for the open Flow. Nodes carry their own summary fields. For a branch, use the previous JSON input with its rootId and omit maxDepth if you need deeper descendants. Large snapshots are bounded (default 2,000 nodes); check truncated, narrow the branch, or raise nodeCap deliberately.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
header: Read gallery notes or a document
content: A gallery snapshot gives permitted titles, notes and metadata; it does not contain the complete underlying files. Gallery metadata can be shortened. To read a document’s actual text, save: {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0} flowjoe-cli action read_item_content --file input.json --json slotIndex: 0 means the first gallery item. Add itemIndex: 1 only if it is a stack and you want its second member. Use get_island_content instead for a spreadsheet, rich document or calendar; use read_media_content for image content, or read_media_blob for media as a data URL. These reads do not automatically ask an AI to summarize the content.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
content: Save as changes.json: [ { "verb":"setNodeSummary", "args":{"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","value":"Review the launch checklist on Friday."} } ] flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --preview --json flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --json Approve the second request in FlowJoe if asked. To skip the approval card, use flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --autoapprove --json. Node notes use setNodeSummary; gallery-item notes use setSlotFields with fields.notes. Neither rewrites the text stored inside a document.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
header: Create a branch and fill its notes in one request
content: A same-patch alias lets later changes refer to a node being created. Save as changes.json: [ {"verb":"createNode","args":{"position":"root","alias":"$research","values":{"name":"Research"}}}, {"verb":"setNodeSummary","args":{"nodeId":"$research","value":"Questions and sources for the next release."}} ] flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --preview flowjoe-cli apply changes.json Both changes succeed together or that patch rolls back. An alias exists only inside its own patch. It is different from a run list’s $result reference, which reads an earlier action’s response.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
header: Add a file or generate an image
content: For a file you want to choose in the app, use request_file. For script-provided text or supported images, follow the complete upload → prepare → place example. Uploads are temporary and must be consumed in that same run list. For image generation, save as steps.json: [ { "action":"generate_image", "input":{"prompt":"A watercolor illustration of a mountain lake","title":"Mountain lake"}, "saveAs":"generated" }, { "action":"propose_flow_patch", "input":{"ops":[{"verb":"addImageSlots","args":{"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","entries":[{"$result":"generated","path":["entry"]}]}}]} } ] flowjoe-cli run steps.json --wait 300 --json Generation uses your configured service and its usual credits. Approve placement when asked; add --autoapprove to skip placement approval. That flag does not skip service setup, make generation free, or change the processing deadline. Five minutes is a longer wait, not a guarantee that the provider will finish. A generated result is staged until the placement step succeeds.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
header: Inspect changes or undo within a script
content: Save as steps.json: [ {"action":"propose_flow_patch","input":{"ops":[{"verb":"createNode","args":{"position":"root","values":{"name":"Temporary CLI example"}}}]}}, {"action":"list_recent_changes","input":{"limit":5}}, {"action":"undo_last_change"} ] flowjoe-cli run steps.json --json This creates a temporary node, reads this command’s history, then attempts to undo that creation. Undo refuses if the Flow changed in the meantime. A separate invocation of undo_last_change cannot undo an earlier CLI command. Neither session history nor undo is a general Flow backup.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
header: Use stable reference IDs in repeatable scripts
content: For verbs that support them, prefer slotEntryId and other ID alternatives from the live catalog over saved positions. This avoids accidentally targeting a different reference after a reorder. For example, setSlotFields accepts: [ {"verb":"setSlotFields","args":{"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotEntryId":"YOUR_ENTRY_ID","fields":{"notes":"Reviewed."}}} ] Read the ID from a fresh gallery snapshot and the alternatives from flowjoe-cli action describe_patch_protocol --json. An entry ID does not bypass permissions or make a deleted reference exist. Not all read actions or editing verbs accept the same ID fields.

title: Everyday CLI tasks
content: --json retains the full result for a script, and the command’s exit code indicates success or failure. A list stops at its first failed step; earlier completed changes stay applied. One apply patch is atomic, but a whole run list is not. A timeout or interrupted command can leave an edit applied or an approval card pending. Check FlowJoe before retrying; see approvals and troubleshooting. Browse the complete action reference and the editing references for nodes, gallery and stacks, and Flow details, memories and automations.

title: CLI action reference
content: Every bridge action: what it does, inputs, examples, results, and approvals. The CLI has simple commands such as show and search, plus access to the running app’s actions. An action is a complete request, such as reading a document or preparing an image. The editing verbs are individual changes sent inside apply or propose_flow_patch; see node changes, reference and stack changes, and Flow details and automations. This page covers the current desktop bridge action surface. Availability depends on the running build, permission level and configured services. Read the actual list with flowjoe-cli actions. get_app_state, query_history and read_history expose current app facts and retained history. Saved history is separate from this command’s recent-change and undo history. Read access includes observational actions, including automation status and app help; it does not grant Flow edits. The editing catalog can still be inspected with Read access, even though applying its verbs requires Propose access. The CLI does not expose MCP resource listing/reading as a command; open_reference supplies app help.

title: CLI action reference
content: On 2026-10-19, real CLI discovery against a fully provisioned desktop (history, repository, scheduler and help services present) returned 27 actions with Propose access and 20 with Read access. Both profiles included 19 observational read tools; Read’s extra action was upload_attachment, which prepares connection-local input rather than reading existing content. Propose also exposes editing, staging, generation, file import, navigation, player control and undo. A desktop without one of those services lists fewer actions. These action totals are separate from the 62 editing verb names returned by describe_patch_protocol: 61 distinct changes, because setNodeReadOnly is an older name for setNodeFrozen. That catalog includes editRepoFileText. Read can inspect the editing catalog but cannot apply its changes. The current catalog returns 63 names (62 distinct changes) and includes the three virtual-slot verbs: makeVirtualSlotReal, removeVirtualMaster and addVirtualSlot. In get_flow_snapshot, a virtual slot carries virtualSlot: true and its master’s place (virtualOf, masterNodeId, masterSlotIndex) instead of content, or virtualMaster: "hidden_from_joe" when the master can’t be seen; a master carries virtualCount and virtualPlaces. Read actions aimed at a virtual slot read its master and say so in readFrom. A second measurement later on 2026-10-19, after Joe’s workflow hand-offs and picture search landed, returned the same totals, and a direct MCP connection was offered exactly the same actions as the CLI at both access levels. Observational tools in both profiles were get_flow_snapshot, describe_patch_protocol, read_media_blob, get_app_state, query_history, read_history, get_node_neighbors, search_flow, get_island_content, read_item_content, read_media_content, list_joe_memories, list_scheduled_tasks, open_reference, list_recent_changes, get_approval_outcome and read_chat_attachment, read_repository and read_repo_file. Uploads, staging, generation, navigation, player

title: CLI action reference
content: player actions and mutations are not counted as observational reads. These are dated measurements, not permanent limits: discover your running app’s catalog before scripting. Native Joe, external MCP and guests can have different services and authority; an owner endpoint does not establish guest or shared-Flow support. Transcription was added after the dated catalog measurements above. Discover the running catalog for current totals.

title: CLI action reference
content: Transcribe an audio recording already in the Flow using saved Transcribe settings. The complete result is kept in Recent transcripts. Propose access is required. Local setup never falls back to paid service. This action is available in Joe’s API and CLI brains and authenticated external MCP. {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","entryId":"YOUR_AUDIO_ENTRY_ID"} flowjoe-cli action transcribe_audio --file input.json --wait 3600 --json Use stable snapshot IDs: entryId names the recording leaf, including inside a stack. No path, URL or provider-setting override is accepted. Missing or sealed recordings are refused. choose_audio returns accessible recording identities: ask the user and retry with one exact entry. local_setup_required means select/install a model in Transcribe and retry. Ctrl+C cancels the run. Success returns saved: true, recordId, method/model and up to 12,000 characters of text. When truncated is true, query transcript history and continue with read_history using its revision/cursor. The same inputs work over MCP. External calls do not open or write to Joe’s chat. See Transcribe audio.

title: CLI action reference
content: Joe works the same on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex). On a Mac this includes Antigravity; on Windows and Linux, Antigravity can’t use Flow tools yet. His chat inside FlowJoe, whether an OpenAI or Gemini model or an installed tool such as Claude Code answering as Joe, uses most of the actions on this page, plus the FlowJoe actions below that the CLI and other assistants connected from outside cannot call. Those actions never appear in flowjoe-cli actions or in the tools a connected assistant is given, and asking for one by name is refused (unknown_action in the CLI). The last row lists tools built into some brains, not FlowJoe actions. In Joe’s chat What it does find_pictures Ranks the pictures in part of your Flow by what they show, so Joe opens only the best matches. Needs a TypeSafe key; without one, Joe picks pictures by their names. request_app_workflow Shows a card that hands you an existing workflow: restore a saved version, export a node, import a Flow or review changes made on another computer. You confirm in the app’s usual dialog; Joe never runs it himself. read_terminal_output, read_browser_tab Read terminal lines you shared, or keep reading a browser page you asked about in parts (the page itself still reaches every brain as context). See the note under Read a repository file. read_youtube_captions Reads a YouTube video’s captions in a background tab of FlowJoe’s browser and pages through the whole transcript. See Ask Joe about a YouTube video. Web search, Code interpreter Built into some brains rather than FlowJoe actions. See Bring Your Own Brain.

title: CLI action reference
content: For each action below, save its JSON input as input.json, replace YOUR_… placeholders with real IDs from flowjoe-cli show --json, and run the command shown. No input file is needed for actions with no inputs. All commands require FlowJoe running with Agent Bridge enabled. Results use the CLI’s JSON envelope; the app’s response is under result, with text and possibly image content blocks. A JSON-looking text block holds the action’s data. --json does not turn an image into a written description. Inspect the actual result before assuming a change succeeded. Private/hidden content remains withheld, even with --autoapprove. Gallery and stack positions start at 0. Only pass itemIndex for a member inside a stack. Files, undo, recent-change history and retained-history and repository cursors are owned by one command’s connection. Content-reader cursors instead bind the target, source revision and identical selectors; using one run list is convenient, but they do not have the history reader’s session restriction. Examples using $result, previous uploads or undo must be steps in one run list, not separate invocations. A two-minute default wait still applies with --autoapprove; the flag removes approval waiting, not processing time. Increase it with --wait when needed.

title: CLI action reference
content: Read the current Flow’s admitted repository status, scoped commit identities/dates, or a saved-versus-committed file comparison. This does not run commands, stage changes, check out files or edit content. Private and Hidden from Joe sources remain withheld. Commit messages and author names are withheld because they can mention hidden paths. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Available with external Read or Propose access when the desktop repository service exists, independently of native Joe’s chat setting. Input Required? Meaning repoNodeId Yes Repository node ID from the current Flow snapshot. view Yes status, log or diff. path For diff Exact admitted repository-relative file path. diffScope No all, staged or unstaged; staged filtering requires an existing current Changes-list baseline. limit No 1–12,000 characters; default 12,000. cursor No Returned continuation; repeat identical selectors in the same run connection. {"repoNodeId":"YOUR_REPO_NODE_ID","view":"status"} flowjoe-cli action read_repository --file input.json --json Result: Bounded content, source/view, branch/history identity and HEAD provenance, character range and optional nextCursor. Status describes saved gallery bytes against the branch. Deleted paths without an admitted live owner are omitted. Staging is explicitly unavailable unless a matching current Changes list exists. A changed Flow, source, privacy, permission, HEAD or canceled request refuses publication.

title: CLI action reference
content: Choose saved, draft or historical explicitly. Saved reads use native Git bytes. Draft reads require the actual already-open editor model; historical reads require an already-open read-only revision model with a unique admitted current file owner. The action never opens, selects or saves an editor. An unavailable draft is never replaced with saved text. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Reading adds no write; the separate editRepoFileText editing verb is reviewed before it changes a file. Input Required? Meaning repoNodeId Yes Current repository node ID. source Yes saved, draft or historical. nodeId, entryId Saved/draft Exact current gallery owner and entry identity. path, oid, revisionTreeOid Historical Exact repository-relative path and identities of the retained open revision model. limit No 1–12,000 characters; default 12,000. cursor No Repeat the same selectors in the same run connection. {"repoNodeId":"YOUR_REPO_NODE_ID","nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","entryId":"YOUR_ENTRY_ID","source":"saved"} flowjoe-cli action read_repo_file --file input.json --json Result: content, explicit source, path/OID and character range; draft/historical results also identify the captured model revision. Changed file ownership, bytes, privacy, model version or session invalidates continuation. Use one run list for all pages. A fresh command starts a different session. Which text you get depends on source. saved is the file as FlowJoe last saved it (an immutable Git blob), draft is unsaved typing in a repository editor tab that is already open, and historical is an older revision that is already open read-only. These are never substituted for one another. To change a file, propose the separate editRepoFileText editing verb with Propose access. Reading never grants it. Browser-page reading is not available to the CLI or any external client. Joe inside FlowJoe can read a page you explicitly ask about, and on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as

title: CLI action reference
content: as Claude, Grok and Codex) he can also keep reading it in parts. No external connection, including this CLI, can receive that approval. Model arguments, a native Joe request, or an open tab cannot supply one. A future page grant must bind this connection to an explicit user request, exact page/revision and revocation lifecycle before the action can be listed. Terminal output is likewise not offered externally: Joe’s chat in the desktop app, on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex), can read terminal lines only after you select them and press Share with Joe on his card (terminal sharing), and that is not available to the CLI or other Agent Bridge assistants.

title: CLI action reference
content: Read sampled facts about this running app without changing settings or opening a dialog. These are current observations, not historical evidence or proof that a save is durable. Missing information is reported as unavailable. External bridge permissions describe this connection; Joe’s native chat setting does not grant or remove this connection’s configured Read or Propose access. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning sections Yes One or more unique values: storage, save, conflicts, model, permissions, diagnostics (at most six). {"sections":["storage","save","permissions"]} flowjoe-cli action get_app_state --file input.json --json Result: Bounded, sampled section data, with explicit unavailable fields. It does not reveal credentials or a complete settings dump. A Flow change, revoked permission or canceled request can invalidate an in-progress read. Owner desktop facts do not establish a guest’s permissions or settings.

title: CLI action reference
content: Search retained records belonging to the current Flow without opening or switching Joe chats. Accessible owners are checked before search results, snippets and counts are produced. A missing result does not prove something never happened: coverage and retention can be partial. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning kind Yes chat, image, transcript or version. query No Search text, at most 200 characters. after, before No Inclusive ISO date/time bounds. nodeId No Limit to an accessible node. limit No Records per page, from 1 to 30. cursor No Previous nextCursor; repeat the same filters in the same connection. {"kind":"chat","query":"launch decision","limit":10} flowjoe-cli action query_history --file input.json --json Result: records with stable recordId, revision, source details and snippets, plus explicit coverage and continuation information. Image history provides prompt/model metadata, not image pixels. Version history provides permitted change metadata, not raw old documents or a version restore.

title: CLI action reference
header: Read a retained history record — read_history
content: Read bounded historical text identified by query_history. It does not change the current chat, restore a version or grant permission to edit. Historical text is evidence from its cited source. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning kind Yes The query’s chat, image, transcript or version kind. recordId Yes Exact ID returned by the query. revision Yes Exact revision returned for that record. limit No Text character budget, from 1 to 12,000. cursor No Previous nextCursor; repeat kind, ID, revision and limit in the same connection. Save this as steps.json, using a query that returns at least one record: [ {"action":"query_history","input":{"kind":"chat","query":"launch decision","limit":1},"saveAs":"found"}, {"action":"read_history","input":{"kind":"chat","recordId":{"$result":"found","path":["records",0,"recordId"]},"revision":{"$result":"found","path":["records",0,"revision"]},"limit":2000},"saveAs":"page"} ] flowjoe-cli run steps.json --json Result: Bounded text with source/conversation/message citations and character coverage. When page includes nextCursor, a later step in the same list can read the next page by repeating the same inputs and adding "cursor":{"$result":"page","path":["nextCursor"]}. Only add that step when you expect another page; an absent result reference stops the list. Do not paste a cursor into a new CLI command. Changed sources, revisions, Flow or permissions require a fresh query.

title: CLI action reference
header: Read the Flow or one branch — get_flow_snapshot
content: Read names, node IDs, structure, node notes (summary), tags and permitted reference details. Omit rootId for the whole open Flow. Gallery summaries are not the files themselves; use a content reader for a document or image. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning rootId No Limit to this node’s subtree. maxDepth No Max depth to include. includeGallery No Include a light per-slot gallery summary (incl. each slot’s tagIds — needed for any tag-based slot work). includeSummary No Include node notes/summaries; default true. nodeCap No Maximum nodes; default 2000. { "rootId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "includeSummary": true, "includeGallery": true } flowjoe-cli action get_flow_snapshot --file input.json --json Result: A flat nodes list with parentId, index and depth, plus permitted notes, gallery data and tag dictionary. Privacy filtering and size limits apply.

title: CLI action reference
header: Find nearby or related nodes — get_node_neighbors
content: Read the parent, children, siblings and other nodes sharing tags. Use this when you need one node’s surroundings rather than the whole tree. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning nodeId Yes The node whose neighborhood to read (an id from get_flow_snapshot or your context). { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID" } flowjoe-cli action get_node_neighbors --file input.json --json Result: The node’s neighborhood and tag relationships; sealed content remains withheld.

title: CLI action reference
header: Find text in your Flow — search_flow
content: Search node names/notes and gallery or stack titles/notes. Matching is case-insensitive substring matching. It does not search inside PDF or document file contents; follow a match with a content reader. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning query Yes The text to search for (case-insensitive substring match). limit No Max results to return (default 20, max 100). { "query": "launch plan", "limit": 10 } flowjoe-cli action search_flow --file input.json --json Result: Ranked matches with nodeId, matching field and excerpt, and slotIndex/itemIndex when applicable. Empty results mean no visible match.

title: CLI action reference
header: Read a document or note file — read_item_content
content: Read extracted text from a gallery note, text file or supported PDF/Word/ODT/PowerPoint/EPUB. Add itemIndex only for a stack member. For scanned PDFs, startPage selects a 1-based page; follow the result’s continuation guidance. To look at chosen pages of any PDF as images (a chart, photo or scanned page), set viewPages with startPage and optionally endPage; the user is asked once per PDF. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning nodeId Yes The node whose gallery holds the item. slotIndex Yes 0-based slot index in that node’s gallery. itemIndex No Only for stack slots: 0-based item index inside the stack. entryId No Expected stable entry ID; a mismatch refuses the read. itemPath No Nested stack indices, starting at 0; replaces itemIndex. startChar, endChar No Character range starting at 0; end is exclusive. startLine, endLine No Line range starting at 1; end is inclusive. heading No Exact Markdown heading text, through the next heading. Choose characters, lines or heading, not a combination. maxChars No Page budget, from 512 to 60,000. cursor No Previous nextCursor; repeat all other inputs. startPage No PDF page images only: the 1-based page to view with viewPages, or to continue a SCANNED PDF from (the result tells you the next page). Omit for a normal read. endPage No With viewPages: the last page to view, at most 4 pages per call. Defaults to startPage. viewPages No PDF only: true looks at pages startPage–endPage as images, for a chart, photo or scanned page marked “No text layer” in the text. The user is asked once per PDF; declining returns view_declined. { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } flowjoe-cli action read_item_content --file input.json --json Result: Text pages include textContent, source.revision, exact coverage, partial, truncated and, when more remains, nextCursor. Scanned PDFs, and any PDF read with viewPages, can instead return page images (a scanned read adds page continuation guidance). For example,

title: CLI action reference
header: Read a document or note file — read_item_content
content: example, {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0,"startLine":2001,"endLine":2050} reads those lines rather than just the beginning of the file. A changed or moved target, changed content or revoked access refuses continuation; restart the read. A canceled read is not a successful empty result.

title: CLI action reference
header: Read a spreadsheet, calendar or rich document — get_island_content
content: Read one workbench reference’s structured content. Add itemIndex only for a member inside a stack. Use page: true for bounded, addressed pages. An open workbench may be flushed before reading; source.policy identifies flushed or stored evidence. A failed flush is reported as flush_unconfirmed, rather than presenting an unsaved draft as saved content. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning nodeId Yes The node whose gallery holds the island. slotIndex Yes 0-based slot index in that node’s gallery. itemIndex No Only for stack slots: 0-based item index inside the stack. { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } flowjoe-cli action get_island_content --file input.json --json Additional optional inputs: Input Meaning page Set true for addressed paging. entryId, itemPath Expected entry ID and nested stack path; itemPath replaces itemIndex. listSheets List workbook sheet IDs, names and dimensions without cell content. sheet Exact workbook sheet ID or name. Omit to read workbook order. range Inclusive A1 range, such as A2001:C2050. startRow, endRow, startColumn, endColumn Alternative inclusive workbook bounds; rows start at 1, columns use letters. startBlock, endBlock Rich-document block range, starting at 0 with exclusive end; body, then headers and footers. after, before, timezone Inclusive calendar dates in YYYY-MM-DD and an IANA timezone, such as America/Denver; defaults to calendar timezone or UTC. No recurrence expansion. limit Record budget: up to 2,000 workbook cells or 200 calendar/document records. maxChars Character budget, from 512 to 16,000 for these pages. cursor Previous nextCursor; repeat all other inputs. For example, use one of these as input.json with the command above: {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0,"page":true,"sheet":"Sheet1","range":"A2001:C2050"} {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0,"page":true,"startBlock":100,"endBlock":110}

title: CLI action reference
header: Read a spreadsheet, calendar or rich document — get_island_content
content: {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0,"page":true,"startBlock":100,"endBlock":110} {"nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0,"page":true,"after":"2026-10-01","before":"2026-10-31","timezone":"America/Denver"} Result: content contains JSON text with addressed fragments, including cell/block/event addresses, textOffset and complete. coverage, summary, source.revision, partial, truncated and nextCursor describe the page. A long record can span pages; keep every fragment before moving on. Repeat identical selectors with the cursor in one run list. A changed source or revoked target invalidates continuation rather than silently mixing revisions.

title: CLI action reference
content: Return an image from the gallery. Add itemIndex only for an image inside a stack. This does not ask an AI to describe the image; a script receives metadata and image content. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning nodeId Yes The node whose gallery holds the image. slotIndex Yes 0-based slot index in that node’s gallery. itemIndex No Only for stack slots: 0-based item index inside the stack. { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } flowjoe-cli action read_media_content --file input.json --json Result: Text metadata plus image content blocks when available; —json retains those blocks.

title: CLI action reference
header: Get a reference’s media bytes — read_media_blob
content: Retrieve the actual stored media of one gallery item or stack member. Unlike a snapshot, this returns a data URL. It is useful when a script needs to display or save the media bytes. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning nodeId Yes Node containing the media. slotIndex Yes Gallery position, starting at 0. itemIndex No Stack member position only, starting at 0. { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } flowjoe-cli action read_media_blob --file input.json --json Result: On success, ok, dataUrl, mime and type; unsupported, missing or sealed media returns an error.

title: CLI action reference
content: Read saved memories for the current Flow. Use their IDs for memory changes, rather than inventing IDs. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning scope No Filter by scope; default all. Choices: flow, node, slot, all. includeDisabled No Also include disabled memories (default false). { "scope": "all", "includeDisabled": true } flowjoe-cli action list_joe_memories --file input.json --json Result: Permitted memory IDs, scope, type, text, targets and current send state.

title: CLI action reference
header: Read automations and their status — list_scheduled_tasks
content: List automations for the open Flow and check when they next run. Availability depends on this bridge connection’s permissions and desktop build. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval; available with Read or Propose bridge access. Editing automations still requires Propose access and ordinary approval rules. Inputs: none. flowjoe-cli action list_scheduled_tasks --json Result: Permitted task IDs, titles, enabled states, schedule summaries, targets and runtime status.

title: CLI action reference
content: Read a named help topic. For a single complete page, add page with its exact manual slug, such as cli/node-changes. Use actions open_reference to see the current topic choices. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning topic Yes Help topic ID from the current actions open_reference instructions. page No Optional exact manual page slug, such as cli/node-changes; reads that full page. { "topic": "cli" } flowjoe-cli action open_reference --file input.json --json Result: Reference text and manual links, with any omitted pages or fallback made explicit.

title: CLI action reference
header: Read every supported editing verb — describe_patch_protocol
content: Discover the running app’s editing names and required arguments. This catalog includes optional stable entry-ID alternatives and valid theme IDs. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Inputs: none. flowjoe-cli action describe_patch_protocol --json Result: Protocol/version, verbs and scopes, argRules, idTargets, blobVerbs, deferred capabilities, stageMediaKinds and nodeThemes.

title: CLI action reference
header: Apply a group of Flow changes — propose_flow_patch
content: Send an ordered ops array of editing verbs. The simpler apply command wraps this action. validateOnly true checks without applying or queuing. A patch is atomic: a failed operation rolls back that patch. For editRepoFileText, validateOnly also runs the edit’s read-only file checks (the text appears once, the file or open draft is unchanged, the file is editable), and Apply checks them again. Changes and approval: Changes data. Follows app approval rules unless —autoapprove; this includes deletion, memory and task review. Input Required? Meaning ops Yes Ordered list of {verb, args} editing operations. validateOnly No Check without applying or queuing approval; default false. { "ops": [ { "verb": "setNodeSummary", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "value": "Next steps: review the draft." } } ] } flowjoe-cli action propose_flow_patch --file input.json --json Result: Applied operation results, validation errors or a pending approval. The CLI normally waits for that approval to settle.

title: CLI action reference
header: Prepare content for the gallery — stage_media
content: Prepare new content without placing it. Supply exactly one source: text, dataUrl or attachmentId. Raw document text and SVG text are supported; MIME must match kind. Raw media staging is limited to 10 MB. An attachmentId must come from this connection’s upload_attachment. Explicit nodeId chooses the intended destination; omitted uses the selected node. Changes and approval: Prepares content; no Flow edit approval until placement. Requires an available staging capability. Input Required? Meaning kind No Media kind; defaults to image (or document when text is given, unless mimeType is image/svg+xml → image). Choices: image, pdf, document, audio, video, spreadsheet, rich-document, calendar. dataUrl No Source A: data:MIME;base64,… (at most 10 MB). attachmentId No An ID returned by upload_attachment in this same connection. text No Source C: raw text/markdown/csv/json (kind document) OR raw SVG markup (kind image, mimeType image/svg+xml) — the app encodes + sanitizes it; do NOT base64 it yourself. mimeType No With text: the document flavor (default text/markdown) or image/svg+xml for SVG markup. title No Optional entry title. nodeId No Intended destination node; omitted means the currently selected node. { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "kind": "document", "text": "Meeting notes", "mimeType": "text/plain", "title": "Meeting notes" } flowjoe-cli action stage_media --file input.json --json Result: A prepared entry and stored-media information. Use the returned entry in addImageSlots or a stack verb in the SAME run list.

title: CLI action reference
header: Generate an image for placement — generate_image
content: Use the configured image service and its normal paid credits. The bridge allows at most two generation attempts per connection, including failed attempts; a longer run list must stay within that limit. Optional size and quality can override the app’s generation settings. A style hint applies only when the app’s Generate Images style is None. The external bridge refuses action edit with chat_history_required; to make a variation, use action generate with sourceImageKey or a caller-owned referenceAttachmentId. referenceAttachmentId uses this connection’s uploaded image; sourceImageKey targets an accessible stored image. Select the destination node in FlowJoe before starting generation. The request keeps that destination if you select another node while it runs. A missing, removed, private or hidden destination cannot receive the generated result. Changes and approval: Calls a paid service immediately; —autoapprove is not a billing confirmation. Placement is a separate Flow edit. Input Required? Meaning prompt Yes What to generate, or what to change when supplying a source image. action No Use generate (the default). The external bridge rejects edit because it requires Joe chat history. size No Image dimensions: 1024x1024 (square), 1024x1536 (portrait) or 1536x1024 (wide). Omit to use your app setting. quality No Choose low, medium, high or auto. Omit to use your app setting. style No Optional style hint; only used when the Generate Images tab style is None. Otherwise that tab’s selected style applies. referenceAttachmentId No For an image reference, use attachment.id returned by upload_attachment earlier in this same run list. Joe-chat attachment IDs and IDs from previous CLI commands are not accepted. sourceImageKey No Stored indexeddb: source key of an accessible gallery image to use for a variation with action generate. Private or hidden-from-Joe images are refused; the original remains unchanged until you place a result. title No Optional title for the staged

title: CLI action reference
header: Generate an image for placement — generate_image
content: staged gallery entry. { "prompt": "A watercolor illustration of a mountain lake", "title": "Mountain lake" } flowjoe-cli action generate_image --file input.json --json Result: A staged image and prepared entry, not an automatically placed gallery item. Place the returned entry in the same run list. For an uploaded image reference, put this step after an image upload_attachment step saved as uploaded in the same run list. Replace YOUR_PROMPT with your instructions: { "action": "generate_image", "input": { "prompt": "YOUR_PROMPT", "referenceAttachmentId": {"$result": "uploaded", "path": ["attachment", "id"]} }, "saveAs": "generated" } This is a run-list step, not a standalone input file. Add a later placement step using {"$result":"generated","path":["entry"]}, as in the image-generation task example. The upload must be an accepted image MIME type; using a text upload or a previous command’s ID is refused.

title: CLI action reference
header: Upload an image or text file for this command — upload_attachment
content: Upload PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, plain text, Markdown or CSV. Current limits: 8 MB per file, 12 attachments and 24 MB total per connection. The base64 field has its own encoded-size limit. PDF, Word, audio and video are not accepted by this upload action; use request_file for the app’s normal import flow. Changes and approval: Uploads to temporary connection storage; no Flow edit approval. Input Required? Meaning fileName Yes File name, 1–180 characters. mimeType Yes Supported image or text MIME type. dataBase64 Yes File bytes encoded as base64, without a data: prefix. { "fileName": "hello.txt", "mimeType": "text/plain", "dataBase64": "SGVsbG8=" } flowjoe-cli action upload_attachment --file input.json --json Result: An attachment with id, fileName, mimeType and sizeBytes. Read or stage it later in the SAME run list; it disappears when the command ends.

title: CLI action reference
header: Read an uploaded attachment or retained attachment memory — read_chat_attachment
content: Omit mode to read a file uploaded by this MCP connection. Upload IDs belong only to this command. With mode: "memory", read retained attachment evidence from an exact admitted conversation returned by query_history; this never borrows whichever native Joe chat is open. Save an upload step as uploaded before the upload example below. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning attachmentId Yes Upload: ID from upload_attachment in this connection. Memory: * to list, or exact memory ID returned by the list. mode No Omit (or image) for the existing uploaded-file read; use memory for retained text evidence. recordId Memory Exact chat recordId returned by query_history. historyRevision Memory That chat record’s revision from records, not the query’s collection revision. revision Memory record/continuation Exact listed memory record revision; list continuations use the memory index revision. start No Returned nextStart: record offset for *, character offset for an exact memory ID; starts at 0. limit No Memory index: 1–30 records; exact memory: 1–12,000 characters. { "attachmentId": { "$result": "uploaded", "path": [ "attachment", "id" ] } } Use this as a step in the same run list as its prerequisite: { "action": "read_chat_attachment", "input": { "attachmentId": { "$result": "uploaded", "path": [ "attachment", "id" ] } } } Result: Uploaded attachment metadata plus image bytes or UTF-8 text content. Use inside a run list. For retained attachment memory, use a query/index/read run list: [ {"action":"query_history","input":{"kind":"chat","query":"YOUR_CONVERSATION_TEXT"},"saveAs":"conversation"}, {"action":"read_chat_attachment","input":{"mode":"memory","attachmentId":"*","recordId":{"$result":"conversation","path":["records",0,"recordId"]},"historyRevision":{"$result":"conversation","path":["records",0,"revision"]}},"saveAs":"index"},

title: CLI action reference
header: Read an uploaded attachment or retained attachment memory — read_chat_attachment
content: {"action":"read_chat_attachment","input":{"mode":"memory","attachmentId":"*","recordId":{"$result":"conversation","path":["records",0,"recordId"]},"historyRevision":{"$result":"conversation","path":["records",0,"revision"]}},"saveAs":"index"}, {"action":"read_chat_attachment","input":{"mode":"memory","attachmentId":{"$result":"index","path":["records",0,"attachmentId"]},"revision":{"$result":"index","path":["records",0,"revision"]},"recordId":{"$result":"conversation","path":["records",0,"recordId"]},"historyRevision":{"$result":"conversation","path":["records",0,"revision"]},"limit":2000},"saveAs":"memory"} ] Check that the query returned the intended admitted conversation before using its result. A missing or ambiguous conversation is unavailable. Memory results give textContent, source identity/provenance, revision, range and optional nextStart; use the same record and memory revisions for more. They explicitly say stored_memory_not_original_bytes. A document’s retained memory can remain readable after its original bytes are gone; unavailable or unprovable memories require existing full context or re-sharing. This grants no original-file download or image pixels. Exact retained-memory addresses with both current revisions can be read in a new authenticated command; upload IDs cannot. Changed stored memory, conversation, privacy, Flow/storage authority, permission or cancellation refuses publication. A memory ID cannot select an uploaded file, and an upload ID cannot select retained memory. External memory reads work with native Joe Off. Native CLI brains use only their exact active turn’s conversation; guests and scheduled runs do not inherit this access.

title: CLI action reference
header: Ask someone at FlowJoe to choose a file — request_file
content: Show the app’s file request card; the chosen file is imported into the currently selected node. This uses the regular import flow, including supported formats that upload_attachment does not accept. Keep the user on the intended node. Changes and approval: Requires a person to choose a file in FlowJoe. —autoapprove does not answer the picker; importing changes the gallery. Input Required? Meaning prompt Yes What file you need and why — shown verbatim to the user on the card. title No Optional title for the imported gallery entry (defaults to the file’s own name). { "prompt": "Choose the reference document to add to the selected node." } flowjoe-cli action request_file --file input.json --json Result: File name, media type and whether it was placed, or the user’s decline. It does not return file bytes.

title: CLI action reference
header: Show a node in the app — select_node
content: Move FlowJoe’s selection and gallery to an existing node. Alternatively use name for an exact case-insensitive name; duplicate names require a nodeId. Changes and approval: Changes the visible selection immediately; no Flow edit approval or data edit. Input Required? Meaning nodeId No The target node’s id (from get_flow_snapshot). Preferred over name — exact and never ambiguous. name No The target node’s exact display name (case-insensitive). Refuses ambiguous_name if more than one node has this exact name. { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID" } flowjoe-cli action select_node --file input.json --json Result: Navigation success or a not-found/ambiguous-name refusal.

title: CLI action reference
content: Control the header player. The action choices and examples below cover playback, mode and saved playlists. Accessible audio only; this is not a transcript or general media editor. Changes and approval: Immediate playback/UI action; no approval card. save_playlist saves a playlist. Flow edit undo does not revert player actions. Input Required? Meaning action Yes What to do with the header player. Choices: show, hide, play, pause, set_mode, play_once, play_tagged, save_playlist, load. playlist No Saved playlist name for action load. Exact match, case-insensitive. Do not combine with nodeId. nodeId No Node id whose audio should load (load), whose one file should play (play_once), or whose tagged audio should be searched/saved (play_tagged/save_playlist with tagId). Do not combine with playlist. play No With action load, true starts playback. Omit or false loads the source and leaves playback paused. mode No Playback mode for action set_mode. Sequential repeats the queue in order; shuffle randomizes track order; repeat-one loops the current track. Choices: sequential, shuffle, repeat-one. slotIndex No 0-based gallery slot index for action play_once. itemIndex No 0-based item index inside a stack for action play_once. Required when that slot contains multiple audio files. tagId No Exact visible user tag id from get_flow_snapshot’s top-level tags dictionary, for action play_tagged or to save matching audio in action save_playlist. playlistName No User-provided name for a new playlist saved from the current queue or tagId source, for action save_playlist. Duplicate names are refused. { "action": "pause" } flowjoe-cli action control_global_player --file input.json --json Result: Player action success/state, or an unavailable/invalid-source error.

title: CLI action reference
header: List changes made by this command — list_recent_changes
content: Read only this connection’s change history, including approval status. Put it after editing steps in one run list. A separate CLI command starts fresh and cannot report the previous command’s history. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning limit No Maximum 50; default 50. Only this connection’s changes. { "limit": 10 } Use this as a step in the same run list as its prerequisite: { "action": "list_recent_changes", "input": { "limit": 10 } } Result: A changes list for this connection, cleared when it closes.

title: CLI action reference
header: Check a request from this command — get_approval_outcome
content: Advanced: read the outcome of an approval created in this same connection. The CLI already polls ordinary patch approvals, so most users do not need this action. You cannot use a new CLI invocation to resume a previous request. Changes and approval: Read only; no approval. Input Required? Meaning approvalId Yes Approval ID from this same connection. { "approvalId": "YOUR_APPROVAL_ID" } Use this as a step in the same run list as its prerequisite: { "action": "get_approval_outcome", "input": { "approvalId": "YOUR_APPROVAL_ID" } } Result: The current pending, applied, rejected or failed outcome, or a refusal for an unknown/foreign request.

title: CLI action reference
header: Undo this command’s last applied change — undo_last_change
content: Use after an edit in the SAME run list. It refuses if the Flow changed afterwards, rather than overwriting somebody else’s work. It does not undo a previous CLI invocation, a player action or another agent’s edit. Changes and approval: Changes the Flow immediately through the existing undo guard; no new patch approval card. Inputs: none. Use this as a step in the same run list as its prerequisite: { "action": "undo_last_change", "input": {} } Result: Whether a change was undone, or nothing_to_undo/changed_since refusal.

title: CLI action reference
content: Save each input below as input.json, then run flowjoe-cli action control_global_player --file input.json --json. Goal JSON input Show the player {"action":"show"} Hide it and stop playback {"action":"hide"} Play the loaded queue, or the first accessible playlist if empty {"action":"play"} Pause {"action":"pause"} Shuffle the loaded queue {"action":"set_mode","mode":"shuffle"} Play sequentially and repeat the queue {"action":"set_mode","mode":"sequential"} Repeat the current track {"action":"set_mode","mode":"repeat-one"} Load a saved playlist and start playing {"action":"load","playlist":"My playlist","play":true} Load a node’s audio, staying paused {"action":"load","nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","play":false} Play one audio item once {"action":"play_once","nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0} Play one member of an audio stack {"action":"play_once","nodeId":"YOUR_NODE_ID","slotIndex":0,"itemIndex":1} Play audio with a tag {"action":"play_tagged","tagId":"YOUR_TAG_ID"} Save the current queue {"action":"save_playlist","playlistName":"My playlist"} Save tagged audio without changing playback {"action":"save_playlist","tagId":"YOUR_TAG_ID","playlistName":"Research music"} load takes either playlist or nodeId, never both. play_tagged and tag-based save_playlist can add nodeId to limit their search. Playlist names match exactly ignoring case, and saving refuses duplicate names instead of overwriting them. Read real tag IDs from the snapshot.

title: CLI action reference
header: Supported staging kinds and file limits
content: The live staging catalog lists image, PDF, document, audio and video, plus spreadsheet, rich-document and calendar kinds. The external bridge currently cannot stage spreadsheet, rich-document or calendar content, including an uploaded CSV selected as kind spreadsheet. Those importers need a file-attachment handle, while this bridge passes uploaded content to staging as a data URL. Use request_file and the normal app importer for those workbench types. The external upload action also accepts only the image/text MIME types listed above. PDF, Word, audio and video files cannot be uploaded through upload_attachment; use the normal file chooser for them. A raw dataUrl can prepare a supported non-workbench kind when its MIME and size are valid; it does not bypass the workbench restriction. Do not invent an attachment ID or relabel a file’s MIME type. Staging is preparation, not placement; see the working example.

title: CLI action reference
content: For transcribe_audio, pass startSeconds and endSeconds alongside the source identities. For example, startSeconds: 0 and endSeconds: 60 transcribes only the first minute. The audio is clipped before recognition or upload; the source file is unchanged. The completed result includes the actual time range.

title: Change nodes
content: Create, organize, tag, freeze, and write notes on FlowJoe nodes. Reading a node conversation’s retained attachment memory uses the memory read action; it does not add a node editing verb. Repository inspection uses separate read actions; these node editing verbs do not grant repository file editing or commands. Repository file text changes use the gallery verb editRepoFileText. Every example below is a separate change. Save its JSON as changes.json, replace all YOUR_… placeholders with IDs from your current Flow, and run: flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --preview --json flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --json The first command checks without applying. The second follows FlowJoe’s approval rules. Add --autoapprove to the second command to skip all approval cards, including deletions, for that command. Permissions, privacy, frozen content and validation still apply. All verbs on these pages change data; none is a read command. A successful patch reports applied and operation results; a failed operation rolls back that patch. See results and exit codes. A gallery position (slotIndex, index, sourceIndex, fromIndex, toIndex) starts at 0: 0 means first, 1 means second. An itemIndex selects a member inside a stack, also from 0. Only use examples whose targets exist and have the required content type. Examples with two or three positions need at least that many items. Read fresh data after an edit that changes positions. The required inputs below come from the editing catalog measured on 2026-10-20: 62 verb names for 61 distinct changes, because setNodeReadOnly is an older name for setNodeFrozen (discover the running build’s catalog for updates). Where an alternative stable entry ID is listed, supply that instead of its positional field, not both. Read IDs with a gallery snapshot; not every verb supports the same ID alternative. removeEntryContexts uses nested positional references. The live catalog is authoritative for your installed desktop version: flowjoe-cli action

title: Change nodes
content: action describe_patch_protocol --json Prepared-entry examples containing $result belong inside a run action list, after a step saved as prepared; they cannot be pasted unchanged into a standalone apply file. See the complete upload → prepare → place example. Replace that example’s final ops with the operation shown here. Never invent a stored-media key.

title: Change nodes
content: Add a child under an existing node. Use position root without parentId for a new top-level node. For sibling-after (or sibling), parentId identifies the sibling to insert after. values accepts name, status, skipPlaceholder and id; put notes in a separate setNodeSummary operation. Required inputs: position, values. [ { "verb": "createNode", "args": { "position": "child", "parentId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "values": { "name": "Research" } } } ] Result: The new node is created; its ID appears in the operation result.

title: Change nodes
header: Rename or change a node — updateNode
content: Change name, status, theme, collapsed, hidden or hiddenFromJoe in patch. Notes use setNodeSummary. A theme must be an ID from the live catalog’s nodeThemes. Hiding content from Joe can make later CLI reads or edits unavailable; this channel cannot reveal sealed content. Required inputs: nodeId, patch. [ { "verb": "updateNode", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "patch": { "name": "Research notes" } } } ] Result: The selected fields change on the node.

title: Change nodes
content: Replace the node’s notes (called summary in returned data). An empty string clears them. This does not edit a document in the gallery. Required inputs: nodeId, value. [ { "verb": "setNodeSummary", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "value": "Questions to investigate next." } } ] Result: The node’s summary contains the supplied text.

title: Change nodes
header: Delete a node and its branch — deleteNode
content: Remove this node and all its descendants. This is a deletion, including the branch’s references; inspect the branch first. Required inputs: nodeId. [ { "verb": "deleteNode", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID" } } ] Result: The branch is removed.

title: Change nodes
content: Remove the nodes listed in ids and their descendants. These are node IDs, not names. This is a deletion. Required inputs: ids. [ { "verb": "deleteNodes", "args": { "ids": [ "YOUR_NODE_ID", "OTHER_NODE_ID" ] } } ] Result: The selected branches are removed together.

title: Change nodes
content: Move under another node with child, beside it with before or after, or to the top level with root (no targetId needed). A branch cannot move into itself or one of its descendants. Required inputs: nodeId, options. [ { "verb": "moveNode", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "options": { "position": "child", "targetId": "OTHER_NODE_ID" } } } ] Result: The branch moves with its descendants and references.

title: Change nodes
content: Use the same options as moveNode, with ids identifying the branches to move together. Required inputs: ids, options. [ { "verb": "moveNodes", "args": { "ids": [ "YOUR_NODE_ID" ], "options": { "position": "child", "targetId": "OTHER_NODE_ID" } } } ] Result: The branches move to the requested destination.

title: Change nodes
content: Apply the same patch to every listed node. Allowed patch fields are name, status, theme, collapsed, hidden and hiddenFromJoe; giving name renames every listed node to that name. Required inputs: ids, patch. [ { "verb": "updateNodes", "args": { "ids": [ "YOUR_NODE_ID", "OTHER_NODE_ID" ], "patch": { "collapsed": true } } } ] Result: Each selected node receives the same fields.

title: Change nodes
content: Duplicate the selected branch beside its original. The copied nodes receive their own identities. Required inputs: sourceNodeId. [ { "verb": "duplicateNode", "args": { "sourceNodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID" } } ] Result: A second branch is created; the source stays in place.

title: Change nodes
header: Freeze a node using the older name — setNodeReadOnly
content: Accepted older spelling of setNodeFrozen. Use locked here, rather than frozen. Set false to request unfreezing, subject to the current permission rules. Required inputs: nodeId, locked. [ { "verb": "setNodeReadOnly", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "locked": true } } ] Result: The node’s Freeze state changes if permitted.

title: Change nodes
header: Freeze or unfreeze a node — setNodeFrozen
content: Set frozen true to protect a node from edits, or false to request unfreezing. Inherited or other protections can still prevent a change. Required inputs: nodeId, frozen. [ { "verb": "setNodeFrozen", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "frozen": true } } ] Result: The node’s Freeze state changes if permitted.

title: Change nodes
content: Use tag IDs from a snapshot’s tags dictionary. The list replaces the existing tags; an empty array clears them. A tag name created earlier in the same patch can also be resolved. Required inputs: nodeId, tagIds. [ { "verb": "setNodeTags", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "tagIds": [ "YOUR_TAG_ID" ] } } ] Result: The node has the supplied tag list.

title: Change nodes
content: Supply a tree of named nodes and optional children arrays. Placement follows createNode, including parentId for child or sibling placement. The tree is limited to 500 nodes and 20 levels. Required inputs: position, tree. [ { "verb": "createSubtree", "args": { "position": "root", "tree": { "name": "Project", "children": [ { "name": "Research" }, { "name": "Delivery" } ] } } } ] Result: The new branch is created together.

title: Change nodes
header: Sort a level of the tree — sortNodes
content: Sort this parent’s children by name or number; direction is asc or desc. Omit parentId (or use root) to sort top-level nodes. Numbers are parsed from names; names without numbers go last. Required inputs: none; the example supplies optional sorting choices. [ { "verb": "sortNodes", "args": { "parentId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "by": "name", "direction": "asc" } } ] Result: That one level is reordered; descendants stay attached.

title: Change references and stacks

Use the memory read action for saved conversation evidence; it does not recover original gallery bytes. A repository-backed gallery file can be inspected with read_repo_file. The one repository change is editRepoFileText: one exact text change to one existing file, held for your review unless you started the session with --autoapprove. No gallery verb gives terminal access, commits or pushes. Every example below is a separate change. title: Change references and stacks
content: not every verb supports the same ID alternative. removeEntryContexts uses nested positional references. The live catalog is authoritative for your installed desktop version: flowjoe-cli action describe_patch_protocol --json Prepared-entry examples containing $result belong inside a run action list, after a step saved as prepared; they cannot be pasted unchanged into a standalone apply file. See the complete upload → prepare → place example. Replace that example’s final ops with the operation shown here. Never invent a stored-media key.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Move a gallery item within its node — moveSlotWithinNode
content: Move one gallery position to another. Read current positions first; both indices start at zero. Required inputs: nodeId, fromIndex, toIndex. Stable IDs: fromEntryId can replace fromIndex; toEntryId can replace toIndex. [ { "verb": "moveSlotWithinNode", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "fromIndex": 0, "toIndex": 1 } } ] Result: The gallery order changes.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Set the complete gallery order — reorderSlots
content: Give every current gallery index exactly once, in the desired order. This two-item example requires exactly two gallery items. Required inputs: nodeId, order. Stable IDs: orderEntryIds can replace order. [ { "verb": "reorderSlots", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "order": [ 1, 0 ] } } ] Result: The gallery takes the supplied order.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Sort by title or number, in asc or desc order. Numbers are parsed from titles; items without numbers go last. Required inputs: nodeId. [ { "verb": "sortSlots", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "by": "title", "direction": "asc" } } ] Result: The node’s gallery is sorted.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Delete the listed gallery positions. Deleting a stack removes its contents too. This is a deletion. Required inputs: nodeId, indices. Stable IDs: slotEntryIds can replace indices. [ { "verb": "deleteSlots", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "indices": [ 0 ] } } ] Result: The selected gallery items are removed.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Add prepared references to a gallery — addImageSlots
content: Despite its older name, this adds supported prepared references, not only images. Prepare entries with stage_media or generate_image in the same run list. Optional index chooses insertion position; omitted means append. The result reference in this example requires the prepared step in the scripting guide. Required inputs: nodeId, entries. [ { "verb": "addImageSlots", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "entries": [ { "$result": "prepared", "path": [ "entry" ] } ] } } ] Result: The prepared references appear as new gallery items.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Replace one item using a prepared entry from an earlier step in the same run list. This overwrites the current reference; it is not a title or notes edit. Required inputs: nodeId, index, entry. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace index. [ { "verb": "replaceImageSlot", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "index": 0, "entry": { "$result": "prepared", "path": [ "entry" ] } } } ] Result: The gallery position contains the prepared replacement.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Move a reference to another node — moveImageSlotToNode
content: Move the complete gallery item, including a stack if the selected item is a stack. Required inputs: sourceNodeId, sourceIndex, targetNodeId. Stable IDs: sourceEntryId can replace sourceIndex. [ { "verb": "moveImageSlotToNode", "args": { "sourceNodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "sourceIndex": 0, "targetNodeId": "OTHER_NODE_ID" } } ] Result: The reference leaves the source and appears in the destination.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Move several references to another node — moveImageSlots
content: Move the selected gallery items together; each index refers to the source gallery before this operation. Required inputs: sourceNodeId, indices, targetNodeId. Stable IDs: slotEntryIds can replace indices. [ { "verb": "moveImageSlots", "args": { "sourceNodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "indices": [ 0, 1 ], "targetNodeId": "OTHER_NODE_ID" } } ] Result: The references move to the destination gallery.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Delete specific gallery or stack occurrences — removeEntryContexts
content: For precise deletion across nodes, give contextRefs with nodeId and slotIndex; add entryIndex for a stack member. This nested field is entryIndex, not itemIndex. Linked original/derived relationships are handled by the app’s deletion rules. This is a deletion. Required inputs: contextRefs. [ { "verb": "removeEntryContexts", "args": { "contextRefs": [ { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } ] } } ] Result: The specified occurrences are removed.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Unlink derived copies from their original — detachDerivedEntries
content: Identify the original entry. Add entryIndex to identify an original inside a stack. Its derived copies are detached from that original; content is retained. Every affected node must be editable. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace entryIndex. [ { "verb": "detachDerivedEntries", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } } ] Result: Derived copies become independent; the result includes a detached count.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Write a reference’s title or notes — setSlotFields
content: fields accepts title, notes and audioTitle (audio only). To edit a stack member, add options with itemIndex, for example options: {itemIndex: 0}. An empty notes string clears notes. This edits reference notes, not the file’s stored text. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, fields. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "setSlotFields", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "fields": { "notes": "Reviewed for the next meeting." } } } ] Result: The chosen reference fields change.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Replace tags on a gallery item or stack container. Tags do not belong to individual stack members. An empty array clears them. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, tagIds. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "setSlotTags", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "tagIds": [ "YOUR_TAG_ID" ] } } ] Result: The reference has the supplied tags.

title: Change references and stacks
content: The target must be a spreadsheet. Choose cell such as B3, or row and column (both zero-based). Optional itemIndex targets a spreadsheet inside a stack. This changes one cell, not a whole workbook. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, value. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "setSpreadsheetCell", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "cell": "B3", "value": "Ready" } } ] Result: The cell contains the supplied value.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Copy a complete gallery item. Omit targetNodeId to copy within the source node; optional targetIndex chooses placement. The copy receives new entry IDs. Required inputs: sourceNodeId, sourceIndex. Stable IDs: sourceEntryId can replace sourceIndex. [ { "verb": "copyImageSlot", "args": { "sourceNodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "sourceIndex": 0, "targetNodeId": "OTHER_NODE_ID" } } ] Result: A copy appears; the original remains. Copying a virtual slot makes another virtual slot of the same master.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Show a slot in another node — addVirtualSlot
content: Add a virtual slot to a node: it shows an existing slot (its master) and stores no content of its own. masterEntryId is the master slot’s entry ID from anywhere in the Flow; naming a virtual slot points at its master. Optional slotIndex chooses the position (default: the end). Refused into a frozen or Private node, for a master that isn’t in the Flow or sits in a Private node, and for a master in a node hidden from Joe. Required inputs: nodeId, masterEntryId. [ { "verb": "addVirtualSlot", "args": { "nodeId": "OTHER_NODE_ID", "masterEntryId": "MASTER_ENTRY_ID" } } ] Result: A virtual slot appears in the node, showing the master. Changing the master changes it too.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Turn a virtual slot into its own slot — makeVirtualSlotReal
content: Make Real Slot: the virtual slot becomes a real copy of its master as it is now, with its own copy of every file, and keeps its place. Refused when the slot isn’t a virtual slot, its master is missing, Private or in a node hidden from Joe, or a file can’t be copied. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "makeVirtualSlotReal", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } } ] Result: The slot no longer changes with the master.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Remove a master slot that has virtual slots — removeVirtualMaster
content: deleteSlots and deleteNode refuse a master that still has virtual slots elsewhere. Use this instead: when you approve it, FlowJoe shows the Remove Master Slot window in the app, and you choose whether one of its virtual slots becomes the new master or they are all removed. Any mode an assistant sends is ignored and the removal is held for your choice. A session started with --autoapprove applies its own mode (promote with promoteEntryId, or remove) without asking and opens nothing in the app; without a mode it is refused. It is held for review like other removals, and refused when one of its virtual slots is in a frozen node or a node hidden from Joe. Required inputs: nodeId, entryId. [ { "verb": "removeVirtualMaster", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "entryId": "MASTER_ENTRY_ID" } } ] Result: The master is gone and its virtual slots were handled as you chose.

title: Change references and stacks
content: The target must be a supported stored image. Coordinates are fractions of the original image, from 0 to 1; the rectangle must fit inside it. Optional itemIndex targets a stack member. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, x, y, width, height. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "cropImage", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "x": 0.1, "y": 0.1, "width": 0.8, "height": 0.8 } } ] Result: A crop is applied using the app’s image workflow.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Create a PDF from an image or note — convertToPdf
content: Convert a supported image or note-like item using the installed PDF service. Optional itemIndex targets a stack member. This is not a general converter for every file format. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "convertToPdf", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } } ] Result: A new PDF reference is inserted beside the source; the source remains.

title: Change references and stacks
content: This example clears the cover. To set one, use coverSrc from a prepared, stored image (an indexeddb: source), not an arbitrary web URL; optional itemIndex targets audio in a stack. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, coverSrc. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex.
