[ { "verb": "setAudioCover", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "coverSrc": "" } } ] Result: The audio cover is cleared or replaced.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Set a gallery item’s color using a supported hex color. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, color. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "setSlotColor", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "color": "#336699" } } ] Result: The reference color changes.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Place an item on the canvas — setSlotCanvasPlacement
content: Supply x, y or customWidth (at least one). Positions are canvas coordinates; customWidth is non-negative, with zero clearing the custom width. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "setSlotCanvasPlacement", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "x": 100, "y": 200, "customWidth": 320 } } ] Result: The item’s saved canvas placement changes.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Add a connection between two gallery items in the same node. Required inputs: nodeId, fromIndex, toIndex. Stable IDs: fromEntryId can replace fromIndex; toEntryId can replace toIndex. [ { "verb": "connectSlots", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "fromIndex": 0, "toIndex": 1 } } ] Result: The canvas connection is added.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Remove the connection between two gallery items in the same node. Required inputs: nodeId, fromIndex, toIndex. Stable IDs: fromEntryId can replace fromIndex; toEntryId can replace toIndex. [ { "verb": "disconnectSlots", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "fromIndex": 0, "toIndex": 1 } } ] Result: The connection is removed; both items remain.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Move an item within a stack — reorderStackItem
content: slotIndex identifies the stack; fromIndex and toIndex identify its members, starting at zero. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, fromIndex, toIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; fromItemEntryId can replace fromIndex; toItemEntryId can replace toIndex. [ { "verb": "reorderStackItem", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "fromIndex": 0, "toIndex": 1 } } ] Result: The stack’s item order changes.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Choose the displayed stack item — setStackActiveItem
content: Choose which existing member the stack displays. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, itemIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "setStackActiveItem", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "itemIndex": 1 } } ] Result: The selected member becomes active.

title: Change references and stacks
content: Delete a member, retaining the other members. Small stacks can collapse back to a plain gallery item. This is a deletion. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, itemIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "removeStackItem", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "itemIndex": 0 } } ] Result: The member is removed.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Keep only the active stack item — flattenStackSlot
content: Replace a stack with its currently active member and discard the others. This is a deletion of the other members; use extractAllStackItems to retain them instead. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex. [ { "verb": "flattenStackSlot", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } } ] Result: One plain gallery item remains in place of the stack.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Add prepared entries to a stack — addEntriesToSlot
content: Append prepared entries, converting a plain item to a stack when needed. Use a prepared result from the same run list. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, entries. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "addEntriesToSlot", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "entries": [ { "$result": "prepared", "path": [ "entry" ] } ] } } ] Result: The entries join the stack.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Insert prepared entries at a stack position — insertEntriesIntoStack
content: Insert prepared entries at options.itemIndex. Omit it to insert after the active item. options.makeActive defaults true. A plain item is converted to a stack first. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, entries. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "insertEntriesIntoStack", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "entries": [ { "$result": "prepared", "path": [ "entry" ] } ], "options": { "itemIndex": 0, "makeActive": true } } } ] Result: The entries are inserted at the chosen position.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Pull one stack member into the gallery — extractStackItemToSlot
content: Move a member out of its stack into a separate gallery position. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex, itemIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "extractStackItemToSlot", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "itemIndex": 0 } } ] Result: The member becomes a standalone reference.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Unpack a stack without deleting its members — extractAllStackItems
content: Turn the stack’s members into separate gallery items. Required inputs: nodeId, slotIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "extractAllStackItems", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0 } } ] Result: The members appear separately in the gallery.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Move a stack member to another node — moveStackItemToNode
content: Move one member out of a source stack into another node’s gallery. Required inputs: sourceNodeId, slotIndex, itemIndex, targetNodeId. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "moveStackItemToNode", "args": { "sourceNodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "itemIndex": 0, "targetNodeId": "OTHER_NODE_ID" } } ] Result: The member leaves the stack and appears in the destination.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Copy a stack member into the gallery — copyStackItem
content: Copy one member as a standalone gallery item. Omit targetNodeId for a copy within the source node; optional targetIndex chooses placement. Required inputs: sourceNodeId, slotIndex, itemIndex. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex; itemEntryId can replace itemIndex. [ { "verb": "copyStackItem", "args": { "sourceNodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "slotIndex": 0, "itemIndex": 0, "targetNodeId": "OTHER_NODE_ID" } } ] Result: A copy appears; the original stack member remains.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Combine two gallery items into a stack — mergeSlotsIntoStack
content: Merge the source gallery item into the target, converting the target to a stack when needed. Required inputs: nodeId, sourceIndex, targetIndex. Stable IDs: sourceEntryId can replace sourceIndex; targetEntryId can replace targetIndex. [ { "verb": "mergeSlotsIntoStack", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "sourceIndex": 0, "targetIndex": 1 } } ] Result: One combined stack replaces the separate items.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Collect several gallery items into one stack — consolidateSlotsIntoStack
content: Choose the target gallery position and the selected indices. Omit indices to consolidate every gallery item into the target. Required inputs: nodeId, targetIndex. Stable IDs: targetEntryId can replace targetIndex; slotEntryIds can replace indices. [ { "verb": "consolidateSlotsIntoStack", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "targetIndex": 0, "indices": [ 0, 1, 2 ] } } ] Result: The selected items are combined in the target stack.

title: Change references and stacks
header: Change text in one repository file — editRepoFileText
content: Propose one exact text change to one existing repository file. It must be the only change in its request, so send it on its own. Scheduled tasks and guest sessions cannot use it. Required inputs: nodeId, entryId, source (saved or draft), expectedOid, oldText, newText. Optional: repoNodeId, and draftVersion when source is draft. Read the file first with read_repo_file using the same source, and copy its oid into expectedOid (and, for a draft, its draftVersion). oldText must appear exactly once in the saved file, or in the open unsaved editor draft when source is draft. A draft edit needs that repository editor tab to be open in FlowJoe; a historical revision cannot be edited. Requires Propose access. [ { "verb": "editRepoFileText", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "entryId": "YOUR_FILE_ENTRY_ID", "source": "saved", "expectedOid": "YOUR_FILE_OID", "oldText": "retries = 3", "newText": "retries = 5" } } ] Result: Held for your review on the approval card, which shows the exact before/after, even when FlowJoe’s Auto-apply setting is on — unless you started this CLI command with --autoapprove, which approves its changes for you. Applying saves the file in FlowJoe only; it does not write your working folder and makes no commit or push. Undo (undo_last_change in the same run list) restores the previous version unless the file was saved again or the open editor tab has newer typing. --preview changes nothing and reports the same refusals the change would get: whether the request is valid, sent alone, and whether oldText appears exactly once in the current saved file or open draft. An ordinary proposal is checked the same way before any card appears, so a stale or non-matching edit is refused right away instead of waiting for review. The card’s own preview and Apply check again; if the file was saved or typed in after the card appeared, Approve stays unavailable or Apply writes nothing, and you reject the card and propose a fresh edit. Refusals: file_edit_must_be_alone,

title: Change references and stacks
header: Change text in one repository file — editRepoFileText
content: file_edit_must_be_alone, old_text_not_found, old_text_not_unique, draft_changed, changed_meanwhile, not_a_repository_file, editing_blocked (the file is Frozen, Private or read-only) and no_change. For a master removal in an explicit --autoapprove session, send mode: "remove" or mode: "promote" with promoteEntryId. If you omit the choice, virtual_slot_mode_required asks you to send it.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: Edit Flow notes, tags, saved memories, and scheduled tasks. The attachment-memory read mode is separate from saved Joe memories and their editing verbs. It grants no memory mutation or scheduler access. Repository read access is separate from Flow edits and scheduled execution. Repository readers do not opt scheduled runs into an ambient editor or browser source. Every example below is a separate change. Save its JSON as changes.json, replace all YOUR_… placeholders with IDs from your current Flow, and run: flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --preview --json flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --json The first command checks without applying. The second follows FlowJoe’s approval rules. Add --autoapprove to the second command to skip all approval cards, including deletions, for that command. Permissions, privacy, frozen content and validation still apply. All verbs on these pages change data; none is a read command. A successful patch reports applied and operation results; a failed operation rolls back that patch. See results and exit codes. A gallery position (slotIndex, index, sourceIndex, fromIndex, toIndex) starts at 0: 0 means first, 1 means second. An itemIndex selects a member inside a stack, also from 0. Only use examples whose targets exist and have the required content type. Examples with two or three positions need at least that many items. Read fresh data after an edit that changes positions. The required inputs below come from the editing catalog measured on 2026-10-20: 62 verb names for 61 distinct changes, because setNodeReadOnly is an older name for setNodeFrozen (discover the running build’s catalog for updates). Where an alternative stable entry ID is listed, supply that instead of its positional field, not both. Read IDs with a gallery snapshot; not every verb supports the same ID alternative. removeEntryContexts uses nested positional references. The live catalog is authoritative for your installed desktop version: flowjoe-cli action

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: action describe_patch_protocol --json Prepared-entry examples containing $result belong inside a run action list, after a step saved as prepared; they cannot be pasted unchanged into a standalone apply file. See the complete upload → prepare → place example. Replace that example’s final ops with the operation shown here. Never invent a stored-media key.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: Optional color and description describe the tag. An existing tag with the same name is reused. Read tag IDs from the snapshot’s tags dictionary. Required inputs: name. [ { "verb": "createTag", "args": { "name": "Research", "color": "#336699" } } ] Result: The tag is created or identified as already existing.

title: Change Flow details and automations
header: Rename or recolor a tag — updateTag
content: Supply tagId plus name, color or description. This changes the shared tag definition wherever it is used. Required inputs: tagId. [ { "verb": "updateTag", "args": { "tagId": "YOUR_TAG_ID", "name": "Reviewed" } } ] Result: The tag definition changes.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: Delete the tag definition and remove its assignments. This is a deletion; the tagged nodes and references remain. Required inputs: tagId. [ { "verb": "deleteTag", "args": { "tagId": "YOUR_TAG_ID" } } ] Result: The tag is removed.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: Set the open Flow’s title. Required inputs: title. [ { "verb": "editFlowTitle", "args": { "title": "Launch research" } } ] Result: The Flow title changes.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: Replace the Flow-level notes. An empty string clears them. These differ from a node’s summary. Required inputs: summary. [ { "verb": "editFlowSummary", "args": { "summary": "Research and decisions for the launch." } } ] Result: The Flow’s summary changes.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: text is required. scope is flow (default), node or slot; node and slot scopes also need nodeId, and slot needs slotIndex or slotEntryId. Optional title and type describe the memory. Memory writes normally receive extra review. Required inputs: text. Stable IDs: slotEntryId can replace slotIndex. [ { "verb": "createMemory", "args": { "text": "Use British spelling in this Flow.", "scope": "flow" } } ] Result: A saved memory is created; its ID is returned in the memory operation result.

title: Change Flow details and automations
header: Delete a saved Joe memory — deleteMemory
content: Find the real ID with list_joe_memories first. This is a deletion and normally receives extra review. Required inputs: memoryId. [ { "verb": "deleteMemory", "args": { "memoryId": "YOUR_MEMORY_ID" } } ] Result: The saved memory is removed.

title: Change Flow details and automations
header: Enable or disable a Joe memory — setMemoryStatus
content: Use active or disabled. Find the ID with list_joe_memories first. This normally receives extra review. Required inputs: memoryId, status. [ { "verb": "setMemoryStatus", "args": { "memoryId": "YOUR_MEMORY_ID", "status": "disabled" } } ] Result: The memory’s active state changes.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: task needs a nonempty title, nodeId and instruction. See the schedule and policy options below. Creation can adopt existing gallery output for the task. Task changes normally receive extra review. Required inputs: task. [ { "verb": "createSchedulerTask", "args": { "task": { "title": "Daily review", "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "instruction": "Summarize the open questions in this node.", "schedule": { "cadence": "daily", "time": "09:00", "timezone": "America/Denver" }, "policy": { "approvalMode": "propose-only" } } } } ] Result: The automation is created; its task ID is included in the scheduler result.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: patch accepts title, schedule, instruction, policy and slotEntryIds. Use setSchedulerTaskEnabled for enabled state. Find taskId with list_scheduled_tasks; task edits normally receive extra review. Required inputs: taskId, patch. [ { "verb": "updateSchedulerTask", "args": { "taskId": "YOUR_TASK_ID", "patch": { "title": "Morning review" } } } ] Result: The automation’s supplied fields change.

title: Change Flow details and automations
header: Turn an automation on or off — setSchedulerTaskEnabled
content: Use true to enable or false to disable. This changes future task runs; it is not a command to run a task immediately. Task changes normally receive extra review. Required inputs: taskId, enabled. [ { "verb": "setSchedulerTaskEnabled", "args": { "taskId": "YOUR_TASK_ID", "enabled": false } } ] Result: The enabled state changes.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: Find the ID with list_scheduled_tasks first. This is a deletion and normally receives extra review. Required inputs: taskId. [ { "verb": "deleteSchedulerTask", "args": { "taskId": "YOUR_TASK_ID" } } ] Result: The automation is deleted.

title: Change Flow details and automations
content: For createSchedulerTask, task accepts title, nodeId, instruction, schedule, policy, useWebSearch, slotEntryIds and guest. Ordinary owner scripts should omit guest; it attaches an existing guest invite identity and is not a way to create a share or gain permissions. schedule accepts: Choice Inputs Daily cadence: "daily", time: "09:00", optional IANA timezone Weekly cadence: "weekly", time, dayOfWeek (0 Sunday through 6 Saturday), optional timezone Interval cadence: "interval", everyMinutes (integer 1–10080) When omitted, cadence is daily, time is 07:00, and timezone is the user’s local timezone. missedRunPolicy is run-on-next-launch (default) or skip. policy accepts approvalMode (propose-only or auto-apply), autoApplyDestructive, replaceOnlyOwnedOutput, maxCreatedSlots, minCreatedSlots, allowedEntryTypes, allowedVerbs, requireUrls and requireNotes. These describe future task runs. The CLI’s --autoapprove only bypasses approval for the current CLI command; it does not make future automation runs unattended. Private/frozen-target permission escalation is not supported here. slotEntryIds can focus a task on existing entries in its target node; unknown IDs are dropped rather than creating new references. useWebSearch controls whether the task requests web search. For createMemory, type defaults to fact; inspect the app’s memory guide before selecting other types. Read back saved memories or tasks to verify their actual IDs and states: flowjoe-cli action list_joe_memories --json flowjoe-cli action list_scheduled_tasks --json

title: CLI scripting and action lists
content: Use JSON, pipes and shared results in repeatable FlowJoe workflows. Retained attachment memory uses exact history and memory revisions plus nextStart, rather than a session cursor. Both revisions are rechecked on every read, including a new command. Upload IDs remain connection-local. Repository nextCursor values belong to the same run connection. Repeat the exact file/source or repository/view selectors; a different session, changed source, privacy or editor version refuses continuation. Use --json when another program will read a command’s result: flowjoe-cli show --json flowjoe-cli search "launch plan" --json Use a JSON file with apply, or send the file through standard input: flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --preview --json cat changes.json | flowjoe-cli apply - --autoapprove --json The pipe example uses a macOS/Linux shell. In PowerShell, use Get-Content -Raw changes.json | flowjoe-cli apply - --autoapprove --json. Passing the filename directly works on all three platforms.

title: CLI scripting and action lists
content: Save an array of steps in steps.json. Each step names an action and can supply an input object: [ {"action": "search_flow", "input": {"query": "launch"}}, {"action": "get_flow_snapshot", "input": {}} ] flowjoe-cli run steps.json --json Actions run in order using one connection. The list stops at the first failed action or rejected approval. Earlier completed changes remain applied. A list is not one all-or-nothing change; put related edits in one apply request when they need to succeed together. Add --autoapprove to skip approval cards for the entire list, including deletions. Without that option, the command waits for approval in FlowJoe whenever an action needs it.

title: CLI scripting and action lists
content: Give a step a saveAs name, then use {"$result":"name","path":[...]} in a later input. The path selects fields from the first JSON text result returned by the earlier action. If it has no JSON text result, the path starts at the complete action response. This example uploads the text “Hello”, prepares it as a document, then places it in a node. Replace YOUR_NODE_ID with a node ID from show: [ { "action": "upload_attachment", "input": {"fileName": "hello.txt", "mimeType": "text/plain", "dataBase64": "SGVsbG8="}, "saveAs": "uploaded" }, { "action": "stage_media", "input": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "kind": "document", "attachmentId": {"$result": "uploaded", "path": ["attachment", "id"]} }, "saveAs": "prepared" }, { "action": "propose_flow_patch", "input": { "ops": [ { "verb": "addImageSlots", "args": { "nodeId": "YOUR_NODE_ID", "entries": [{"$result": "prepared", "path": ["entry"]}] } } ] } } ] The final step asks FlowJoe to place the prepared document in the gallery. Approve that request in the app, or run the list with flowjoe-cli run steps.json --autoapprove to skip the card. Read actions stage_media and the current change catalog when adapting the example to other content. Result references may select array items using a numeric path element. Names must start with a letter and be unique within the list.

title: CLI scripting and action lists
header: Keep related work in one connection
content: Uploaded files, recent-change history, undo and retained-history cursors belong to the connection that created them. They are cleared when the command ends. A later terminal command gets a new connection and cannot reuse those uploads or undo the earlier command’s edit. Retained chat/image/transcript/version history is separate from connection-local change history. Use query_history and read_history for retained records; keep their query/read/continuation steps in one run list. A new CLI command cannot resume a previous connection’s cursor. Use one run list for upload → prepare → place workflows, or for an edit followed by undo_last_change. Undo still refuses if the Flow changed after that connection’s last edit. This prevents a script from undoing someone else’s later work. If a command stops waiting, loses its connection or is interrupted, earlier completed steps are not rolled back. The CLI never automatically repeats a failed edit request. Read the result and check FlowJoe before running the list again.

title: CLI approvals and troubleshooting
content: Understand approval choices and resolve common connection or command problems. Memory mode needs an admitted chat recordId and its historyRevision; conversation_required means those selectors are missing. A stale memory revision requires a fresh index. Neither a memory ID nor an upload ID grants access to the other namespace. Repository reads need no approval card, but still require Read or Propose access and a currently admitted source. model_unavailable means no matching open draft/revision model exists; stale_cursor requires a fresh read in the same run connection. A repository file edit (editRepoFileText) always waits for the card, even with Auto-apply on, unless the command uses --autoapprove. An edit whose text no longer matches the file is refused before any card appears; --preview reports the same refusal without proposing anything. The card previews the exact before/after; if the file or its open draft no longer matches, Approve stays unavailable. Apply checks the file again and, if it changed at the last moment, refuses with changed_meanwhile (or draft_changed for an open draft) and writes nothing. In either case reject the card, read the file again and propose a fresh edit. Read the proposed changes before approving. This diagram explains the process; it is not a fabricated Joe response.

title: CLI approvals and troubleshooting
content: Without --autoapprove, the CLI follows the bridge’s current approval rules. When a request needs review, it says Waiting for approval in FlowJoe. Approve or reject the Agent request card in FlowJoe, then let the terminal command report the result. The default waiting time is 120 seconds; use --wait 300 if you want five minutes. The app’s existing Apply changes without asking (Agent Bridge → Advanced) setting can already let ordinary edits apply without a card. Its extra review holds still apply unless the CLI command explicitly uses --autoapprove.

title: CLI approvals and troubleshooting
header: Skip approval cards for a command
content: flowjoe-cli apply changes.json --autoapprove flowjoe-cli run steps.json --autoapprove --autoapprove skips approval cards for that command, including deletion approvals and the usual extra review of saved-memory and scheduled-task changes. Use it when you want the supplied actions to run without those confirmations. The default two-minute wait still applies with --autoapprove: there is no approval-card wait, but FlowJoe and any configured service still need time to finish. Use --wait 300 for five minutes. It does not change the app’s approval setting, affect other connected clients, or carry over to the next CLI command. Permissions, privacy protections, locked/read-only content and action validation still apply. It does not reveal content hidden from Joe or make every requested edit valid. It also does not dismiss file pickers or configure paid services for you. The CLI checks that the running app supports this choice before sending actions. If it does not, update FlowJoe. Read-only bridge connections cannot use the bypass.

title: CLI approvals and troubleshooting
content: Keep the desktop app open. Turn on Settings → Joe AI → Agent Bridge (MCP). Run flowjoe-cli status again. If you run a development app or a separate profile, point --settings-file at that profile’s mcp-bridge.json. The CLI never writes this file. Keep it private because it contains the token. The CLI normally checks the app settings folder for your platform: Application Support on macOS, AppData/Roaming on Windows, or XDG config on Linux. It tries the flow-joe, FlowJoe, and flowjoe profile names in that order. An existing disabled or damaged first profile is reported instead of silently connecting to another profile.

title: CLI approvals and troubleshooting
content: Open a new terminal. Check that npm’s global installation folder is on your PATH. You can find the prefix with npm prefix --global; on macOS/Linux the executable is in its bin folder. Do not replace the desktop app’s flowjoe launcher—the CLI command is flowjoe-cli.

title: CLI approvals and troubleshooting
content: Run flowjoe-cli actions to see the actions offered by your running app and permissions. Use flowjoe-cli actions ACTION_NAME for its input instructions. Use --json to retain the full error returned by an app action. A private or hidden item may be absent from search and reads.

title: CLI approvals and troubleshooting
header: Timed out, interrupted, or connection lost
content: Check the current Flow before trying again. An edit may already have applied even if its response was lost. The CLI does not automatically repeat it. A waiting approval card may still exist in FlowJoe after the CLI disconnects; inspect or reject it there. A new CLI command cannot resume the previous command’s approval lookup, uploaded files or undo history. For a list of actions, earlier completed changes remain in the Flow. --json includes completed step results when available. After an interrupted request, the last in-flight action may have an unconfirmed outcome; do not assume it was undone.

title: Workspace Folders
content: Save a Flow as a normal folder on your drive, so your work sits in plain files you can back up, version, and see. Normally FlowJoe keeps your Flow in its own storage inside the app. Workspace Folder mode writes it to a folder you choose instead, as ordinary files you can open, copy, and back up. Workspace Folders are available in the desktop app. Media reads stay tied to the opened Workspace folder. Replacing a media folder or file with a symbolic link does not redirect a read to files elsewhere. If a file changes during reading, FlowJoe stops that read. Closing or switching Workspaces also stops a waiting media read from being returned to the previous Flow. Hardlinked files still work. A live Workspace folder and a portable exported copy serve different purposes.

title: Workspace Folders
content: Use a Workspace Folder when you want to choose where your Flow lives and manage its files with your usual tools. You can: Keep a Flow and its media together in a folder you can find in Finder or Explorer. Back up that folder with your normal backup tools, or copy it to another drive. Move the folder to another computer and open it in FlowJoe there. Keep the Flow’s readable data under version control with a tool such as Git. You keep working in FlowJoe normally; saves go to the connected folder automatically. Local storage is enough if you prefer FlowJoe to manage storage for you. You can still export .fj packages for backups or transfers. Workspace Folders are optional, and you can switch between a Workspace and Local storage when you choose; see Switch between Workspace and Local storage. Older backups are protected automatically. When a Flow already contains private nodes, FlowJoe preserves their full content in owner-only storage, replaces it in the Workspace with redacted placeholders, and verifies the saved file before resuming saves. A copy shared or backed up before migration cannot be recalled. If an older Workspace backup still contains private text, FlowJoe does the same to that backup: your private notes stay safe on this computer and the backup keeps a placeholder. A backup that is damaged and cannot be checked is removed. Saving then resumes and a notice tells you what was done.

title: Workspace Folders
content: Open Settings → Data and look for the Workspace Folder card. Everything below happens there; there is no File menu entry or context-menu item for this. On first launch, the desktop app offers Keep FlowJoe local, Workspace Folder, and Decide later. Choosing Workspace Folder takes you to this card to select or create the folder. If you skip onboarding, the card remains available in Settings.

title: Workspace Folders
content: The card shows different buttons depending on whether a folder is connected. Button When you see it What it does New Workspace No folder connected Pick an empty folder. FlowJoe copies the current Flow and all its media there, then starts saving there. Connect Workspace No folder connected Open a folder that is already a FlowJoe workspace. Reconnect Workspace FlowJoe remembers your last folder Reconnects to it without picking again. Change Workspace A folder is connected Switch to a different workspace folder. Switch to Local Storage A folder is connected, or FlowJoe is temporarily saving locally Copies the workspace back into the app’s own storage and keeps editing there. The folder is left untouched. Disconnect Workspace A folder is connected Detaches from the folder without taking a copy of your Flow. Editing stays paused until you reconnect the folder or start a new Local Project. To keep working with your Flow, use Switch to Local Storage instead. Delete Workspace A folder is connected Removes only the files FlowJoe manages in that folder. This cannot be undone. Reveal Workspace Folder A folder is remembered Opens the folder in Finder or Explorer. When you create a workspace, FlowJoe shows its progress — “Preparing workspace…”, then “Copying media 3 of 12…” — and you can Cancel partway through. One Flow lives in one folder. New Workspace is hidden while you are already connected. Delete Workspace needs free space on the drive of about the size of the workspace, because FlowJoe first makes a temporary safety copy inside the folder. If cleanup fails afterwards, a leftover folder whose name starts with .flowjoe-delete- may remain. Once FlowJoe has reported the delete as finished, or has put the Workspace back, that folder is safe to delete. Otherwise it may hold the only copy of your Workspace, so leave it alone and open the folder in FlowJoe first; FlowJoe tidies it up when you do. If FlowJoe is closed or crashes in the middle of a delete, the next time you open

title: Workspace Folders
content: open that folder FlowJoe puts the Workspace back exactly as it was and tells you; delete it again if you still want to. Any flow.unreadable- files (see below) are not removed. The card shows the current Flow name, the selected or last-known folder path, and whether that folder is connected. Before connecting to an existing folder, FlowJoe summarizes both versions and calls out missing media references separately from files not used by the current Flow. The review makes no changes; Workspace media is not deleted automatically.

title: Workspace Folders
content: My Project Folder/ ├── flow.json Your whole Flow — tree, notes, tags, summaries — as readable JSON ├── media/ One file per image, audio file, video, and document └── .flowjoe/ FlowJoe's own bookkeeping .flowjoe/ holds backups (FlowJoe keeps the newest 20), a shareable change journal, and small per-computer notes. Each note contains that computer’s name and a timestamp, refreshed about once a minute while the workspace is open, so other computers can tell it is in use. If the folder is synced or shared, those notes travel with it. Version History and restore points stay with the app on this computer. flow.json is plain, indented JSON, so a version-control tool like Git can diff and merge it as text. media/ holds your files one per item. They are named by FlowJoe’s internal id and carry no file extension, so treat this folder as storage rather than a gallery to browse. Ordinary Joe conversations and their picture backups travel with the folder. A conversation marked Keep on this computer only, and conversations belonging to private nodes, stay on this computer. Joe Memories, standalone Image History prompts, your preferences, and browser data also stay local. Scheduled tasks (automations) and your custom placeholder picture travel with the Flow. Edit flow.json outside FlowJoe only if you know the format. If a Git merge leaves conflict markers in it, FlowJoe cannot open the workspace until you clean them out. If it becomes unreadable while the workspace is already open, see the next section.

title: Workspace Folders
content: A copy of this folder does not include the full content of Private nodes or other computer-only records. Keep the whole folder, including media/ and hidden .flowjoe/ files. For owner-only content, make an explicitly inclusive full-package export as well. See What each copy preserves before relying on a folder copy after losing a computer. Back up a Workspace Folder like any other directory: Time Machine, an external drive, or a sync client. Git can track the folder too, but that tracks the Flow’s storage files together; it is not how FlowJoe’s project repositories work.

title: Workspace Folders
header: Move a Flow to another computer
content: Let the Flow finish saving, then close FlowJoe on the source computer. Copy the whole Workspace folder, including flow.json, media/, and the hidden .flowjoe/ folder, to a local drive on the other computer. On that computer, open Settings → Data → Workspace Folder → Connect Workspace and select the copied folder. Private nodes and conversations marked Keep on this computer only stay on their original computer. Version History and restore points also stay with that computer’s app storage. Copying a Workspace moves its folder content; it does not move all of FlowJoe’s settings and local history. A Workspace Folder chooses where the Flow’s data is stored. A repo node gives one node its own Git repository for project files. Those are separate choices: repo-node files appear in the node tree and galleries and are saved through FlowJoe’s normal storage, while Git history is kept as FlowJoe-managed hidden data.To bring a project into Git in FlowJoe, create or clone a repo node from the New Node window. Do not make the whole Flow’s Workspace Folder the project repository. Each repo node has its own hidden Git history; its files remain in the Flow’s tree and galleries. See Repo nodes and Git for HTTPS and SSH remotes.

title: Workspace Folders
header: iCloud Drive, Dropbox, and Google Drive
content: You can choose a Workspace Folder inside a folder managed by the desktop app for iCloud Drive, Dropbox, or Google Drive. FlowJoe reads and saves the files through your computer’s filesystem; the sync service copies changes to and from the cloud in the background. FlowJoe does not need a separate cloud connection or upload your Workspace through those services’ APIs. Keep the whole Workspace folder downloaded, including media/ and .flowjoe/, so the files remain available while you work: iCloud Drive: in Finder, select the folder and choose Keep Downloaded where available. See Apple’s iCloud Drive guide. Dropbox: choose Make available offline for the folder. See Dropbox’s offline-files guide. Google Drive for desktop: use Mirror files, or make the Workspace folder Available offline when using streamed files. See Google’s stream and mirror guide. A file left online-only may need downloading before FlowJoe can read it. Google Drive’s streamed files may appear on a virtual drive; they are still checked through the filesystem like other Workspace folders. Saved in FlowJoe means the files were saved in the selected folder. It does not mean the sync service has finished uploading them. Before moving to another computer, finish saving, close the Workspace on the first computer, and wait for syncing to finish on both computers before opening it on the second. Editing on two computers before their files have synced can produce competing versions; FlowJoe’s outside-change review helps you choose between them. The folder paths and conflict-handling code support this arrangement. This does not claim that all three services have been verified in live end-to-end tests.

title: Workspace Folders
content: You can use a Workspace Folder on a network or shared drive. Connect the drive through Finder or Explorer first, sign in there if needed, then select the folder in FlowJoe. On Windows, a mapped drive or a UNC folder path can be used. A server address such as smb://server/share needs to be connected through your computer before you select its folder. FlowJoe checks that it can write and replace files in the folder before connecting. A network-drive label alone does not prevent connection. If the checks fail, fix the reported access or drive problem and try again. FlowJoe checks periodically for outside changes as well as listening for file-change notifications, so a drive that does not send those notifications can still be used. Outside changes may take about 15 seconds to appear. Saving also checks for outside changes before replacing the saved Flow. If the drive becomes unavailable or refuses a save, FlowJoe continues saving locally and reconnects automatically when it can. See Switch between Workspace and Local storage for the available recovery choices. Network devices vary; passing the checks does not certify every device’s behavior during a power cut or connection failure. If a sync service (Dropbox, iCloud Drive, Google Drive, OneDrive) leaves a conflict copy of flow.json in the folder, FlowJoe notices it and tells you. Replacing files inside media/ by hand is not a supported way to swap media — FlowJoe watches flow.json, not the media folder.

title: Workspace Folders
content: If flow.json changes on disk while FlowJoe is running — a sync client pulling a newer copy, or you editing it directly — FlowJoe tells you rather than silently picking a side. If the change does not collide with your work, it refreshes on its own (and tells you when the change turns up while you are saving), and any unsaved edits to your unlocked private nodes are kept. If it does, you get Someone changed this Workspace file outside FlowJoe and choose: Use External Changes — take the version on disk. Your own version, including any private nodes you have unlocked, is kept as a complete copy on this computer only. If the file changes again while FlowJoe is taking it, you are asked again instead of the newer file being accepted unseen. Keep My Changes — keep what is in FlowJoe and overwrite the file. Open External as New Flow — open the disk version separately and decide later. Decide Later — close the dialog without choosing. Folder saving stays paused, the status bar shows Outside change waiting · saving paused, and clicking it reopens the dialog. Edits you make meanwhile are kept on this computer and saved to the folder once you decide.

title: Workspace Folders
header: When the workspace file can’t be read
content: If flow.json becomes unreadable while the workspace is open (a Git merge left markers in it, a hand edit broke it, or it is too large), FlowJoe shows FlowJoe can’t read the workspace file. Your work stays safe in FlowJoe. You can: Check Again — after you fix the file. Keep My Changes — FlowJoe first saves the unreadable file next to it as flow.unreadable-<date>.json, then saves your version. Decide Later — leave saving paused for now.

title: Workspace Folders
content: If the workspace was used on another computer within the last 5 minutes, FlowJoe warns This Workspace is open on another computer before you open or reconnect it, and when you reconnect it. Choose Open here anyway or Cancel. Automatic return waits while another computer is using the folder; your work continues saving locally. Cancelling an explicit reconnect leaves your current Local work available. While both computers have it open, the status bar shows Also open on (computer name). Editing on two computers at once can leave two different versions of your Flow.

title: Workspace Folders
content: A missing media reference is listed separately; FlowJoe does not replace it with a different file. Files present in the folder but unused by the current Flow are counted and retained; Workspace media is not deleted automatically. Settings → Data → Inspect Stale References shows missing targets and any safely repairable metadata. Safe repairs remove only the stale metadata link; they do not delete media files. If FlowJoe detects that a media file changed after it was read, it stops the write and opens the existing review path. The outside copy is preserved until you resolve the review.

title: Workspace Folders
header: Using one Workspace on two computers
content: If two computers, or two FlowJoe windows, save the same Workspace at the same moment, FlowJoe lets one finish first and the other waits a few seconds, then saves. Nothing you type meanwhile is lost. If a sync service delivers a version that was made without your latest save, FlowJoe asks which version to keep and keeps a copy of the other one. After launch, FlowJoe opens your verified Local copy while it checks the folder. Independent changes can be combined automatically; conflicting changes leave your Local work saved and available for review. Explicitly opening a changed folder can also preserve your previous version as a copy listed in Settings. The Open on another computer note is only information. It never stops you from opening or saving.

title: Workspace Folders
content: You can keep working during a temporary folder outage. Review conflicting changes before deciding what to keep. If the drive disconnects, the folder refuses a save, or its disk fills up, FlowJoe automatically continues saving your current Flow on this computer. You can keep editing. The status bar says Saving locally · reconnecting automatically; you do not need to switch storage or answer a recovery prompt for an ordinary temporary outage. When the same folder is available again, FlowJoe checks it and saves your latest Local work back before resuming folder saving. Independent edits in the folder are combined with your Local edits when they can be kept safely. It keeps your newer edits rather than opening an older folder copy. This also works after restarting FlowJoe while the folder is still unavailable. If the folder contains conflicting changes, your work stays saved locally while you review the versions. FlowJoe does not guess which work to discard. A replaced folder or a different Workspace or Flow needs an explicit reconnect. Choosing Switch to Local Storage deliberately stops automatic return. Choosing another Flow or Workspace also stops the old folder from taking over later. Ordinary Local saving and closing the app do not wait for a disconnected drive. Automatic recovery needs a usable Local copy and enough space on this computer to save your work. If neither destination can save, FlowJoe tells you and retains the work it can recover rather than claiming it is saved. The explicit recovery tools remain available for an incomplete or damaged copy. Your ways out, all on the same card: Reconnect Workspace — reconnect once the drive is back. Use Local Copy — continue from FlowJoe’s own recent copy of your work. Rebuild Workspace — write the workspace out to a new folder. Switch to Local Storage — go back to the app’s own storage. Start New Local Project — begin a fresh Flow. FlowJoe keeps a Local Recovery Copy inside the app while you work in a workspace,

title: Workspace Folders
content: workspace, which is what Use Local Copy restores from. See History & Recovery. If a save was interrupted halfway, connecting reports it and offers Clear Interrupted Save. FlowJoe only clears saves it can prove never completed; anything else it leaves alone and tells you so. If a save from another computer never finished in this folder (for example it was switched off mid-save), Settings shows A save from that computer never finished. It isn’t part of your Flow. FlowJoe waits a couple of minutes first, in case the other computer is still saving. This computer never applies another computer’s unfinished save, so your Flow is never replaced by it. The card offers one action, Clear, which asks you to confirm and then deletes the leftover. Your Flow stays exactly as it is. If it was your own other computer, open FlowJoe there before clearing: it finishes its own interrupted save, as long as nobody has saved this Flow since. If someone has, that save is dropped there too.

title: Workspace Folders
header: Switch between Workspace and Local storage
content: You can go back and forth using Settings → Data → Workspace Folder. Only one location receives your Flow’s saves at a time. Workspace → Local: choose Switch to Local Storage. FlowJoe saves pending work, copies the Flow and its media into the app’s storage, and continues there. The Workspace folder is left intact. Use this rather than Disconnect Workspace if you want to keep editing the same Flow. Work locally: new edits save inside FlowJoe. They do not update the disconnected folder. Local → Workspace: choose Reconnect Workspace for the remembered folder, or Connect Workspace and select the original folder. If you edited the Local copy, review how those edits should return to the Workspace using the choices below. If saving to the folder has failed but FlowJoe can still read it, Switch to Local Storage keeps what is currently on screen, including the latest edit that could not be saved to the folder. It checks that the Local save succeeded before completing the switch. If the folder cannot be read, use the recovery choices under When a folder becomes unavailable. You can repeat this process. Returning to a folder after Local edits can require a decision about which version to use. FlowJoe does not continuously sync the two locations. If a required save or safety copy cannot finish, the switch stops and reports the problem.

title: Workspace Folders
content: If you edited a Local copy before reconnecting, FlowJoe asks how to bring the two versions together: Choice What happens Keep Workspace Open the folder’s version and keep the differing Local version separately. Send My Changes Write your Local version into the folder. Merge Safe Changes Add Local changes that do not conflict. Where both versions changed the same work, keep the folder’s version. Keep as Separate Flow Preserve your Local work as its own Flow. Not Now Leave both versions unchanged. Find preserved versions under Settings → Data → Retained Reconcile Flows. Export one before removing it if you want a portable copy. See History & recovery for a different recovery prompt that offers Keep Workspace, Use Local Copy, or Rebuild Workspace.

title: Workspace Folders
content: A Private node’s contents, media, autosaves and local history are saved encrypted on this computer and open only with its password. A password-protected .fj export additionally encrypts the whole exported copy. Opening it restores normal app storage, where each Private node stays encrypted under its own password. See What is encrypted today and Encrypted backups. Workspace files represent password-protected private nodes as “Private node (not shared)” placeholders. When you create one in a Workspace, FlowJoe keeps it out of the live Flow until protection and its device-only copy are confirmed; only then can it be saved to the Workspace. When opening an older Flow, FlowJoe first confirms a durable owner-only copy before running load-time migrations, then checks the Workspace file before normal saving resumes. If FlowJoe cannot confirm that local copy, the connection stops before hydration or saving. Copies made before migration may remain elsewhere and cannot be recalled. If a retained Workspace backup still contains private text, FlowJoe replaces that text with a placeholder (your private notes stay on this computer) and removes any backup too damaged to check, then lets saving resume. Pictures and files you add to a private node are kept on this computer — FlowJoe does not put them in the Workspace folder itself, and guests cannot load them. If the node stops being private (for example, you remove its password), FlowJoe copies its pictures into the folder the next time it saves. This also holds when you open a .fj file (File > Open, Recent imports or Import Node(s)) while a Workspace is connected: pictures and files that belong to its private nodes stay on this computer, and only the rest goes into the Workspace folder. These protections also apply when you drop a .fj file onto the tree. Its private nodes retain their passwords, and their files stay on this computer. Importing into a private node makes the imported branch private too; FlowJoe asks first. Pictures

title: Workspace Folders
content: Pictures and files that private nodes put in the Workspace folder before this protection existed are moved to this computer automatically the next time you open the Workspace, once an identical copy is safely on this computer. They keep working for you, and the folder no longer holds them. A spreadsheet, document or calendar of a private node that you have edited since may still have an older copy in the folder; FlowJoe leaves that copy in place so your newer version is never lost. Copies that other computers, sync services or backups already made cannot be recalled. FlowJoe confirms that private edits are safely saved on this computer before marking a Workspace save complete or switching to another Workspace. If that local save fails, saving pauses and the switch stops so the latest private edits are kept with the current Flow. When you delete the last private node, a completed save also updates this Flow’s local startup recovery copy and removes the deleted node’s old private copy so it does not return when you reopen the Flow. If the folder save or that local cleanup fails, saving pauses and the earlier private copy stays recoverable. A recovery copy belonging to another Flow is left alone. A private node’s content stays on the computer where it lives. It is not stored in the Workspace folder, so it does not follow you to your own second computer: there, the node appears only as the “Private node (not shared)” placeholder.

title: Workspace Folders
content: When you quit or close the window, FlowJoe closes straight away if nothing needs to finish. If it has to wait, a Closing FlowJoe… cover shows while FlowJoe saves your work and stops any running terminals (it waits about 2 seconds, then force-stops them); the cover appears at once when terminals are running, or after a moment if a save is still going. If the last Workspace save could not finish, FlowJoe tries to keep those changes on this computer for recovery at the next start. If it cannot confirm they are safely stored, it tells you and offers Retry, Stay open, or Close anyway / Quit anyway. Choosing to leave anyway closes the app even if its extra recovery record cannot be written; the warning explains that unverified changes may be lost. A failed save does not force you to keep the app open indefinitely.

title: Workspace Folders
content: Workspace mode does not replace .fj export. You can still export a full .fj package or JSON at any time — see Export & Import. Restore points are not included in a workspace folder or a .fj file; they live with the app on this device.

title: Workspace Folders
content: History & Recovery — restore points, the Local Recovery Copy, and getting unstuck Export & Import — .fj packages and JSON Storage & Diagnostics — where data lives and how much room it takes

title: Workspace Folders
content: When reconnecting a Local copy, Merge Safe keeps your custom placeholder replacement, on/off change, or removal alongside an unrelated node edit in the folder. If both copies changed Flow-wide settings, the folder’s version stays in the merged result. Available placeholder picture files are copied with the merge; a missing picture does not prevent saving.

title: History & Recovery
content: Restore points that let you jump back to an earlier version of your Flow, plus the safety nets that keep your work when something goes wrong. FlowJoe keeps two different safety nets, and it helps to know which one you want: Restore points let you deliberately jump back to how your Flow looked at an earlier moment. Use it after a change you regret. The Local Recovery Copy is an automatic backup that exists only in Workspace Folder mode, for when the folder itself becomes unreachable. Review the saved version before restoring it. Keep portable backups as well. Blocked Local saves: When FlowJoe offers Try Again after a blocked Local save, it retries the waiting saves and keeps the recovery window open if the retry is refused. If another window opens while the retry is running, its result leaves that newer window alone.

title: History & Recovery
content: FlowJoe automatically keeps working and saving locally, with a small save-status warning. You do not need to choose a recovery action for an ordinary temporary outage. When the original folder returns, FlowJoe checks it and saves your latest work back automatically. Restarting while the folder is offline keeps you on the Local session. Independent folder edits are combined automatically when both versions can be kept safely. Conflicting folder changes need review; your Local version stays saved while you decide. A deliberate choice to stay Local stops automatic return. See When a folder becomes unavailable.

title: History & Recovery
content: A restore point keeps a copy of your whole Flow (tree, notes, tags, summaries) as it was at one moment.

title: History & Recovery
content: Click History in the app rail. History lists your saved versions from the last 30 days, newest first and grouped by day (Today, Yesterday, then the date). Each row shows the time (hover it for the exact date and time), what happened, and who did it — You, Joe, a Scheduled task, a Connected app, or Automatic. Several quick changes by the same person are shown as one row, with the number of changes. Rows with a stored summary or a retained older copy say what changed in plain words — for example “Renamed ‘Research’ → ‘Notes’ · Added 2 images to ‘Moodboard’”. Click Show what changed on a row to see the full list. Older rows whose copies were compacted away keep their general saved label. A change inside a password-protected private node is never named — it only ever counts as “1 private node changed”. The newest row is marked Current version. Restore points appear inline, on the version they belong to, with their name. Restore points from more than 30 days ago are listed at the bottom under Older restore points. History updates by itself while it is open. Use the Close X at the right of the title row to return to your gallery; it is separate from the History tabs.

title: History & Recovery
header: Ask Joe about a saved version
content: Native owner/API chat can look up dates and revision details for verified public changes in the current Flow without opening or restoring a version. A private branch does not hide an unrelated public change, while private-only changes contribute no search results. Joe reads only metadata from locally compared retained copies; older gaps and uncertain sources remain unavailable, and results are explicitly partial. Historical private labels and full saved Flow documents are not sent to the model. Restoring still uses the ordinary History confirmation.

title: History & Recovery
header: Ask Joe to restore a version
content: If you ask Joe to go back to an earlier version, he finds it and shows a Restore a saved version card in the chat, naming the Flow and the version’s number and date. Joe never restores anything by himself. Press Review restore to open the usual restore confirmation (it still saves a restore point first, and Go back to where I was is still offered afterwards), then confirm or cancel there. Cancel on the card, or New chat, drops the request. Joe can only offer versions that History shows with a Restore button, so the current version and quick saves merged into a later one cannot be offered. After you restore, Joe’s chat starts fresh (the restored Flow is a different document) and the usual Go back notification confirms what happened. If you cancel, the card says Cancelled · nothing changed. If a different Flow opens while you are confirming, nothing is restored. This is available only in your own Joe chat when Joe may propose changes, on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex). The FlowJoe CLI and other assistants connected from outside cannot offer it. On a Mac this includes Antigravity; on Windows and Linux, Antigravity can’t use Flow tools yet.

title: History & Recovery
content: The History window has three tabs, Versions, Chats and Images, and its title changes to match: Version History, Chat History or Image History. Guests see the same tabs for shared, nonprivate content. They can ask the owner to restore a version or change a restore point, but cannot execute those actions themselves. Reading Chats and Images here does not depend on enabling new Joe conversations or image generation for the invitation. Chats lists every Joe conversation in your Flow, newest first, each with the place it belongs to. Use the search box, or the filters All, Slots, Nodes and Summaries, to narrow the list. Open takes you to that place and opens the conversation in docked Joe. Conversations whose node or slot was deleted are kept under No longer in your flow. They open read-only: you can read and copy from them, and start a new conversation somewhere else to keep talking. One whose node was private, or whose old place FlowJoe can’t tell, shows without its words and can’t be read. Ordinary conversations travel with your Workspace folder, including the picture backups needed to reopen pictures in a chat. Anyone who opens that folder can read those conversations. Use the desktop icon on a conversation row to toggle Keep on this computer only. The current conversation and each older conversation have their own setting. A conversation with this setting, and its chat-only picture backups, stay on that computer and are excluded from the Workspace folder, history exports and browser sharing. Automatic Workspace storage and browser sharing exclude conversations about password-protected (Private) nodes, including their chat-only picture backups. Moving a slot into a private node applies the same restriction to its conversation immediately; you do not need to reopen the chat. A portable export may include eligible history when you explicitly select that Private node with password confirmation. Unlocking alone does not include it in a transfer. Each Flow has its own

title: History & Recovery
content: own conversations and Flow-summary chat. When upgrading older history, the former computer-wide summary is assigned once to the Flow open when that migration runs. Later Flows get their own summary conversations. Conversations on a password-protected (Private) node are not listed until you unlock that node. The trash icon on a row deletes that one conversation. Delete all shown deletes only the conversations currently shown, after any search or filter. Every delete asks first and tells you how many will be removed. Deleting cannot be undone. Conversations that only hold Joe’s greeting are not listed, and neither are the review chats from Source Control’s Review current branch. If FlowJoe cannot establish that an older conversation belongs to this Flow, it does not include it in bulk deletion. Switching Flows while a deletion confirmation is open cancels that deletion. If a conversation cannot be read, FlowJoe protects its saved messages from being replaced by an empty conversation. Reopen it after storage is available again before continuing. Images lists the pictures Joe made for nodes that are still in your Flow, grouped by day. Pictures from deleted nodes, and from locked private nodes, are not listed. Search, or filter by All, In a slot and Not placed. Each picture has Open, Send to slot, Copy prompt and a trash icon. Deleting a picture asks first. After deletion succeeds, its card goes; the stored picture is kept for as long as a slot or a chat message still uses it. If deletion cannot be saved, the card and picture are kept so you can retry. Delete all shown works the same way as in Chats, and only removes the rows that have a trash icon. If Image History cannot read its saved pictures, FlowJoe shows an error with Retry instead of saying that no pictures are saved. Starting a new conversation keeps the outgoing conversation with its original place. If you move to another conversation while the old one is being saved, that newer conversation stays intact. The

title: History & Recovery
content: The Saved label follows the picture’s current destinations. It hides the names and slot titles of locked private destinations. Standalone Image History stays on this computer when you copy a Workspace folder. A generated picture saved into an ordinary gallery slot can travel with the Workspace folder as gallery media; its separate Image History record does not. A .fj export with Include AI chat and image history selected includes only eligible conversations from the Flow you are exporting. Private-node conversations start excluded; explicitly selecting their Private nodes with password confirmation can include eligible conversations, chat picture backups and prompts according to the export options. Computer-only conversations remain excluded. A picture independently saved in an ordinary gallery follows the gallery’s export rules. Eligible chat pictures still travel in a full package after their standalone Image History rows have been deleted. A selected-node export includes only eligible chat and image history in that branch. Import keeps conversations anchored in the imported Flow. Conversation sharing also respects private-node and computer-only exclusions, even when ordinary Joe conversations are enabled for an invitation.

title: History & Recovery
content: Three kinds of restore point exist, and you control each independently. Kind When it happens Timed Automatically as you work, on a schedule you choose Before a restore Automatically, just before you restore — so you can undo the undo Ones you save yourself When you click Create restore point at the top of History, or Mark as restore point on any recent version Automatic ones are named Automatic restore point, and ones you create or mark are named Restore point — each shows beside its time. Click Rename on a restore point to give it your own name: a restore point with a name is kept until you remove it, however many new ones are made. Remove restore point stops keeping it (the version itself stays in History while it is recent). Restore point settings at the top of History opens Settings → Data → Restore Points. There, Save restore points automatically turns automatic ones on or off, and Save one automatically sets how often — from Every 15 minutes to Once a day. Timed restore points are taken when your Flow is saved, not by a clock running in the background — if you are not editing, nothing accumulates. Switching Flows while a restore point is being made can cancel it. Return to the original Flow and try again.

title: History & Recovery
content: In Settings → Data → Restore Points, each kind has its own limit: How many timed ones to keep How many to keep from before a restore How many you saved yourself to keep Set any of these to 0 to keep none of that kind. The card shows the running total — “Keeping up to 25 in total, plus any restore points you have renamed.” When a limit is reached, the oldest of that kind drops off; when that happens because you created or marked one, History tells you. Restore points you have renamed don’t count toward these limits and are never removed automatically. A restore point keeps the images and files it contains on disk until the restore point itself is removed, even if you delete them from the gallery — lowering the restore-point limits in Settings frees those sooner. Recently deleted images and files that aren’t in a restore point are also kept for a while (roughly your last 20 saves, a fixed window the restore-point limits don’t change) so Undo can bring them back. Once nothing can bring a file back, its space is freed the next time FlowJoe starts. Delete all restore points clears them for the current Flow. Your Flow itself is not changed.

title: History & Recovery
content: Click Restore on any row to go back to that version — a restore point, or any of your recent saves. Older versions that are not restore points are greyed and say Too old to restore: FlowJoe keeps a full copy of roughly your last 20 saves, plus every restore point. FlowJoe asks you to confirm, then replaces your Flow with that version. Before it does, it saves your current version as a restore point — including any edit you made a moment ago — so nothing is lost. A restore point includes your whole Flow, galleries too, so restoring puts images, files, links and slot notes back as they were — including one you mark on an older version. A restore point made before this update, still sitting in a Flow you haven’t touched since, is the one exception and holds only the tree and text. After a restore, a message appears with Go back to where I was, and History shows the same button at the top for as long as your Flow is still at the restored version. Click it to return to the version you had just before restoring. Going back is itself saved as a restore point, so you can change your mind again. That earlier version is also in History as a restore point named Before restoring ”…” (if you set How many to keep from before a restore to 0, it is kept only until the next restore point is made — Go back to where I was still works right after a restore). Undo last change at the top of History goes back to the version before your most recent change, with the same confirmation and the same safety restore point. It reaches back through your recent saves, galleries included: a change to images, files, links or slot notes — or deleting a slot or a whole node — is undone like any other, with its images. Moving or zooming the canvas, clicking through a stack, or moving a card is never counted as a change. Now and then a gallery change can’t be undone this way (for example one made with an older version of FlowJoe); Undo tells you so rather than undoing something older, and a restore point

title: History & Recovery
content: point is the way back. A restore is saved like any other change: closing FlowJoe or reloading afterwards keeps the restored version. If a restore cannot complete, FlowJoe tells you what state your Flow is in.

title: History & Recovery
header: What restore points do not cover
content: Importing a Flow over the current one, and starting a New Flow, do not take a restore point. Both replace your Flow completely, so a restore point taken then would not survive. Both offer to save or export your current Flow first — that export is your safety net, so take it. Both also start with an empty Chat History and Image History, so tick Include AI chat and image history in the export if you want to keep your Joe conversations and pictures. Merge-import is different: it keeps your Flow’s identity, and your restore points stay valid. Restore points also: Live on this device, with the app. They do not travel inside a .fj export or a workspace folder, and they do not sync to another machine. Belong to one Flow. Switching Flows does not carry them across. Reference your media rather than copying it. If a file was already gone, restoring brings back the slot but not the missing file.

title: History & Recovery
content: When your Flow is connected to a Workspace Folder, FlowJoe also keeps one automatic copy of it inside the app. It provides the last verified Flow and media for recovery when the folder becomes unreachable. For an ordinary temporary outage, FlowJoe preserves your current edits and automatically continues in Local storage. Use Local Copy remains an explicit recovery action when that automatic handoff cannot complete; it restores the verified copy and can be older than your latest edits. Your options, on the Settings → Data → Workspace Folder card: Reconnect Workspace — once the drive is back. Use Local Copy — continue from FlowJoe’s copy, in the app’s own storage. Rebuild Workspace — write everything out to a new folder. Switch to Local Storage — stop using the folder. Start New Local Project — leave the folder behind and begin a fresh, empty Flow in the app’s own storage. Disconnect Workspace leaves a folder without taking a copy of your Flow, and FlowJoe clears its local copy, so Use Local Copy is not offered afterwards. Reconnect, start a new local project or open another folder; to keep working with your Flow here, choose Switch to Local Storage instead. If the copy has fallen behind, the card says so plainly rather than implying it is current. Switch to Local Storage and Use Local Copy also save the connection to the Flow’s original Workspace before finishing. If that cannot be saved, the switch stops and keeps the Recovery Copy. This protects edits you make locally from being silently replaced when you reconnect the folder.

title: History & Recovery
header: When the folder and Local copy disagree
content: A recovery prompt may offer Keep Workspace, Use Local Copy, or Rebuild Workspace. Keep Workspace opens the folder’s version and preserves the differing Local copy. In Settings → Data, Resolve Retained Conflict Copies lets you export a retained recovery copy or explicitly discard it. A successful export removes that copy from the retained list, so keep the exported file. If you reconnect after editing a Local copy, a separate review offers Send My Changes, Merge Safe Changes, and other choices. See Reconnect after working locally. Those preserved versions appear under Retained Reconcile Flows.

title: History & Recovery
header: When a workspace file was changed elsewhere
content: If your workspace’s flow.json changes on disk while FlowJoe is running, you are asked what to do (Use External Changes, Keep My Changes, Open External as New Flow or Decide Later), and an unreadable file gets its own dialog; the full steps are in Workspace Folders. FlowJoe does not pick silently. Any copy it sets aside is kept rather than deleted (your own side is kept complete, including unlocked private nodes, and stays on this computer): open it as its own Flow, export it to .fj, or discard it.

title: History & Recovery
header: Ask Joe to review outside changes
content: If a change from another computer is waiting for your decision (the status bar shows Outside change waiting · saving paused), you can ask Joe to bring the review up. He shows a Review changes from another computer card in the chat, naming your Flow and showing your version, the outside version and how many items conflict, when any do. Joe never chooses for you and never replaces your changes. Press Review outside changes to open the usual review, then choose there. The card follows what happens: Resolution chosen · waiting for completion, Outside changes resolved, or Review closed · conflict still unresolved if you pick Decide Later or press Escape. If a choice fails, the review stays open and the card says so; you can try the choice again or pick Decide Later. If you use the outside version or open it as a new Flow, your chat ends with the switch, because that is a different document, and a notification confirms what happened. Keep My Changes keeps the chat, and the card shows the result. This is available only in your own Joe chat when Joe may propose changes, for Workspace Flows on the desktop app, on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex). The FlowJoe CLI and other assistants connected from outside cannot offer it. On a Mac this includes Antigravity; on Windows and Linux, Antigravity can’t use Flow tools yet.

title: History & Recovery
content: Keep an off-device backup of the work you want to recover. A full package can carry the Private work you explicitly include; enable package password protection and retain the package and node passwords separately. Copying the Workspace folder preserves its shared files, while Private content and other computer-only records stay in app storage. Restore points and the Local Recovery Copy also live on this computer, so they cannot replace an off-device backup. See What each copy preserves for media, workbenches, chats, transcripts, preferences and exclusions. Documenting these contents does not replace testing a restore on another computer. If a Workspace’s shared conversations file was saved by a newer FlowJoe, or is damaged, this FlowJoe leaves it untouched, keeps your conversations on this computer, and shows one notice per session that the shared conversations are not being updated. Choosing “keep on this computer only” then reports that it did not work, because the shared copy could not be changed.

title: History & Recovery
content: Workspace Folders — saving a Flow as a folder on disk Export & Import — .fj packages and JSON, the portable backup Storage & Diagnostics — what is taking up room Conversations keep following their original slot when it becomes part of a stack. Moving that stack into a Private node excludes those conversations from automatic Workspace storage and browser sharing, and from exports by default. An export can include eligible conversations if you explicitly include that Private node with password confirmation; unlocking alone does not include it. While History covers a gallery, keyboard shortcuts cannot delete its selected connections, jump between its slots or zoom its canvas. Closing History returns the gallery to its previous interaction state.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Invite people to view or edit a Flow in their browser, see who is where, and walk them through your Flow live. You can share a Flow with someone who has nothing installed. They open a link in their browser and see the same FlowJoe you do. Your computer stays the home of the Flow: guests work on it live through your computer. A guest’s browser keeps only what it needs while the link works (their own settings and the pictures, audio and video it has downloaded) and wipes all of it when the link is revoked, expires or ends, or when they choose Forget or Leave this Flow. Leaving also stops downloads and prevents late background work from saving shared content back into that browser. Choosing Leave also cancels uploads and changes still waiting to send. Sharing needs FlowJoe open on your computer. If you quit, guests see that you are offline and reconnect by themselves when you are back. Sharing also pauses on purpose in a few cases, listed under When something is wrong; guests are told why and their unsent edits wait for you. Sharing switches itself back on when you restart FlowJoe if it was on when you quit. Choose the shared area and permissions first, then use presenting to guide the tour.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Open Share in the header and turn Sharing on. You can move the window by dragging its title, including while it is opening. Choose Invite someone, type their name and choose Can view or Can edit. Choose what they see: the whole Flow or only the nodes you tick. Copy the link and send it. Each link is for one person and you can end it at any time. A guest sees only what you shared with them. Their theme, their language and their other settings are their own and never change your Flow. Where a card sits and how wide it is belong to the Flow, so they are the same for you and for everyone you shared with. (While you present, guests who follow see your screen, so show only what you are happy for them to see.)
