Action Can view Can edit Read shared nodes, galleries, repository files, Versions/Chats/Images in History, and retained transcripts Yes Yes Create and edit shared nodes, slots, notes, tags and memories, whoever created them No Yes Rename, save and commit shared repository files through your computer No Yes Move, resize and copy slots, work with stacks, add links, change slot colours and draw connections No Yes Freeze or unfreeze a shared node, or change its theme No Yes Remove their own content when it contains no protected contributions from others No Yes Remove someone else’s shared content, or their own container holding others’ contributions No Only with your additional removal permission Ask you to restore a version or change a restore point Yes Yes Execute a version restore or change restore-point settings No No Use Joe when enabled for the invitation Questions, conversation and background research; no shared-content changes Ordinary Joe features within their shared access, including background research and review on your account Generate pictures in the Images tab when enabled for the invitation Read only Yes Export, download, copy or print No Only when you enable Let guests export Chat in the group and message you, when Chat with each other is on Yes Yes

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Yes Message other guests privately When you also allow Guests can message each other When you also allow Guests can message each other Change their own appearance, language, layout and audio preferences Yes Yes Manage your invitations, credentials, workspace storage or native computer tools No No The same removal permission protects shared Joe conversations in Joe’s history popup: an Edit guest can remove their own conversation only when it has no protected contributions from someone else. Clearing a conversation or saving a shortened message list cannot remove those protected contributions. Choose the additional removal permission in the invitation to let an Edit guest remove other people’s shared content. It never reveals private content and never turns a View invitation into Edit access. Editing a title or note does not change who created the item. Older items without a recorded creator count as yours. For mixed selections, permitted removals proceed and protected items stay, with an explanation. Making a shared node private removes guest access. Currently, making it public again can require you to confirm the newly available content in Sharing before guests see it again. This extra confirmation is under review; it is not an additional guest permission.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Shared repositories also support branches, tags, remotes, merge, history and stashes through your computer. Guests see native branches except those tied to private or unshared nodes. Actions that discard existing work or rewrite Git history require elevated removal; ordinary file editing, saving and committing require Edit. Private folders inside a repository remain excluded and preserved. See Repositories for the individual actions. The repository’s Switch to File Explorer control and Source Control rail are available for shared repositories. View guests can browse shared files and the associated readable history. Edit guests can edit, save, rename, create files and folders, and commit through your computer. Save saves the file; Commit records the saved changes in Git. Your credentials stay on your computer. Private and unshared files are preserved when a guest commits shared changes. History uses the same Versions, Chats and Images tabs as your app. Reading history does not require enabling new Joe conversations or picture generation. Only records belonging to currently shared, nonprivate content are shown; private content is also withheld from older records and open history previews. Guests use Ask owner to restore to request an action from you. They cannot execute a restore themselves. Recent transcripts in Joe’s Transcribe tab also uses your retained Flow history. View guests read shared results; Edit guests can edit them and save through your computer. Private and computer-only results stay with you. Ordinary Edit can remove its own results, while removing other people’s results or their separate conflict copies requires elevated removal. Reading retained results does not enable new AI requests. See Transcribe audio. FlowJoe puts no limit of its own on what a guest writes or uploads: you decide who you invite and what you share. Joe knows who he is talking to. He talks to each guest as “you”, uses their first name now and then, and names you when he mentions

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: mentions you (“ask Elena for edit access”). He is also told who else is in the Flow, so he can mention them by name. A name is only a label: a guest who types “owner” or “admin” as their name still gets exactly the access you gave them. Joe’s existing rail button and panel stay available when you turn Joe off or your app is offline. Guests can still open the panel and browse retained shared history. New requests are disabled until execution is available again. When Joe is enabled for an invitation, that guest joins the same Joe conversation you already have for the shared node or slot. Your messages, the guest’s messages and Joe’s replies appear together in your normal Joe chat. A small avatar sits beside the bottom-right corner of each person’s message bubble; hover it or focus it with the keyboard to see their name. Guests who can see that node or slot can read its shared conversation in History even when new Joe requests are disabled; when Joe is enabled, an Edit guest who is not following your presentation can add messages. A View guest can ask Joe questions about what is shared with them and read his answers, but cannot ask him to change anything — controls that change shared content stay read-only for them. Joe uses the owner’s ordinary provider, model, settings, approval behavior and request handling. Ordinary Joe tools, output and proposal behavior stay the same within the shared area. CLI brains are isolated from your unrelated local files, commands and installed integrations; an unsupported CLI version or Antigravity cannot execute a guest request, and Joe does not switch providers automatically. See CLI brains in shared conversations. When someone else is typing to Joe in the conversation you are viewing, their avatar and a typing notice appear just above the message box. The typing avatar is the same size as the avatars beside messages. The notice stays outside the input border, whether Joe is docked or in a floating window. The conversation is saved

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: saved with your ordinary Joe chat on your computer, so it remains there after the guest leaves, sharing stops or FlowJoe restarts. The Joe conversations with guests screen is a separate, read-only way to browse the guest turns grouped by guest; it does not hold a separate live conversation. Joe access is set per invitation. Joe does not read the people chat described under Chat with each other below; that switch is about people talking to each other, not about Joe. If you remove a node or slot from a guest’s access, retrying an earlier Joe request cannot retrieve a saved answer about content they can no longer see. Pending requests also stop before releasing more content or changing a conversation or memory after that access changes. A saved computer-only conversation stays private even when someone knows an older conversation or message id. Native Browser and Terminal windows belong to your computer and are unavailable to guests. Source Control works through your computer for shared repositories; settings that manage your storage, accounts and credentials remain yours. A trusted linked file can be read from a shared slot while your computer is connected. Guests receive the file content through your app; your local path and permission to open, reveal or relink native files are not shared. An untrusted or missing link remains unavailable until you resolve it.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Top-level nodes. If you shared the whole Flow, an Edit guest’s new top-level node is a real top-level node in your Flow. If you shared only some nodes, it sits beside the shared top node, where it belongs in your tree, and it is added to that guest’s share. An Edit guest can also drop files into empty tree space to make a top-level node, including when an existing whole-Flow share has become empty. Removing top-level nodes follows the same creator, contribution and additional removal permission as other shared nodes. Tags. An Edit guest can create tags, and rename or recolour a tag they can see when nothing outside their access uses it. Deleting it also follows the creator and contribution rules: a guest’s own tag used by someone else on their content needs your additional removal permission. A tag lives in your whole Flow, so one that also sits on a node you did not share, or on a hidden or private slot, cannot be changed or deleted by a guest. Tags a guest cannot see stay hidden from them. Schedules. An Edit guest can ask Joe to set up a scheduled task. It runs on your computer with your key, but it can only read and change what is shared with that guest, and you see who made each task. A task does not start while you present, while sharing is deliberately paused, or after the guest’s access ends. Disconnecting the Workspace pauses these tasks before they use AI credits; reconnecting lifts that pause. Flow summary. A guest who was shared the whole Flow sees your written Flow summary, and an Edit guest can edit it. A guest who sees only some nodes gets a read-only summary of what is shared.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Turn on Let guests generate images in the Share window and an Edit guest sees Joe’s Images tab. The picture is made through your computer with your AI key and credits and shown in the guest’s preview. Send to Gallery adds it to the node like any picture they add. A guest who can only view sees the tab with the prompt and Generate switched off. Shared Image History includes only pictures recorded for this Flow. Copying a Flow does not bring another Flow’s picture history into the share. Older pictures without a recorded Flow stay available on your computer and are withheld from guests. Gallery files, link-preview pictures and the media list also follow current access. Ending the invitation or removing a shared slot while a file is loading prevents that pending request from delivering it. Image history and its pictures follow the guest’s current access. If you remove access to a node, make it private, or end the invitation while a picture or history request is waiting, that request cannot deliver the content afterwards.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: The Share window has a Chat with each other switch. It covers everyone you share this Flow with and is on unless you turn it off. Under it are two choices that only apply while Chat is on: Guests can message each other: guests can send each other private messages. When this is off, guests can message only you and the group. Save group chat with the Flow: the group conversation is kept with the Flow and is there next time you share. When this is off, it’s gone when sharing ends. Private messages are never saved in the Flow; each person keeps their own copy on their own device. Messages between two guests pass through your FlowJoe, which doesn’t show them to you or keep them. You can change these switches while people are connected. How to open and use Chat is in Chat.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Guests have FlowJoe’s real Settings. Personal appearance, density, surface style, language, layout, Tree, Gallery and Audio preferences affect their own browser. Personal save/reload prompts, reminders and export preference choices are also available; export itself still requires the permission you granted. Settings → Data → Reset Layouts, Delete Undo, onboarding replay, the startup profiler and Open-source licenses are also available. Controls for your workspace, storage, restore points, provider accounts and native computer remain yours. Changing a shared node’s theme requires Edit access; resetting themes affects only accessible shared nodes and respects protected subtrees. The coffee-mug logo also opens the same personal coffee-break game for View and Edit guests. Leaving or ending access closes the game.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: In the Share window the People with access heading has a Joe conversations button, and each guest’s row (ended ones too) has a speech-bubble button. Either opens Joe conversations with guests: a read-only record of guest turns grouped by guest, with the guest who spoke to Joe most recently first. It is a browsing view of contributions to your ordinary chat, not a separate conversation. Choose Everyone or one guest’s name to narrow the list. When a guest applied one of Joe’s suggestions, it shows “Applied by” followed by the guest’s name. This record stays on your computer after a share ends. Clearing ended invitations never removes it: the Joe conversations button stays, and on the first-time screen (no invitations left) it appears whenever saved conversations exist.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
header: If an access change cannot be saved
content: Changing a guest to View or revoking an invitation reduces their access immediately in the running app. If FlowJoe cannot save that change, it shows an error instead of reporting success. Check the guest’s current access; a failed save may not survive closing and reopening FlowJoe. A successful save is needed before you can rely on the change after a restart. Get a new link stops if the old invitation’s revocation cannot be saved, so it does not issue a replacement invitation after reporting that failure.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: When people are in your Flow you see them as avatars in the header: you first, then everyone else. Choose the + button to open Everyone here, grouped as Owner, Can edit and Can view, with what each person is doing. The breadcrumb row shows who is on the node you are looking at. Tree rows show who is on which node. A slot someone is typing in, moving or resizing is outlined in their colour and says so (“Leon is moving this card”). Under a slot’s notes you see who last added or changed it and how long ago, whether a guest or you. It is saved with the Flow, so it is still there after FlowJoe restarts or sharing ends. If you change something while sharing is off, the old guest credit is dropped rather than put on your new text. If your computer goes offline, every slot says editing is paused until you are back, and everyone else’s avatar gets a slowly turning dashed ring until you return. If a guest chooses Discard changes while your computer is unreachable, a message names the changes that were dropped so nothing is lost silently. A guest who opens an invitation sees the app blurred behind the join dialog. Your Flow itself only appears after they join.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
header: Transfer sharing choices to another Flow
content: A whole-Flow export can separately include sharing setup and conversations guests had with Joe. Review the guest names and saved history before including them. Imported sharing setup stays inactive. Open Share, review the saved choices, and send new invitations. Existing invitation links do not grant access to the imported Flow.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Use Present in the header (next to the Sharing pill) to walk guests through your Flow live. It starts off. It ends when you press Stop presenting or stop sharing; presenting stays off after a restart until you choose Present again. Selected cards keep their highlights when following opens another node, including when its gallery takes a moment to load. When the presenter clears the selection, the follower clears it too. While you present, guests are invited to follow. A guest who follows sees what you see, live: the node you have open, your canvas camera and zoom, your layout, the cards you have selected (and the selection rectangle while you drag it), your open windows, menus, Joe’s column and your Joe chat, and your Settings and History. They watch; they do not act. Nobody edits while you present. Every guest’s screen turns read-only and your computer refuses guest changes, including changes to shared memories and restoring memory snapshots, until you stop. Reading shared memories remains available. Guests choose to follow, and an unlocked guest can stop following. Guests can pan, zoom, scroll the canvas, and use canvas Fit or Reset while following. Other actions ask Stop following? first, so a click does not take them out by accident. Show my Joe chat while presenting is yours to switch off. Hidden or private slots and conversations kept on this computer stay out of the shared view, including older conversations. For stacks, this includes the picture or file currently shown and every stack containing it. If access changes, the copied conversation or slot preview clears. Public node-summary windows show your unsaved summary text too; the whole-Flow summary stays out of the presentation. A history popup containing a conversation kept on this computer is withheld. What each reply cost (the token total under a reply and its receipt) is never shown to followers, or to any guest: your spend stays on your computer. The Presenting panel on the pill lists who follows and

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: and who is looking around on their own. Guests who cannot see the node you are on see a short note that you are somewhere they cannot follow.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: When you invite someone you can choose how they join: Normal: they open the Flow and can follow when you present. Start in follow mode: they open straight into following you, and can stop. Keep them following until I release them: they follow without a Stop button until released. They can still pan, zoom, scroll, and use canvas Fit or Reset to adjust their own view. Before you present they see a waiting screen. You can also set Presenting starts to a date, time and time zone. A guest who opens the link early sees when to expect you in their own time zone, in yours and in UTC, with a countdown. FlowJoe only shows the time; you still press Present. Open the Presenting panel to Lock all, Unlock all or lock and release one guest. Releasing never removes anyone from the Flow. If you stop presenting, stop sharing or go offline, the lock ends by itself. Stopping Present also releases Joe for guests who were following. Guests already released by ending Present stay released when you turn sharing off and back on with their session retained. Starting a new presentation or explicitly locking them again reapplies the invitation’s lock preference; a new locked guest still waits for their first presentation.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: “Editing is paused while the owner presents”: the owner is presenting; try again when they stop. A guest sees “owner offline”: your FlowJoe is quit, your computer is unreachable, or you are not sharing. Turn Sharing on and they reconnect on their own. Someone opens your address directly (for example yourname.flowjoe.app) and sees “This link can’t open a shared Flow”: the address on its own doesn’t let anyone in. Send them their invitation link. A guest sees “Paused” and a reason: sharing is on hold on purpose, not broken. “Paused · (your name) opened another Flow”: you switched to a different Flow. Going back to the shared Flow lifts the pause. “Paused · (your name) closed this Workspace”: you chose Delete Workspace or Disconnect, or closed the Workspace. Reconnecting it (or continuing locally) resumes sharing. “Paused · (your name)‘s FlowJoe window is closed”: on a Mac, closing the window keeps FlowJoe running but pauses sharing until you open a window again. While paused, guests are not shown as present, but changes they made are kept and sent automatically when you are back. A guest who chooses Discard changes is told which changes were dropped. A guest sees “(Owner’s name)‘s FlowJoe needs an update”: the guest page is newer than the FlowJoe on your computer. They can keep the page open and it connects as soon as you have updated; there is a Try now button, and the page checks again by itself every so often. You see “Update needed” when you try to share: your FlowJoe is too old to work with your guests’ browsers. Update now opens the FlowJoe download page; install the new version, then turn sharing on again. Everything else you do on your computer keeps working. Guests can use Joe after the owner enables it during the session, without reloading their browser. Joe checks the owner’s current provider availability when an action starts.

title: Sharing, Guests and Presenting
content: Guests receive permitted link-card pictures through the owner’s computer. Picture downloads have size, time and connection limits; unused redirect downloads are closed before another address is tried. Guest edits are admitted only with a current Edit invitation and valid browser session checks. Those checks run before the owner’s app buffers the submitted changes, and again before applying them. Guests who share a display name still have separate edit credits. You refers to your own session; an older credit without that identity keeps its saved name. A visible stack does not let a guest move or remove hidden items inside it. To leave as a guest, open your own avatar and choose Leave this Flow, then Leave Flow. A goodbye screen confirms that you left; Close this page is ready for keyboard use. This browser forgets your name, mark and stored shared content. Anything you added stays in the owner’s Flow, and your invitation link still works if you want to return. Choose Cancel to stay.

title: Chat
content: Talk with the people you share a Flow with: one group conversation for everyone, and private messages between two people. While you share a Flow, you and your guests can talk to each other in FlowJoe. There is one group conversation, Everyone, and a private conversation between any two people. Chat is people only: Joe does not read it, and it is separate from your Joe conversations. Chat is on unless you turn it off in the Share window (see Chat with each other).

title: Chat
content: Choose Chat (the speech bubbles) on the left rail or in the header, right after Joe (the robot). Guests have it while the Flow is shared with Chat on. As the owner you always have it in the desktop app, even with no guests, with sharing off, or with Chat turned off for the share, so you can read the Flow’s saved group chat, and your own private conversations, at any time. Or press Cmd+Shift+X (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+X (Windows and Linux). The same keys close it. Chat opens in the right-hand column that Joe also uses. Whichever of the two the column is showing is highlighted, on the rail and in the header. If Joe is open, Chat slides over Joe and Joe waits underneath, just as you left it: choose Joe (the robot) to switch back to Joe, or close Chat. If Joe is closed, Chat opens the column on its own. Press Escape or the × to close Chat. The speech bubbles always mean chatting with people; the robot always means Joe — even Joe’s own Chat tab shows the robot. Everyone, saved with the Flow. A green count on the Chat button, and on each conversation at the top of the panel, shows how many messages you haven’t read yet. Someone who has sent you a private message you haven’t read also gets a green count on their picture at the top of the window. When a private message arrives while Chat is closed (or while you’re in another conversation), a small notice shows who it’s from and what they wrote. Choose Reply to open that conversation, or Dismiss. Messages in Everyone only raise the count; they never pop up.

title: Chat
content: Point at (or click) anyone’s picture at the top of the window to see their card. Choose Message on the card to open Chat straight to your private conversation with them. Green 1: an unread private message. If the owner has turned off messages between guests, another guest’s card says so instead; you can still write in Everyone and message the owner. If the owner has muted you in Chat, the card says that instead: you can still read along and message the owner. As the owner, a guest’s card also has a mute button (a bell with a line through it). Mute in Chat stops that guest writing in Everyone without removing them from the Flow; they can still read along and message you. Choose it again to unmute.

title: Chat
content: The row at the top of the panel lists Everyone first, then the people in the Flow. Choose one to open that conversation. Everyone: everyone in the shared Flow sees it. A person: a private conversation between the two of you. A private conversation with Rin. If the owner has turned off messages between guests, guests can still write in Everyone and message the owner; other guests’ names are greyed out. Each conversation keeps its own unsent words: switch to another conversation and back, and what you started is still there. As the owner, your private conversations with a guest stay in the list after they leave, so you can read them back; you can write again when they return. When sharing is off, or Chat is turned off for the share, the owner can still open Chat to read the Flow’s saved group conversation (a Flow with none says No messages yet), and each private conversation kept on this computer, listed after Everyone. None of them can be written to until you share again with Chat on.

title: Chat
content: Drag a slot from the gallery onto the Chat panel, or right-click a slot and choose Add to Chat (this works even where you can only view, or on a frozen node). It waits in the message box as a small chip (choose its × to take it back out); add words if you like, then send. You can send a slot on its own. In the conversation, a shared slot shows as a card with its picture and name. Choose the card to open the slot in the preview. Each person sees the slot from their own copy of the Flow, so someone whose share doesn’t include that slot sees Not available to you instead, and its name is never shown to them. Guests can only share slots they can see.

title: Chat
content: Choose the paperclip at the left of the message box, drag a file from your computer onto the Chat panel, or paste a picture into the box. Like a slot, it waits as a chip until you send, so you can add words first, and you can send a file on its own. There’s no size limit; a big file takes as long as your connection needs. If a file can’t be sent, nothing is sent, everything stays waiting, and a line under the box says which file it was. In the conversation a picture shows itself and any other file shows its name and size. Choose either to save it to your computer. With Save group chat with the Flow on, pictures and files sent in Everyone are saved inside the Flow along with the messages, so the owner can still open them after sharing ends. Pictures and files in a private conversation are kept with your own copy of that conversation on your device, so they still open after the owner’s computer has let go of them (for example once you’ve both downloaded them). They’re never saved in the Flow, and a guest’s copy goes when they leave the Flow. A file that’s no longer anywhere says No longer available. Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter to send. Shift+Enter starts a new line. Web addresses (starting with http or https) become links.

title: Chat
content: Point at a message (or move to it with the keyboard) to see its small toolbar. Reply on someone else’s message in Everyone opens your private conversation with them. Delete removes your own message; the owner can also Delete for everyone on any message in Everyone. Deleting always asks first, and can’t be undone. A removed message leaves a short line saying who removed it.

title: Chat
header: When the owner’s FlowJoe is offline
content: If a guest’s connection to the owner’s FlowJoe drops, Chat stays open and everything already there stays readable, but nothing can be sent until it reconnects. Nothing is saved up to send later.

title: Chat
content: A line above each conversation says what happens to it. Conversation Where it is kept Everyone, with Save group chat with the Flow on In the Flow itself, so it travels with the Flow, its exports and its Workspace folder, and is there the next time you share. Everyone, with saving off New messages are kept nowhere: they’re gone when sharing ends, and are never saved later. Turning saving off doesn’t erase anything already saved with the Flow. A private conversation Never in the Flow. Each of the two people keeps a copy on their own device: the owner in FlowJoe on their computer, a guest in their browser. If a browser can’t keep its copy (for example its storage is turned off), Chat says so in that conversation instead of promising a copy, and keeps trying. Messages between two guests pass through the owner’s FlowJoe on the way; it doesn’t show them to the owner. It holds them only until both guests’ browsers have saved their own copy, and a picture or file on its way is kept locked (encrypted) so nothing readable stays on the owner’s computer. A guest’s copy is erased with everything else the share stored in their browser when they choose Leave this Flow, or when the link ends.

title: Chat
content: Chat is never shown to people following your presentation. Each person’s Chat panel is their own, and a guest you have locked to your presentation can still open Chat and talk. Keyboard focus stays on the conversation tab you are using when new messages arrive. Your selected conversation and its unsent draft stay in place.

title: Export & Import
content: Transfer workspaces, copy subtree JSON, and save password-protected archives. FlowJoe exports the work you select, with the media and histories supported by your chosen options. You can move individual branches or entire workspaces between devices, and protect sensitive exports with whole-package encryption. Review the export scope and history choices before choosing a format. This capture stops before exporting a file. Choose a full package when the media needs to travel, and verify linked-file paths on the destination.

title: Export & Import
content: FlowJoe supports two primary export shapes:

title: Export & Import
content: What it contains: The complete tree structure, text notes, summaries, tag mappings, and slot metadata. What it omits: The actual media binary files (images, audio, PDFs are referenced by name but not bundled). Best For: Small backups, version-tracking text in Git, or sharing outlines.

title: Export & Import
content: What it contains: The tree and the media referenced by the Flow or branch you export, gathered from its active storage. Unused database files are not bundled. Best For: Archiving projects, backing up files, or moving your work to a different machine. Linked local files remain references; their original files are not bundled. Copy those files separately and relink them on the destination computer.

title: Export & Import
content: Every Private node starts left out of an export. To include one, tick its row, enter its password and read the warning. Everything inside a Private node shares its password, so one choice covers the whole Private branch. Exporting a selected child inside a Private node also requires including that Private node; only the selected branch is written, as a Private node of its own that opens with the same password. These choices reset when you reopen Export or change its scope. Included nodes keep their FlowJoe locks and carry their contents. Their chats, picture history, transcripts and undo notes follow the history options below; records you keep on this computer stay here. Private-only tags and Memories travel only with their node. A Flow-wide Memory proposed from an excluded Private chat stays home too. An included Private node stays encrypted inside the exported file and opens only with its own password after import. Its name and the rest of the file are readable by anyone who opens it directly unless you also choose Protect package with a password. Send it only to people you want to have it. If the Flow, access or Private protection changes while you are choosing, reopen Export to review it. Leaving out a Private branch produces a partial copy and does not clear the Flow’s unsaved reminder.

title: Export & Import
content: The export window’s Include transcript history option is enabled by default for JSON and full packages, including password-protected exports. It includes completed transcript text and retained edits, even if you have not saved a gallery copy. Turn it off to omit this history. Transcripts from a Private node travel only when you explicitly include that node. Records marked Keep on this computer only remain excluded. A gallery copy is part of the gallery’s ordinary data and follows that data’s export rules. Whole-Flow imports restore included history under the imported Flow’s local identity. Merge imports remap its source links to the imported nodes and slots. Import Node(s) includes history only for the selected imported branches. History can still be opened, copied, and saved when its original recording is missing; a JSON export does not carry the recording’s media file. In Local mode the restored history lives in local app/browser data. In Workspace mode eligible history also goes into .flowjoe/transcript-history.json; that file is separate from the Workspace’s main Flow JSON. You can reopen, remove, or clear records from Recent transcripts in Joe’s Transcribe tab. Clearing history leaves original recordings and saved gallery copies in place.

title: Export & Import
content: When exporting a full package or data-only JSON, select Protect package with a password, then enter and confirm a package password. A protected data-only export also uses the .fj extension; it still does not bundle the media bytes. This encrypts the entire exported file: the outline, selected content and history, included media, and filenames inside the package. The outer file name and file size remain visible. An ordinary .fj without this option is not encrypted. To include a Private node, select its row before exporting. If the node is already unlocked, you do not need to enter its password again; a locked node still requires its node password. Those choices and package encryption are separate: you need both to put Private content into an encrypted backup. When opening the backup, FlowJoe asks for the package password before importing its contents. A wrong password or canceling that password prompt leaves the current Flow unchanged. After a successful import, included Private nodes remain locked and require their separate node passwords; the package password does not unlock them. Import restores the contents into FlowJoe’s normal storage. Private nodes stay encrypted there; ordinary nodes and the Workspace Folder are saved as usual. See Security & privacy. Private nodes when importing: an imported Private node arrives locked and opens with its own password. Importing into an unlocked Private node asks for the imported node’s password, then it joins that node’s protection and FlowJoe shows “Now protected by “…”‘s password.” Importing a Private node back into the Flow it came from brings it in as a separate copy that opens with the same password: FlowJoe shows Import as a copy and asks for that password first. Cancel or a wrong password imports nothing. Exporting a node from inside a Private node writes it as a Private node of its own that opens with the same password. See What is encrypted today. New protected exports use stronger password derivation to make

title: Export & Import
content: make password guessing more expensive. Older protected backups still open with their original passwords. Existing backup files keep their original protection; export a new protected copy to use the stronger setting. Choose a long, unique package password. There is no package-password recovery. Keep the password somewhere safe, separately from the backup. Full packages saved through the desktop save window or a browser’s file-saving window use a streaming encrypted format. FlowJoe can export and import these packages above 2 GiB without loading the whole archive into memory. You still need enough free space for the imported media and the retained original backup. Use a current version of FlowJoe on the receiving computer; older versions cannot open this format. Protected data-only exports and browser download fallbacks use the earlier format and still need to fit in memory. Earlier protected packages of 2 GiB or larger cannot be imported. Very large outlines or media lists may also need to be split into smaller exports.

title: Export & Import
header: Ask Joe to export a node
content: If you ask Joe to export a node, he shows an Export the selected node card in the chat, naming the Flow and node (“node and children”) and the package type (full package, history and credentials excluded). Joe never exports anything by himself. Press Review export to select that node and open the usual Export dialog, set up as the card says (the node with its children, histories off; you can still change any option), then choose the format, options, password and where to save. Cancel on the card drops the request. The card then tells you what happened: Save chooser opened · no file exported, Export completed, Cancelled · nothing changed, or Export did not complete · no file was saved. Joe is only told the dialog was opened; he never sees the file or where you saved it. A node that is private, locked or hidden — or sits inside such a branch — cannot be offered. If the selected node changes before you pick a format, nothing is exported. This is available only in your own Joe chat when Joe may propose changes, on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex). The FlowJoe CLI and other assistants connected from outside cannot offer it. On a Mac this includes Antigravity; on Windows and Linux, Antigravity can’t use Flow tools yet.

title: Export & Import
header: Ask Joe to import a Flow
content: If you ask Joe to import a Flow, he shows an Import a Flow card in the chat, naming your Flow (“entire Flow”) and reminding you to choose a .fj, .zip or .json file and review the import mode. Joe never imports anything by himself, and he never picks or sees the file. Press Choose import file to start the usual File menu import: if your Flow has unsaved work you are first asked whether to save, then your computer’s file chooser opens, and then the usual import options appear so you can overwrite, merge at the root, or merge at the selected node. The card follows what really happens: System file chooser opened · awaiting your file choice, Import options opened · your file selected; nothing imported, Import confirmed · waiting for completion, and then Import completed, Cancelled · nothing changed, or Import did not complete · no success reported. Cancelling at any step, including the save prompt, imports nothing. Joe is only told the import was opened; if you merge, cancel, or the import fails without replacing your Flow, he is also told how it ended (never the file name or contents), so he can carry on from there. A failed merge may already have added some nodes, so check the tree before trying again. If you overwrite, the Flow is replaced and the chat ends, as with any overwrite. If you load a different Flow before the import runs, it is cancelled. Only one import can run at a time. This is available only in your own Joe chat when Joe may propose changes, on every brain that uses Flow tools (OpenAI, Gemini, and CLI brains such as Claude, Grok and Codex). The FlowJoe CLI and other assistants connected from outside cannot offer it. On a Mac this includes Antigravity; on Windows and Linux, Antigravity can’t use Flow tools yet.

title: Export & Import
content: The Recent list in the File menu keeps shortcuts to your last five imported Flows, not copies of their contents. On desktop, choosing an entry opens the original file at its saved location. If that file was moved, deleted or cannot be accessed—or you are using the browser—choose the file again in the file picker. FlowJoe reads the file as it is now; the entry is not a backup of an earlier import. The usual save-before-import, package password and import choices still apply. Clear removes the shortcuts, not the original files. FlowJoe also removes cached Recent imports retained by older versions when their storage is available; external originals, current Flows and their normal history are unchanged.

title: Export & Import
content: When you import a .json or .fj file, FlowJoe prompts you for a merge strategy: Overwrite: Replaces the current Flow with the imported backup after protecting the outgoing Flow. The imported Flow receives a fresh local identity. Merge at Root: Appends the imported nodes as new roots side-by-side with your existing workspace. Merge Under Selected: Ingests the imported subtree as nested children under the currently selected node. When a package has enough verified information to compare it with the connected Workspace, FlowJoe explains whether using it would advance the Workspace or replace it with an older version. It protects the current Flow and asks before updating it. A saved revision number alone does not prove which version is newer: packages from another app session or computer, and older packages without that proof, use the existing safe choices to keep the Workspace or open the package as a new Flow. Restarting the app does not mean the package belongs to a different Flow; it means its revision number cannot safely establish the relationship. If a password-protected .fj was made by a newer version of FlowJoe, FlowJoe tells you to update instead of reporting an invalid file. If a package carries sharing setup or guest Joe history from a newer version, FlowJoe keeps the parts it understands and shows a notice when anything was skipped; the Flow itself always imports. Protected nodes inside an imported package retain their individual password locks even after the package itself is unlocked and imported.

title: Export & Import
content: Copy Node JSON: Right-click a node and select Copy Node JSON. This puts the branch’s structure and metadata onto your clipboard. Media files are not bundled into the copied text. You can paste this code block directly into a text editor or share it with Joe. Copy Slot JSON: Right-click a gallery card to copy individual card styling, tags, and notes data.

title: Export & Import
content: Shared guests read retained transcripts from the owner’s Flow; their browser’s pending edit recovery is not an independent export source. The owner’s export can include eligible retained transcript text with Include transcript history, subject to the privacy rules above. A guest’s export/download availability still follows the permissions granted for that share. Clearing guest browser data does not delete owner-retained transcripts. See Transcribe audio.

title: Export & Import
content: Cancel releases the export controls even if the browser is still finishing a file operation. FlowJoe removes a newly created empty file when it can safely do so. It preserves existing backups, files changed elsewhere, and completed files. If the browser finishes saving after you press Cancel, the completed file stays on disk; check that destination before starting another export.

title: Export & Import
content: Use Include AI chat and image history to carry eligible history with the exported work. Conversations from an excluded Private node stay home, together with their chat-only backup pictures and image-history prompts. If you explicitly include the Private node, its history follows this checkbox like any other node. Current and older conversations marked Keep on this computer only remain excluded independently. A picture independently saved in a gallery follows its node’s export choices. Its prompt copy travels only when Include AI chat and image history is on. A branch export includes only eligible chat and image history belonging to that branch. Full packages include the backup pictures that eligible current and older chats still use, even after you delete their separate Image History rows. Plain JSON keeps the references but does not carry picture bytes. Imported image history follows the imported Flow, nodes and slots instead of attaching itself to an older Flow with matching identifiers. Whole-Flow exports can separately include sharing setup and conversations guests had with Joe. Review guest names and saved history before including them. Imported sharing choices are inactive until you review them in Share and send fresh invitations; old links do not open the imported Flow. For an off-device backup checklist and a comparison with Workspace copies, see What each copy preserves. Version History and restore points stay with the app on the original computer. See History & recovery for the difference between portable conversation history and local restore points.

title: Storage & preferences
content: Check saved data, inspect unused media, and include your preferences in backups. Slots and media are different counts: a stack is one slot, while its members count as media.

title: Storage & preferences
content: Open Settings → Data → Storage Stats to see how much data FlowJoe keeps on this computer. The local database holds your Local Flow, media, and growing records such as histories. Smaller browser storage mainly holds settings and recovery information. A connected Workspace Folder is a separate storage destination. Use the inspection controls before deleting anything: Inspect Orphaned Media finds files no longer referenced by saved work. Inspect Stale References checks references whose files may be missing. Inspect Orphaned Image Prompts finds image-prompt records no longer attached to their images. View Diagnostics Log, on desktop, opens troubleshooting information. For slow Joe replies, the desktop app also keeps bounded local support summaries of OpenAI request times and reported cache reuse. These summaries contain counts and timings, without conversation text or API keys. They help investigate delays; they do not measure the complete time you waited for a reply. New summaries separate ordinary HTTP requests from persistent-connection requests; attempts without an observed response stay unknown. Older summaries may have no connection breakdown. These samples can mix models and tasks, so their timings do not prove that one connection method is faster. Read the inspection results before choosing a cleanup. Export a backup first if you are unsure.

title: Storage & preferences
content: FlowJoe saves normal edits automatically to the active storage. Check the bottom save indicator for pending or blocked saves. File → Export Flow, the save indicator, and Cmd/Ctrl+S create a portable backup. Changes waiting to be exported are separate from whether the current storage save succeeded. See History & recovery if saving is blocked.

title: Storage & preferences
content: Use Settings → Data → Save Preferences With Exports to include choices such as appearance, audio settings, and saved playlists in an export. API keys are excluded by default. Only select Include OpenAI API key in export when you intend the recipient to receive that credential.

title: Build a Research Board
content: Step-by-step guide to gathering, annotating, and reviewing research materials. This guide walks you through setting up a structured research workspace in FlowJoe to compile academic, competitive, or design materials. An observation plan, a methods checklist, and notes about uncertainty give this research branch a purpose. No study findings are claimed.

title: Build a Research Board
content: Use the same three steps with your real sources and evidence.

title: Build a Research Board
content: Select your root node and press N (or Ctrl+N) to add a new child node. Press F2 (or Enter when the tree has focus) and rename it to Research Hub. Create more child nodes the same way for different sources (e.g. Web Articles, PDF Papers, Competitive Audits).

title: Build a Research Board
content: Open your system Finder/Explorer. Select your PDFs, spreadsheets, or images and drag them directly onto the gallery surface of the PDF Papers node. FlowJoe creates cards for each file. Double-click the PDF slots to read the articles inline.

title: Build a Research Board
content: Open a PDF slot and write a brief summary in its notes, highlighting key citations. Open Node Summary from the toolbar (or press S with the node selected) and write an executive summary of the branch.

title: Build a Research Board
content: Press Cmd+Shift+A / Ctrl+Shift+A to open the Joe panel. Ask Joe: “Read the selected PDF paper slot and summarize its primary findings in three bullet points.” Use the reply’s Send to Gallery action, choose the slot’s notes, then confirm.

title: Organizing Stacks & Tags
content: Learn how to manage design variants and tag references across nodes. This guide demonstrates how to manage multiple creative design iterations and catalog them using tags.

title: Organizing Stacks & Tags
header: Step 1: Set up a Creative Branch
content: Create a node named Creative Assets. Under it, add children nodes for Logos, Mockups, and Copy Drafts.

title: Organizing Stacks & Tags
content: Paper Moon keeps three graphic-novel cover studies together. The active study changes while the comparative slot notes stay with the stack. Drag your first logo design (logo_v1.png) into the Logos gallery. Drag logo_v2.png and drop it directly on top of the first logo card. FlowJoe creates a Stack. Use the left/right arrow buttons to cycle through the versions. Hover over the stack and drag thumbnails to promote a new version to the top active preview.

title: Organizing Stacks & Tags
content: Select a slot, click the tag badge, and select Edit Tags. Create tags named Approved, In-Review, and Needs-Work with corresponding visual colors. Assign the In-Review tag to the stack.

title: Organizing Stacks & Tags
content: Open Query by tags (Q) and choose In-Review. Review matching slots together; use each result’s origin badge to return to its node. Clear the tag query to return to the regular gallery. For text search instead, turn on Include tags and search for In-Review; enable All nodes to search across the Flow.

title: Restructuring with Joe
content: Use Joe to organize, clean up, and reschedule your hierarchy. Learn how to work with Joe to automate structural edits and clean up a cluttered project hierarchy. Read the proposed changes before approving. This diagram explains the process; it is not a fabricated Joe response.

title: Restructuring with Joe
content: Select a node that has become disorganized (e.g. containing 20 loose sibling nodes with files attached). Limit map to my location (on by default) then gives Joe this branch instead of the whole tree, which keeps the send smaller. See Token usage with Joe.

title: Restructuring with Joe
content: Press Cmd+Shift+A / Ctrl+Shift+A to open the Joe panel. Ask Joe: “Review my current branch. Group these 20 sibling nodes into three logical child folders based on their content types, and move the nodes into place.”

title: Restructuring with Joe
content: Joe processes the hierarchy and returns a Proposal Card. Inspect the card. You will see green + indicators showing the three new child nodes Joe wants to create, and move indicators showing where original nodes are going. Click Approve. The changes apply instantly.

title: Restructuring with Joe
content: Ask Joe: “Every Friday at 4 PM, check this folder for any new nodes, tag them as ‘unassigned’, and write a summary card.” Approve the schedule card. A clock icon appears on the parent node, showing that a scheduled task is attached. It runs at its scheduled time while this Flow is open and scheduled runs are enabled. Use Settings → Tasks → Run Now for an immediate run; safety checks may still hold its result for review.

title: Move a Flow to another computer
header: Move a Flow to another computer
content: Take your tree, references, and optional preferences with you. A full .fj package brings your selected Flow content and media together in one portable file. Choose the Private content and histories you want to preserve, and add package password protection for sensitive work. To protect against losing this computer, keep the completed backup on a separate drive or trusted backup service; automatic saves and recovery copies on the same computer cannot provide that protection.

title: Move a Flow to another computer
content: This inventory describes FlowJoe’s current storage and export paths. Check your choices each time you make a backup, especially after changing Private protection or history settings. Content Copy of the whole Workspace folder Full .fj package Data-only JSON Included tree, notes, summaries, tags and gallery layout Yes, as last saved to the folder Yes, within the chosen export scope Yes, within the chosen export scope Imported images, audio, video, PDFs and other stored files Copy media/ with the folder Included referenced media; unused stored files are omitted Media references only; no bundled file bytes Saved spreadsheet, document and calendar workbenches Keep the whole folder and its media Included saved workbench assets travel with the package Do not rely on it for workbench assets stored as media Private node text and media Redacted placeholders; full content stays on the original computer Only Private nodes you explicitly select and confirm with their passwords Same explicit selection, but media bytes are omitted Joe conversations and their chat pictures Eligible ordinary conversations and picture backups; Private and computer-only conversations stay local Select Include AI chat and image history; eligible history and chat picture bytes travel Selected eligible text/history and picture references, without picture bytes Standalone Image History and prompts Stay local; a picture saved in an ordinary gallery travels as gallery media Eligible records follow Include AI chat and image history Eligible records follow that choice; no picture bytes Transcript history Eligible records in .flowjoe/transcript-history.json; include the hidden .flowjoe/ folder Include transcript history, on by default, carries eligible text and retained edits Same history option; original recording bytes are omitted Slot text and undo-note history Do not treat the folder as a portable copy of the app’s undo history Follow Include undo notes history Follow the same option Joe Memories Stay

title: Move a Flow to another computer
content: Stay local Included for the exported Flow or branch, subject to Private exclusions Same scope and exclusions Scheduled tasks Travel with the Flow Included unless you turn off their export option Same option Saved Everyone chat and its attachments Travel when Save group chat with the Flow was enabled Saved messages and referenced attachment bytes travel Saved messages and file references; no attachment bytes Private conversations between people and their files Stay on each participant’s device Excluded Excluded Preferences and saved playlists Preferences stay local Enable Save Preferences With Exports for supported preferences Same setting Browser data Stays local Only the browser data offered by the explicit export option Same option; not a backup of every browser profile or sign-in Sharing setup and guests’ saved Joe conversations Not a backup of working invitations or account access Whole-Flow export has separate choices; imported sharing stays inactive until reviewed and freshly invited Same choices Version History and restore points Stay in this computer’s app storage Excluded Excluded API keys Not part of the Workspace folder Excluded by default; only the explicit OpenAI-key option transfers that credential Same option; leave it off for ordinary backups Histories marked Keep on this computer only remain excluded even if you select their history option or include their Private node. Nested Private nodes each need their own inclusion choice. Exporting a branch leaves out work and histories outside that branch. Linked files are separate. A saved path is not a copy of the file. Copy linked originals separately and relink them on the destination. Live websites and external embeds still depend on their services. A Flow export is not a backup of a Git repository’s complete commit history, your installed tools, AI models, account sign-ins or every app setting; back up those separately if you need them. Ordinary Workspace files, JSON and unprotected packages are

title: Move a Flow to another computer
content: are readable outside FlowJoe. Protect package with a password encrypts the exported snapshot, including admitted Private content; it does not add missing content or encrypt the restored working Flow. A protected data-only export is still data-only, even though its encrypted container uses the .fj extension. See Export & import.

title: Move a Flow to another computer
content: Finish saving your work. If saving is blocked or a folder is unavailable, resolve that state before treating a folder copy as current. Export the whole Flow as a full package with media. Explicitly include every Private node you need, and choose the histories, tasks and preferences you want to preserve. Leave API-key transfer off unless you deliberately need it. Enable Protect package with a password for sensitive content. Keep the package password and the included nodes’ separate passwords or existing node recovery keys safe, separately from the backup. A node recovery key cannot unlock the outer package, and FlowJoe cannot recover a lost package password. Copy the completed package and any linked originals to another drive kept separately, or to a backup service you trust. A second file on the same computer is still vulnerable to loss of that computer. Keep an earlier dated copy as well; sync alone can propagate accidental deletion. Open a copy in a separate test installation before relying on it. Check ordinary and Private text, actual media files, saved workbenches and the histories you selected. Verify linked originals after relinking. Export any existing work before replacing it during an import. The Local Recovery Copy, restore points and the Workspace’s retained .flowjoe/ backups help with local mistakes or a folder outage. They are not a complete off-device backup of owner-only data. This guide is a contents inventory and procedure, not evidence that a clean-computer disaster-recovery rehearsal has been completed. Choose a full package when the media needs to travel, and verify linked-file paths on the destination.

title: Move a Flow to another computer
content: If you want your display settings and playlists included, choose Settings → Data → Save Preferences With Exports. Choose File → Export Flow. Export the whole Flow as a .fj package, including its media. Private nodes start excluded: explicitly select each one you need and confirm its password. Choose the histories you want to carry. Keep the API-key option off unless you deliberately want to transfer that key. Choose package password protection if needed. Save the package, then copy it to the other computer or backup drive. A whole-Flow export includes all root branches. Export Node… in a node’s right-click menu is the alternative for taking just that branch. The package gathers media referenced by the chosen work, rather than every unused file in the app’s database.

title: Move a Flow to another computer
header: Open it on the other computer
content: Open FlowJoe and choose File → Import Flow. Select the package and enter its password if it has one. Review whether to replace the current Flow or merge the incoming work. Export the current Flow first if you want a separate backup. Check a few media cards and linked files before relying on the transfer. Linked files may need to be relinked when their original paths do not exist on the new computer. Private-node protection travels with a package; it does not mean a plain package is encrypted. For regular use across computers, consider a Workspace Folder. For export choices, see Export & import.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts
content: Hotkey reference aligned with the in-app Keyboard Shortcuts legend, plus a few extra app-wide keys. This page follows the Keyboard Shortcuts legend in the app (tree toolbar K, status bar Shortcuts). A short Also useful section at the end lists a few extra keys that are real in the product but not every row in that legend. [!IMPORTANT] Open Joe: Cmd+Shift+A / Ctrl+Shift+A toggles the Joe chat panel (open / minimize to a floating pill / restore). Ctrl+J copies node JSON — it does not open Joe. New node: N / Ctrl+N (not Enter or Tab). On Mac, Cmd+N is New Flow, not add node. Open the same legend from the tree’s information button or press K when you are not typing.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts
content: In ordinary confirmation and single-text-entry prompts, Tab and Shift+Tab move through the current controls and wrap within the prompt. Closing returns keyboard focus to the control you came from, unless you have already moved focus to another window. Screen readers can identify the prompt by its displayed title and hear the text field’s instructions. Custom choice prompts follow the same Tab and return-focus behavior; Escape also closes an Info notice.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts
content: Hotkey Action Ctrl+F Tree search Q Query by tags N / Ctrl+N Add node (child of the selected node, or a root if none is selected). Ctrl+P Unlock private nodes ↑ / ↓ Previous / next visible node ← / → Collapse / expand (or previous / next node when already collapsed/expanded as appropriate) Space Toggle node collapse + / - Expand / collapse selected node Shift+= Expand all nodes Shift+- Collapse all nodes / or \ Hide / show tree There is no Enter / Tab / Insert shortcut for creating siblings or children. Creating a node is N (or Ctrl+N).

title: Keyboard Shortcuts

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: The shared writing surface behind Node Summary, Flow Summary, slot Preview notes, and gallery slot notes — slash commands, emoji, the bubble menu, AI actions, and markdown shortcuts. FlowJoe uses one rich-text editor everywhere you write more than a title. It stores what you write as Markdown, so nothing is locked into a proprietary format, and it behaves the same way on every surface that uses it.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Surface How you open it Persistent toolbar Node Summary Top-bar Summary button (or S with a node selected) Yes Flow Summary Top-bar Flow Summary button Yes Slot Preview notes Click a gallery slot to open it full-size Yes Gallery slot & stack notes Click into the note on the card itself No — bubble menu only The three modal surfaces (Node Summary, Flow Summary, Preview) get the full toolbar. Gallery notes on the board are deliberately chrome-free: you get the same slash commands, emoji picker, markdown shortcuts, and floating bubble menu, just without a toolbar taking up room on the card. [!TIP] Every modal surface has a Keyboard Shortcuts & Formatting Guide button in its toolbar. It’s the same list as this page, available without leaving the app.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Type a slash at a word boundary to choose a block. This is the actual editor menu. Type / and a menu of blocks opens. Keep typing to filter, ↑/↓ to move, Enter to insert, Escape to dismiss. / only opens the menu at a word boundary — the start of a line, or right after a space. Typing and/or mid-word does nothing, which is intentional. On the modal surfaces the full list is: Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3 Task List Bullet List Numbered List Blockquote Code Block Table of Contents Insert Table Divider Collapsible Details Insert Image Image Upload Box Embed YouTube Reset Formatting Ask Joe AI Gallery slot notes carry a deliberate subset — Heading 1–3, Task List, Bullet List, Numbered List, Blockquote, and Text (reset formatting). Images, tables, code blocks, and the AI item aren’t on the card-level menu.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Type : followed by a few letters — :smi, :fire, :rocket — and a searchable emoji menu appears. Pick one and it replaces what you typed. : follows the same word-boundary rule as /. It has to be at the start of a line or directly after a space. Typing a colon mid-word (ratio:2, 10:30) will not open the menu — this is the single most common source of “the emoji thing isn’t working”. The picker matches on emoji name and keywords, and shows up to eight results at a time.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Select any text and a small floating toolbar appears next to it. The same set of buttons appears on every surface, including gallery notes on the board: Button What it does B Bold I Italic U Underline S Strikethrough Highlighter Highlight the selection Lists ▸ Bullet list, Numbered list, Checklist Link ▸ Add Link, Remove link </> Inline code ✨ AI actions (Joe) When you select an image in one of the modal surfaces, the bubble menu swaps in image controls instead: align left / center / right, float left or right so text wraps around it, add a caption, add alt text, and reset to original size.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Click ✨ in the bubble menu (or the toolbar’s ✨, or / → Ask Joe AI) to hand the selected text to Joe. 1 Select some text, or just place your cursor in a paragraph 2 Pick an action Improve writing Fix grammar & spelling Simplify Shorten Expand Change tone ▸ — Professional, Casual, Confident, Friendly Translate to ▸ — any of FlowJoe’s supported languages, or Other… to name one yourself Turn into bullet points Summarize Continue writing Ask Joe… — type any instruction you like 3 Watch it stream in Joe’s answer appears in a card below your text, filling in as he writes. Stop cancels a request in progress. 4 Decide what to do with it Once it’s finished, the card shows the result with changes highlighted, plus an editable box — you can tweak Joe’s answer before you use it. Then choose: Replace — swap your selection for the result Insert below — keep both Copy — put it on the clipboard Retry — ask again Discard — throw it away For Summarize, Continue writing, and Ask Joe…, Insert below is offered first, since those usually add to your text rather than rewrite it. Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes an accepted change. AI actions use your selected Joe connection: an API key or a supported signed-in command-line brain. Shared guests use the owner’s enabled connection. See Bring Your Own Brain.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: These convert as soon as you type the trigger: Block triggers, typed at the start of a line: # , ## , ### for headings 1–3; - or * for a bullet list; 1. for a numbered list; [ ] for a checklist item; > for a blockquote; ``` then Enter for a code block; --- then Enter for a horizontal divider.Inline triggers, anywhere: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `code`, and ==highlight==. ==text== is FlowJoe’s own addition — it round-trips both ways, so a highlight you apply with the toolbar button saves back out as ==text== in the underlying Markdown.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Modal surfaces (Node Summary, Flow Summary, Preview) carry a persistent toolbar. Left to right, it holds: Heading Sizes ▸ — Normal Text, Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 3 Bold, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough Text & Highlight Color ▸ — a twelve-swatch palette (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, crimson, white, gray, dark gray, black) applied as either text colour or highlight colour More Formatting ▸ — Inline Code, Subscript, Superscript, Clear Text Formatting, Reset All Formatting Hyperlink Text Alignment ▸ — Left, Center, Right, Justify Checklist / Tasks Bullet List Numbered List Formats ▸ — decimal, lowercase/uppercase alpha, lowercase/uppercase roman Table Tools ▸ — insert a 3×3 table, add/delete rows and columns, delete the table Insert Blocks ▸ — Blockquote, Code Block, Horizontal Rule, Collapsible Details, Insert Image, Embed YouTube Video, Table of Contents AI actions (✨) Find and Replace Undo / Redo Save, Print, and the Keyboard Shortcuts & Formatting Guide Dictation and spell-check also live on this toolbar — see Node Summaries.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Hotkey Action Cmd/Ctrl+B Bold Cmd/Ctrl+I Italic Cmd/Ctrl+U Underline Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+X Strikethrough Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H Highlight Cmd/Ctrl+K Add / edit hyperlink Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+1 / 2 / 3 Heading levels Tab / Shift+Tab Indent / outdent a list item Cmd/Ctrl+Z Undo Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z Redo Cmd/Ctrl+F Find and replace (Summary and Preview only, not gallery notes) Escape Finish editing a gallery note (closes an open / or : menu first) Cmd/Ctrl+Enter Finish editing a gallery note; Save on the Summary surfaces Undo and redo run on FlowJoe’s own 50-level, persistent history — the same one the rest of the app uses — so your edits are still there to step back through after a reload. There are no text-alignment keyboard shortcuts. Cmd+Shift+R collided with the browser’s hard-reload, so the whole Cmd+Shift+L/E/R/J set was removed rather than leaving an inconsistent three. Use the toolbar’s Text Alignment dropdown instead.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Select some text, open the bubble menu’s Link ▸ dropdown, and choose Add Link — or press Cmd/Ctrl+K. Remove link in the same dropdown takes it off again. A link in a note at rest (not being edited) is clickable. On the desktop app it opens in the in-app browser panel in a new tab, so following a reference doesn’t pull you out of FlowJoe.

title: Rich-Text Editor
content: Three ways to highlight, all producing the same result: the highlighter button in the bubble menu, typing ==your text==, or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H. For coloured highlights, use the toolbar’s Text & Highlight Color dropdown on a modal surface — it offers twelve swatches applied as highlight colour. Multicolour highlights are stored with the colour attached, so they survive a save and reload.
