title: Settings Map
content: A comprehensive breakdown of all application settings in FlowJoe. Open Settings from the sidebar (gear) or the app rail. Sections appear as tabs on the left of the Settings panel. Cards inside each tab can be reordered with the grip handle (⋮⋮). The section buttons keep their names for screen readers when the menu is collapsed, and the selected section is identified. Settings announces its current title. Tab and Shift+Tab stay within its current controls. Close or an unhandled Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to the control that opened it, unless you have moved focus elsewhere. Menus and key windows handle their own Escape first. Closing Settings removes its controls from keyboard navigation. API-key windows announce their title, keep Tab within their current controls, and return keyboard focus to the button that opened them when closed. Use the bottom Status Bar (Footer) to check save state or change Joe’s brain, theme, language, and scheduled tasks. It offers common controls without opening Settings. These captures use Compact density and Modern Ember. Appearance settings apply to your view of the app. Tab order matches the app (top to bottom): Appearance Tree Gallery Audio Browser (desktop / Electron only) Joe AI APIs Data Tasks

title: Settings Map
header: Settings when you join someone else’s Flow
content: Your personal display preferences belong to your browser: appearance, density, surface style, language, layout, Tree, Gallery and Audio. Data’s personal save/import prompt policies, reload warnings, save reminders, export preference choices, onboarding replay, Reset Layouts, startup profiler, Delete Undo (5s) and Open-source licenses also work in a guest session. Changing an import preference does not grant permission to import or replace the owner’s Flow. Your choices do not change the owner’s preferences. The owner’s Joe voice and auto-read settings remain the shared runtime settings. You can preview that voice through the owner’s OpenAI connection while Joe execution is available; you do not need your own API key. Shared-node themes require Can edit. Workspace storage, restore-point management, invitations, credentials and native computer settings belong to the owner. See Sharing, Guests and Presenting for the permission and removal rules.

title: Settings Map
content: Language: First card on Appearance (also available from the Language control on the status bar). FlowJoe ships full-app localization for 20 languages: Arabic, Bengali, German, English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Thai, Turkish, Urdu, Vietnamese, Chinese (Simplified), and Chinese (Traditional). Changing language rewrites UI chrome (Settings, toolbars, menus, modals, tooltips, toasts, and related surfaces). A fresh install starts in English until you pick another language. This is interface language only — it does not translate your flow content, notes, or files.

title: Settings Map
content: Density: Comfy / Compact (default) / Dense — spacing and control sizes app-wide. Surface Style: Outlined or Filled (default) — chrome button borders vs fills.

title: Settings Map
content: Modern Ember Modern Paper Sage Storyboard Modern Ember · Compact density. Modern Paper · the same content and Compact density. Sage Storyboard · the same content and Compact density. Theme: Full global theme catalog in Appearance (Dark / Light / Sepia / Cozy and the rest of the theme list). Reset editable nodes to the global theme when needed; frozen and password-locked branches keep their overrides, including during a factory-preferences reset. Per-node overrides are available from the node Theme Manager and the status-bar Theme control. Mac development launches through npm run dev also show FlowJoe in the top macOS application menu. Restart the app after updating; a direct electron . launch still uses Electron’s name. On Mac, the window title bar follows the currently displayed theme, including per-node themes. The window buttons, coffee mug, FlowJoe name and header controls share one compact row. Drag empty header space to move the window. Full screen gives the window-button space back to the header. Font style, justification, line height for notes and readable surfaces. Informative descriptions use stronger secondary text, and the active Settings section keeps its selection marker with a primary text label. Visual effects: optional surface / glass / visual-effect toggles, nav tooltips, toast notifications and toast theme-match. Routine notifications are exposed as polite status updates for screen readers; error notifications are exposed as alerts without moving keyboard focus. Status Bar: show or hide the bottom status bar (default on). See Status Bar (Footer).

title: Settings Map
content: Auto-resize tree width, resizer width. Branch toggle style (flat / themed). Status indicators, slot counts, child counts on tree rows. Open summary on new node preference.

title: Settings Map
content: Image Editor (desktop app, Flow owner only): says the editor is built in and shows its version; nothing to download or remove. See Edit Image. Scrubber show/hide, position (top/bottom), style, FX and shadow. Embed performance / virtualization for heavy embeds. Slot action controls (animated vs expanded). Slot scrubber, title position, stack-count badges, media labels, metadata, scheduler chip, tags, and notes chrome toggles. Custom placeholder image for empty/missing thumbs. In Local storage it stays on this computer; with a Workspace folder it is saved with the Flow and travels with the folder. Image compression on import (Always / Never / Ask) where configured.

title: Settings Map
content: UI sounds: enable, volume, hover sounds, test button. Header audio player: show/hide, play mode (sequential / shuffle / repeat), target node, tag filters for playlists. Continue playback when advancing stacks (where offered).

title: Settings Map
content: Startup behavior when the browser opens (restore tabs, home, blank, gallery, etc.). Homepage URL, default search engine. Tab, bookmarks, history, downloads, and clear-browsing-data controls.

title: Settings Map
content: Agent Bridge (MCP): enable local tool connections, choose read-only or proposal access, connect detected assistants, copy setup details, allow automatic edits for the session, and rotate the access token. Auto-compact chat, attachment-memory preferences, Context Director on/off. Link previews for cards Joe adds: Load automatically (default) or Wait for a click. Governs link cards added by Joe, a scheduled task, or a connected agent — your own link cards always load their preview immediately. See Proposals & Approval. Related AI behavior controls that live on this tab (voice and chat helpers may also appear here depending on build). Per-send map size is controlled on the Joe chat panel, not here: Limit map to my location (on by default) and Omit entire flow map. See Token usage with Joe.

title: Settings Map
content: Your AI accounts: OpenAI API Key, Anthropic API Key (Claude by key), Gemini API Key and xAI API Key (Grok by key). Extra services: TypeSafe API Key for optional faster context selection and checks. A line under each name shows Key saved with the start and end of the key, No key yet, or Key rejected at last check. Each key window has Test, a Show key eye and a Remove key trash icon that asks before removing. Desktop keys use OS-backed encryption when available. See Bring Your Own Brain.

title: Settings Map
content: Workspace folder connect / create copy / switch back to local storage. Delete-undo retention. Anti-nag prompts for save and import (always ask / dirty only / never, etc.). Restore Points: automatic saving on/off, how often to save one, how many timed / before-a-restore / manually-saved points to keep, a running total of how many points that keeps (not a disk-space estimate), and a Delete all restore points button. Open-source licenses: a list of the open-source software FlowJoe is built with. Filter by name or by license type (MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL/LGPL, Other), open any component to read its version, license and full license text, and follow the link to the source download page. Long license badges shorten in the list so the component name and arrow remain visible; open the component to read the complete license. Texts are shown as published and are not translated. Disk usage, cleanup, reset, and backup-related tools on this tab.

title: Settings Map
content: Enable scheduled background runs. List of scheduled tasks (pause, resume, run now, delete). Review inbox for propose-only automation results. Recent run history. In a shared browser session, View guests can inspect the shared lists and task records. Edit guests can manage shared tasks and proposals within their access; deletion follows creator/elevated-deletion permission. Joe-off disables running and approving, while the lists remain readable. The global background-runs switch belongs to the owner. A run’s restore control asks the owner to undo it.

title: Settings Map
content: Cards can be dragged to reorder within a tab; that does not change the left-hand tab list. Some browser settings only appear in the desktop (Electron) app. Settings icon actions expose their localized purposes to assistive technology. In Data, prefix-removal buttons keep their names when rows are rebuilt, license search has a localized name, and each license entry remains a named button within the component list.

title: Status Bar (Footer)
content: What the bottom status bar shows and what you can change without opening Settings. The status bar is the thin strip pinned to the bottom of the FlowJoe window. It is always available while visible, so you can monitor the flow and change a few common choices without digging through Settings. Show or hide it under Settings → Appearance → Status Bar (on by default). Layout (left cluster, then right cluster): Left: Stats · Save · Joe brain (plus short-lived notices such as “Outside change waiting” and “Also open on a computer” when they apply) Right: Scheduled tasks · Theme · Language · Shortcuts · Version The status bar provides compact monitoring and shortcuts. A changed-export reminder is separate from whether your working data saved.

title: Status Bar (Footer)
content: Segment What it shows Stats Total nodes in the flow and total gallery slots (across the whole tree, not only the selected node). Read-only. Save Save health: clean / unsaved changes (with pending count when available) / still loading storage / blocked when the workspace cannot save. Joe brain Active Joe model or CLI brain name (and brand mark). Tasks Always visible. Shows the count of scheduled tasks, or No tasks when empty (the segment stays on the bar either way). Theme The effective theme for the selected node (node override when set; otherwise the global Appearance theme). With no node selected, shows the global theme. Language Current interface language. Shortcuts Keyboard shortcuts entry point. Version The FlowJoe version you are running, such as “FlowJoe 0.9.65-alpha”. Also visible in browser and guest sessions. A browser shows the version of the app deployed to that site. Read-only. Outside change waiting · saving paused Appears only when something changed your Workspace folder from outside FlowJoe and you have not decided what to do yet. While it shows, saving to the folder is paused (your edits are kept on this computer). Click it to reopen the decision window. Also open on <computer> Appears only while another computer has been working in the same Workspace in the last few minutes. Click it for an explanation. It goes away by itself.

title: Status Bar (Footer)
content: Click What happens Joe brain Opens an in-bar menu of available brains — OpenAI models (GPT-6 Luna, Sol, Astra; GPT-5.6 Luna, Terra, Sol) and, on desktop, CLI brains (Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku, Grok, Antigravity) when the matching CLI is installed and signed in. Unavailable options are dimmed with a short reason (e.g. no API key, not signed in). Choosing one updates the same preference the Joe chat window uses. Save Saves / exports the flow when changes are pending (same family of action as Ctrl/Cmd+S / Export flow). Tasks (clock) Opens Settings → Tasks so you can manage scheduled runs. Theme Opens an in-bar theme picker for the selected node (same theme list as the node Theme Manager). You can pick a node theme or restore the global theme for that node. With no node selected, the control reflects / sets the global Appearance theme. Language Opens an in-bar language picker (same 20 UI languages as Settings → Appearance → Language). Changes interface language only — not your notes or files. Shortcuts Opens the keyboard shortcuts legend (K does the same).

title: Status Bar (Footer)
content: The status bar is for fast checks and frequent switches (brain, node theme, language, dirty state). Full detail for each area still lives in the matching Settings tab or node tools. On desktop, opening a footer popover ducks the native browser view so the menu stays visible. If the bar is missing, turn Status Bar back on under Settings → Appearance. See also: Settings Map, Keyboard Shortcuts, Bring Your Own Brain.

title: Glossary
content: Key terminology and concepts used throughout FlowJoe. Use this list to familiarize yourself with the vocabulary of FlowJoe.

title: Glossary
content: The primary document workspace in FlowJoe. A Flow contains a tree structure, node metadata, summaries, tag lists, and references. It corresponds to a single project file.

title: Glossary
content: A single unit in a Flow’s hierarchical tree outline. Nodes are living containers that contain notes, themes, summaries, and media galleries.

title: Glossary
content: A single card or cell inside a gallery. Slots hold image previews, audio players, web links, or editable spreadsheet widgets.

title: Glossary
content: A collection of multiple media files layered inside a single gallery slot. Stacks allow you to organize file revisions or design variations without cluttering the screen.

title: Glossary
content: The metadata layer (notes, summaries, tags, and context summaries) that captures the intent of your project outline.

title: Glossary
content: FlowJoe’s AI assistant. Joe communicates via the Chat panel and suggests tree changes through proposal cards.

title: Glossary
content: The name-and-id outline of the tree that Joe is given on a send — nodes, slots, and stack items, plus the Flow Summary, the Theme-menu looks he can set, a node’s own look, and a slot’s canvas color or lines when it has them. Not file contents. Controlled by Limit map to my location and Omit entire flow map. See Token usage with Joe.

title: Glossary
content: The segmented meter at the bottom of the Joe panel showing how this send would use the model’s context window. Flow map, Location, and Slot data are separate slices.

title: Glossary
content: A chat card that displays proposed tree or gallery changes from Joe. Changes are only applied when you click Approve.

title: Glossary
content: A read-only gallery view compiled dynamically from tag queries or search results across all nodes.

title: Honest Limitations
content: A transparent list of boundaries and unsupported behaviors in FlowJoe. We believe in stating product limits clearly. Here are the boundaries and intentional limitations of FlowJoe.

title: Honest Limitations
content: FlowJoe’s structure is a tree: every node has exactly one parent. You cannot draw connections between nodes in the tree, or give a node two parents. The tree is a hierarchy, not a graph. Slots inside a node’s gallery are a different matter: the Canvas layout lets you place them freely on an infinite 2D board and draw relationship lines between them. Those connections live within that one gallery and cannot cross into another node. See Canvas Connections.

title: Honest Limitations
content: FlowJoe renders document previews locally: Previews for DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX display inline text and formatting. Previews for legacy formats (.doc, .xls, .ppt) require LibreOffice to be installed on your machine and configured in your path setting; otherwise, the app can only display raw text extractions.

title: Honest Limitations
content: The mobile version of FlowJoe is currently in design and layout development, focusing on high-density outlines and quick media inputs: A current narrow-browser capture of the Lantern Vale example. This illustrates the layout limitation; it does not demonstrate a native mobile app.

title: Honest Limitations
content: Virtual galleries compile dynamic search results: To prevent accidental structural corruption, virtual galleries are read-mostly. You can edit slot notes and view files, but you cannot drag cards, merge stacks, or delete files directly in a Virtual Gallery. You must click the jump-back badge to edit the file at its original node.

title: Honest Limitations
content: Free local Whisper transcription is a desktop feature. There is no recording length or file-size limit. Recordings are converted in a separate, locked-down background step first, which for a very long recording needs free memory; running out shows a message and never closes the app. Local runs need a compatible installed/downloaded model. Local output supports plain text or segment timestamps; speaker labels are currently an online option. Download size is separate from working memory, and speed depends on your computer. See Transcribe audio.

title: Security & privacy
content: Understand where your work stays and what you choose to share. FlowJoe gives you control over where your work lives, what Joe can read, and what you share. Local-first work: keep your tree, notes and imported media on your computer, with a Workspace Folder you can back up yourself. Controlled sharing: choose what guests can access through your computer; Private nodes stay out of browser sharing. Encrypted Private nodes: a Private node’s contents are saved encrypted on your computer and open only with its password. AI access controls: choose Joe’s provider and permissions, and use Private or Hidden-from-Joe protection for sensitive content as described below. Encrypted portable backups: protect an exported package with its own password, including the Private content you explicitly choose to include. Each control has a specific purpose. The details below explain what it protects and what to check when sharing or moving work. Node locks, AI access, guest access and export encryption are separate controls; review the details below.

title: Security & privacy
content: Normal desktop work stays in app storage, or in a Workspace Folder you choose. A Workspace Folder keeps the Flow and its shared media in files you can back up or sync with your own tools. You choose which content guests can access, and sharing sends that permitted content through the owner’s computer. Remote sharing can use a Cloudflare tunnel, with encryption between each computer and Cloudflare. Cloudflare decrypts traffic before forwarding it, so this is not end-to-end encryption between owner and guest. AI features send the context they need to your selected provider; that provider’s account and data policies apply. Web browsing and link previews contact the websites you use. See Workspace folders, Sharing, and Token usage.

title: Security & privacy
content: What you save Protection in the current release A package exported with Protect package with a password The complete selected package is encrypted, including admitted Private content and included media/history. Private content saved on this computer Encrypted. The node’s contents, pictures and other media, autosaves, older versions, recovery copies, and the chats, transcripts and picture history saved with it open only with its password. An ordinary .fj or JSON export The rest of the Flow is readable outside FlowJoe. A Private node you include stays encrypted inside the file and opens with its own password. A repository you commit or push Committed content is readable by anyone who has the repository’s files. Private folders inside a repository always stay out of its commits; to include one, remove its protection first. A repository itself is never Private. See Repositories. Supported API keys saved by the desktop app OS-backed encryption when secure storage is available; a session-only choice when it is unavailable. API keys in a standalone browser Session-only by default. Saving a key on this computer requires explicit consent to plain-text storage. Private-node encryption is on. Older Private nodes made with the previous password protection can’t be opened or changed while it is on; FlowJoe says so (“This Private node uses an older protection this version can’t open.”) instead of reporting a wrong password. Keep using your computer’s disk protection for everything else you keep on it.

title: Security & privacy
content: On desktop, supported keys are encrypted using the operating system’s secure-storage service when available and saved in FlowJoe’s app data. If that service fails or provides only weak protection, you can enter a key for this session only while the existing saved key stays intact. You can also try opening secure storage again. FlowJoe never silently saves a desktop key as plain text. In a standalone browser, new keys default to For this session only. They disappear on refresh or close. To keep one, you must explicitly choose Save on this computer as plain text; anyone or anything with access to the browser’s storage could read it. If a plaintext key already exists, Cancel keeps it, and you can choose to keep the saved copy or remove it and use the key for this session. Desktop temporary keys last until you quit FlowJoe. After restarting, enter the key again before tasks using it can run; any previously saved encrypted key remains available instead. Remove is an explicit deletion. Including a key in an export still requires the separate opt-in. Keys appear masked in Settings. Use the eye button to reveal or copy them. Keys are excluded from portable exports by default; the export dialog lets you explicitly include an OpenAI key. Review that option before sharing a package.

title: Security & privacy
content: Private nodes are protected by a password and saved encrypted. While a Private node is locked its contents are unavailable; once you unlock it, it works like any other node. Their contents are excluded from the shared Workspace Folder and browser guests. You can explicitly include individual Private nodes in a portable export; an already-unlocked node does not need its password again. Private folders inside a repository always stay out of it (see below). After unlocking a node, you can discuss it with Joe or attach its contents through the normal controls. Private does not automatically turn on Hidden from Joe or Frozen; those remain separate choices, just as on an ordinary node. Use Hidden from Joe separately to withhold content from Joe. A Private folder inside a Git repository always stays out of every commit and push, and a Private node, or anything inside one, can’t be made a repository with Make This a Repository…. Git keeps everything as ordinary, readable files, so FlowJoe never puts a Private folder there. For the same reason a repository is never Private: Make Node Private is dimmed on a repository and on a node that holds one, Create as a repository is dimmed inside a Private node and while Password-protect this node is ticked, and a repository can’t be moved into a Private node. Importing a file that would put a repository inside a Private node stops and offers Import at Root Level or Cancel; a copy of a repository is always ordinary folders. To protect a folder that holds a repository, move the repository out first. To put something Private in a repository, remove its protection first; it then goes in like any ordinary node. See Repositories. FlowJoe runs Git with its own fixed settings, so a repository can’t make your computer run a program. Settings that would run one, such as a filter, a merge or diff tool, a signature checker or a credential helper, are switched off; when a repository’s own settings name such a program anyway, FlowJoe refuses that

title: Security & privacy
content: that step instead. Large files stored with Git LFS are downloaded and sent by FlowJoe itself, never by a program the repository names. Your GitHub sign-in goes only to the repository’s own host when FlowJoe asks where a large file is or where to send it, never to the server the file then comes from or goes to. A push sends large files only after the Private-folder check has passed, and never a file from a Private folder you kept out. FlowJoe checks the current Private folders again after the first-push review. Each push sends the exact commits it checked; a commit or tag changed during the push waits for the next one. See Repositories. Your Joe chats, picture history, transcripts, undo notes history and Memories go into a repository only when you choose them for that repository; each choice is off to begin with. Chosen history goes to anyone who can read the repository, and Git keeps it even if you later turn the choice off. A conversation or transcript you keep on this computer, and the history of a Private folder, never go in. See History in the repository. Hidden from Joe seals a node’s contents from Joe while leaving them available to you. Sealed node names and positions can still appear in Joe’s outline, so keep secrets out of names. A media read still waiting for its result checks these protections again before returning it. Hidden from Joe is a preference for your own Joe: a guest’s Joe can still read content that guest is allowed to see. Neither setting recalls information already sent in an earlier message. For a portable copy of Private work, explicitly select each Private node and unlock it or confirm its password. An included Private node stays encrypted inside the exported file and opens with its own password after import. The rest of the exported file is readable outside FlowJoe unless you also enable Protect package with a password, which encrypts the whole file.

title: Security & privacy
content: Everything inside a Private node uses that node’s password. You can’t give a node inside a Private node a password of its own. In Add Child, Password-protect this node is dimmed with the note “Already protected: this node is inside the Private node “…” and uses its password.” In the node menu’s Set Visibility / Privacy…, Make Node Private is replaced by a dimmed “Already protected by “…”” naming the Private node whose password covers it. Moving or copying into another Private node: protected content you move or copy into a different Private node asks for the password of the Private node it comes from, even when it is unlocked (“Move into “…”?” / “Copy into “…”?”). Afterwards FlowJoe tells you which password now opens it: “Now protected by “…”‘s password.” Ordinary content dropped into a Private node needs no password; it just shows that message. Moving or copying out: taking content out of a Private node into an ordinary place asks first: Move outside Private protection? (“This node and its contents will no longer be encrypted when saved here.”) or Copy outside Private protection? (“The copy will not be encrypted when saved here.”), together with the Private node’s password. Cancel changes nothing. When you copy out, the original stays protected. Locked content can’t be moved; unlock it first. Joe follows the same rules. Joe can’t type passwords, so a change from Joe that moves or copies protected content waits for you to enter the password in the same window. Duplicate: a duplicate of a Private node opens with the same password. FlowJoe asks for it first (“Same password for the copy”). The copy has no recovery key of its own; the original’s recovery key doesn’t open it. Import and export: an imported Private node arrives locked and opens with its own password. Importing into an unlocked Private node asks for the imported node’s password, then it joins that node’s protection. Importing a Private node back into the Flow it came from brings it in as a separate copy

title: Security & privacy
content: copy that opens with the same password (“Import as a copy”). Exporting a node from inside a Private node writes it as a Private node of its own that opens with the same password. Scheduled tasks: for a Private node, Joe’s scheduled-task history keeps no readable proposed changes or previews. When you make a node Private, the previews already stored for it are removed, and the run entries stay. A waiting review for a Private node shows its preview until you restart FlowJoe or lock the node; after that you can only reject or delete it. Repositories: when a picture, link or event file leaves a Private node in a repository (moved to another node or deleted), FlowJoe removes its readable copy from its own Git storage after the next save. For a delete, this happens once its Undo is no longer available. Browsing from a Private node: a link you open from a Private node (its URL slot, its preview window, or a link in its notes) opens in a browser tab that stays out of the browser’s History, isn’t saved with your open tabs, and isn’t added to Reopen Closed Tab. The tab is titled by the web address, not by the slot’s or link’s name, and it closes when the node locks. The browser’s ordinary web cache and your site logins still work as in any browser, so the websites you visit, and the browser’s own cache files on this computer, can still show which pages were opened. Existing virtual slots can remain together inside one unlocked Private area for your own use. Joe follows the same unlocked-owner and Hidden from Joe rules; browser guests cannot read the Private master. Making separate branches Private treats each branch as a separate area and converts pointers between them to real copies. Moves that would separate a retained pair across a Private boundary are refused without moving any of the selection. See Virtual slots.

title: Security & privacy
content: Joe normally proposes Flow changes for you to approve, reject, or revise. Scheduled tasks and connected agents can apply changes under permissions you authorize. See Proposals & approval and Automations before enabling automatic work.

title: Security & privacy
content: Select Protect package with a password when exporting to encrypt the entire exported file, including any Private nodes, media and history you explicitly chose to include. Private nodes start excluded. You can include an already-unlocked node without entering its password again; a locked node still requires its node password. Including a node does not turn on package encryption. The recipient needs the package password to import the file. Included Private nodes keep their separate node passwords and remain locked after import. Unlocking the package does not unlock those nodes. Package encryption protects that whole exported copy. Import restores its contents into FlowJoe’s normal storage, where Private nodes stay encrypted and ordinary nodes are saved as usual. Keep using your computer’s disk protection. The outer file name and file size remain visible. To preserve Private work off-device, explicitly include each Private node and its needed history in a full, password-protected package, and keep its package password and separate node passwords safe. A Workspace folder copy alone leaves that owner-only content on the original computer and cannot recover it if the computer is lost. See Backup contents and exclusions. Full packages saved through a file-saving window use streaming encryption, including packages above 2 GiB. Use a current FlowJoe version to open them. Data-only exports, browser download fallbacks and earlier backups retain their memory limits. Keep the package password safe: FlowJoe cannot recover a package if you lose it. See Password-protected packages for the export and import steps.

title: Security & privacy
header: GitHub access when sharing a Flow
content: The owner can ask Joe to list and clone all repositories accessible to the owner’s signed-in GitHub account, including private GitHub repositories. A guest can list or clone that account’s public repositories, plus repositories already visible in their shared Flow even if private on GitHub. Other private GitHub repositories are withheld. A View guest can read the permitted list; creating or cloning a repository node requires Edit access to its destination. The owner’s computer rechecks this access before the clone is attached. Joe uses named FlowJoe repository actions. Downloads, commits, pushes, merges and branch changes require an approval slot on every brain, including external assistants with ordinary edit autoapproval. GitHub credentials remain on the owner’s computer and are never sent to Joe or guests. A repository marked private on GitHub is different from a password-protected Private node in a Flow: the Flow’s normal Private and sharing rules still apply.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: Sign in at account.flowjoe.app with an email code, see your account, manage signed-in computers and browsers, and change your email. Your FlowJoe account lives at account.flowjoe.app. Your Flows never leave your computer because of it: the account holds only your sign-in, profile, trial and signed-in devices.

title: Your FlowJoe account
header: Signing in or creating an account
content: Signing in and creating an account both use a code sent to your email. Open account.flowjoe.app. To sign in, enter your email and choose Sign in. New to FlowJoe? Choose Create account under the button, enter your email and choose Create account. Open the newest FlowJoe email and type its six-digit code on the sign-in page. There is no password to remember: every sign-in uses a fresh code sent to your inbox. Creating an account and signing in both send you a code; if you choose Create account with an email that already has an account, the code simply signs you in. Keep codes private — never send a code to another person or enter it on a page someone sent you.

title: Your FlowJoe account
header: If the code does not work
content: Check that you typed all six digits from the newest email. Requesting a new code makes older ones useless. Sending can be briefly limited if you ask for many codes in a row; wait a minute and try again. If the sign-in request has ended, choose Start again to begin a fresh one.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: After signing in you see your account overview: the email you are signed in with, your current access and sharing address, and how many computers are signed in. If your account has a plan, Current access shows it — for example Pro with Sharing on and its end date (or “No end date”). If your account owns a sharing address, Your sharing address shows it — for example yourname.flowjoe.app — marked Active. Details that are not available yet appear as a dash. Use the menu on the left to move between Overview, Devices and Security; they switch instantly without reloading the page. Plan & Passes and Team are marked Soon and are not available yet.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: Devices lists the computers signed in to your account. The list stays current on its own while the page is open, so a computer signed in elsewhere appears without reloading. Sign out next to a computer ends that computer’s account access. Its Flows stay on that computer. Sign out all computers ends account access on every computer and keeps this browser signed in. If your last email code is more than ten minutes old, FlowJoe first asks for a fresh code. The code alone does not remove anything — you confirm again afterwards.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: Security shows the email you sign in with, links to support and to how your account data is handled. Change email: enter your new address, then confirm the code sent to your current inbox and the different code sent to your new inbox. The change happens only after both confirmations. Use the new address next time you sign in. Sign out everywhere: after a confirmation, ends FlowJoe account access on every computer and every browser, including this one. Your Flows stay on your computers. If the sign-in service cannot confirm its part, the result says so — FlowJoe account access is still ended.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: Sign out (top right of your account page) ends only the current browser session. Your other browsers and computers stay signed in. To use a different account, sign out and sign in again with the other email.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: On Security, choose Delete account…, type the email you sign in with, and confirm. If your last email code is more than ten minutes old, FlowJoe first asks for a fresh code, then brings you back to the confirmation — the code alone never deletes anything. Deleting your account: signs out every computer and browser and ends sharing from this account; removes your profile, sign-ins, computers, plan and trial history; frees your sharing address immediately, so anyone can choose it; keeps only a minimal, unlinked record that your email and computer already used a trial, so a new account doesn’t get a second one. The Flows on your computers are not affected. If you have paid time left, contact support before deleting. Deletion can’t be undone; you can create a new account later with the same email.

title: Your FlowJoe account
header: Signing in from the FlowJoe app
content: In the FlowJoe app, click your avatar (top right) and choose Sign in (or Create account if you don’t have one yet — it opens the same page, titled Create your FlowJoe account), or open Settings › Account and choose Sign in with your browser. FlowJoe opens a short sign-in page in your web browser. If that browser isn’t already signed in, enter your email and the 6-digit code. Check that the code shown matches the one in the app, then approve. You’re returned to the app, signed in. The first code creates your account, just like on the website. The app stays signed in until you sign out or remove that computer under Devices. On a computer without secure storage, FlowJoe shows Signed in until FlowJoe closes and you sign in again after closing it. If FlowJoe can no longer read its saved sign-in — for example after you reset your system keychain or moved your FlowJoe data to another computer — it shows you as signed out; just sign in again (you can remove the old computer under Devices). Manage account in the avatar menu opens this website.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: If your email and computer haven’t used a trial yet, Settings › Account offers Try Pro free for 7 days. Choose your sharing name and confirm. No card is needed, and the trial ends without a charge.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: With sharing access (Pro, a trial, a Project Pass or Team), the avatar menu shows your plan and Sharing as yourname.flowjoe.app, and FlowJoe sets up your sharing address on that computer automatically — there is nothing to configure. Press Share and turn sharing on to let guests in. When your address is set up on this computer, the Share window starts with Sharing access: your plan, your address, this computer and how many guests can edit. Signing out stops any share that is running.

title: Your FlowJoe account
content: Changing your display name or language. Plan & Passes (plans and billing) and Team — shown as Soon in the menu. Choosing or changing your sharing address from the website. These will be documented here when they become available.

title: Account data and privacy
content: What your FlowJoe account stores, where it is kept, and what never leaves your computer. This page explains how the FlowJoe account at account.flowjoe.app handles your information. It covers the account only — not the FlowJoe app on your computer, which keeps your Flows locally.

title: Account data and privacy
header: What never leaves your computer because of your account
content: Your Flows, their notes, pictures, media, documents and Joe conversations are not stored in your account. Signing in, signing out or removing a computer never uploads, copies or deletes them.

title: Account data and privacy
content: Information Why Your email address To send you sign-in codes and identify your account. Display name and preferred language, if set Used to personalize your account and emails. Signed-in browser sessions Kept encrypted on the server so you stay signed in; a browser session ends after eight hours or when you sign out. Signed-in computers So you can see and sign out the computers using your account. Trial records Each email can use the free trial once, and a computer can start another account’s trial only after a year. These are kept as one-way fingerprints of the email and computer, not readable copies. Your sharing address, if you choose one So people can reach the Flows you share. Sign-in codes are sent by email and expire; we do not keep them. Browser cookies used by the account site are limited to keeping you signed in and protecting your requests — there are no advertising or tracking cookies.

title: Account data and privacy
content: Supabase runs the account database and sign-in service. Cloudflare hosts the account website and sends the sign-in emails. Database access for the account service uses a restricted login that can only perform account operations; it cannot read other data.

title: Account data and privacy
content: Change your email from Security. Sign out any computer, all computers, or everywhere at once. You can delete your account on the Security page. Deletion removes your sign-in identity, profile, signed-in computers and browsers, plan, trial history and sharing address (the address is released immediately). FlowJoe keeps only two minimal records with no link to you: a keyed fingerprint showing that your email address already used a trial, and one showing that your computer did, so the one-trial rules still apply. The Flows on your computers are never touched. This page describes how the account works today. A formal privacy policy will replace it before general availability.
